## Notes for All Sessions

- Read `FRUS-Explorer-Specification.md` before beginning any session
- All code must compile under Swift 6 strict concurrency checking
- All user-facing strings must use `String(localized:)`
- All new types and functions require documentation comments
- `#if DEBUG` telemetry logging required for all significant operations
- Update `FRUS-API.openapi.yaml` if the session touches GitHub API or local volume data
- Run all existing tests before committing session output
- Each session produces its own unit tests

## Implementation Notes for All Sessions

### `lastModified` must be updated explicitly at the call site
`@Model` transforms stored properties into computed properties backed by persistent storage. `didSet`/`willSet` observers are syntactically accepted but do not fire reliably in practice. Any code that writes to a SwiftData model must set `instance.lastModified = .now` explicitly at the mutation site — never rely on an observer to do it automatically. This applies to every model type that carries `lastModified` (Session 04 models and any new models added in later sessions).

## Session 2026-10-01 — After Rebuild Index the app knows what is indexed, Volumes & Storage states no measurement it has not taken, Free Up Space's rows hold still while it removes, and the Mac's research-database export writes a whole copy (lane STOR; #1526, #1476, #1432, #1538)

**The question.** Lane STOR of the 2026-09-28 plan of record: four issues and two fold-ins, all about what Settings ▸ Volumes & Storage (and the Mac's Data & Recovery export) states and does.

**What was measured.**
- **#1526.** `IndexingPipeline.indexAllVolumes()` reports no volume as it finishes it: its one `.complete` carries the empty volume id, at the end of the pass, and `rebuildSearchIndexFromCache()` ends the same way. `AppState.connectIndexingProgress` stored that id, and both hubs' Rebuild Index emptied the set first, so after a rebuild the set was `[""]` until relaunch; a boot re-index left it one too high. A real two-volume pipeline reproduces both: on the unfixed routing the set read `[""]` after Rebuild Index and gained `""` after a whole pass.
- **#1538, by a probe on this Mac.** The copy `sqlite3_backup` makes of the live WAL-mode index is in WAL mode too, and its writes after the page copy live in `-wal`/`-shm` beside it. Opened alone, read-only, such a file fails ("unable to open database file"); switched to `journal_mode=DELETE` it opens and holds every write. So the in-place export also left two sidecars at the destination, each another file a sandbox refuses. The first fixed build caught this: staged and moved without the switch, 8 exporter tests failed with 29 issues — six that predate the lane and two of its own new ones (*No connection opens in the destination's folder…* and *A second export to the same file replaces the first*) — because the moved file had no sidecars.
- **The fold-ins.** The side-loaded Remove message is a `Text(String)` whose `**…**` printed as asterisks (iPhone and iPad, measured in the UI suite). No boot path called `ManifestStore.refreshLocalEntries`, so the UI suite's seeded rows read `uitest-storage-04` instead of "UI Test Storage Row 04" at launch on both idioms.

**What changed.**
- **#1526.** `AppState.indexAllVolumes(with:)` runs the pass and then re-reads the set from the index (`reseedIndexedVolumeIds`); it is the app's only caller of `indexAllVolumes()`, used by boot's date re-index and by `AppState.rebuildSearchIndex(pipeline:)`, which both hubs' Rebuild Index now call. The subscription ignores an empty id (`markVolumeIndexed`). Because the re-read runs off the main actor, every incremental write to the set now goes through `markVolumeIndexed` / `markVolumeUnindexed` / `clearIndexedVolumeIds`, which journal while a re-read is in flight, and the re-read replays that journal over its answer — the removal routing, the deleted-volume hook and Erase Local Data included.
- **#1476**, the owner's 2026-09-30 wording. The hero is `DownloadedVolumesListModel.heroContent(catalogCount:interruptedCount:)`, drawn by both hubs: "—" and "Measuring…" (VoiceOver reads the dash as the sentence) until the first measurement, "—" and "Could not measure storage" after one fails with no earlier report, and a volume being removed counted in "1 being removed" / "%lld being removed", in neither "downloaded" nor "not yet indexed". Both hubs measure through `DownloadedVolumesListModel.measure(_:)`, which keeps the last report and records the error; the Mac's `try?` is gone and the Mac shows iOS's failure row. The dash is a key of its own (`settings.hub.hero.unmeasured`).
- **#1432.** iOS Free Up Space's rows carry `.disabled(isRemoving)`.
- **#1538.** `IndexDatabaseExporter.export` builds, switches to a rollback journal, strips, stamps and verifies the copy in a staging directory (the item-replacement directory for the destination, or the app's temporary directory), then moves it to the chosen file — an existing file is replaced in one step (`replaceItemAt`, review round 1). Nothing is created at the destination until the copy is complete, a failed copy — or a failed hand-over, unless the copy had to be staged on another volume — leaves an existing file there untouched, and the file handed over is one self-contained file. *Complete* is not *verified*: as before #1538, a copy whose verification finds problems is still handed over, with the problems in the report, so the plan of record's "until the copy verifies" is met as "until the copy is complete" (an owner question, below).
- **Fold-ins.** Both side-loaded Remove messages read their Markdown (`AttributedString(markdownBody:)`), so the owner's `**…**` stays in the text and no asterisk prints; review round 1 found the same defect in Archives' library-mode intro (“**your**”) and Archival Flows' unprinted outgoing caption (“*away*”) and fixed both. Boot calls `AppState.reconcileSideloadedVolumes()` once the volumes directory is set and the UI-test rows are on disk; the two doc comments that claimed a boot reconcile are now true.

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

The review's verified findings, each resolved in code, measured, or handed back to the owner.

**Fixed in code.**
- **Two more localized defaults printed their Markdown.** Archives' library-mode intro (`archival.library.intro %lld %lld`, the owner's "**your**", both platforms) and Archival Flows' unprinted outgoing caption (`archival.flows.caption.unprinted.outgoing %lld %lld`, "*away*") went to `Text(String)`, which renders verbatim. Both are drawn through `AttributedString(markdownBody:)` now, the `String(format:)` formatted first and then wrapped. The guard is tree-wide, where the lane's covered only its two keys: `EmbeddedMarkdownLinkTests.localizedMarkdownIsDrawnAsMarkdown` finds every localized default in the app carrying `**…**`, `*…*` or a link — five today: these two, the two side-loaded Remove messages and About's FRUS description — and fails until each is listed with the call that draws it and that call is in the code.
- **The #1538 guard looked once.** The exporter's observer is called after every step of the copy (`IndexDatabaseExporter.CopyStep`: the page copy, the journal switch, the strip, the views, the stamp, the verification), and `copyIsBuiltAwayFromTheDestination` requires every step, with the reader's writing kept and removed, each writing outside the chosen folder with nothing at the destination.
- **A failed hand-over lost the reader's earlier export** (both nits). `handOver` removed an existing file and then moved the copy, so a move that failed left neither. It now replaces an existing file with `replaceItemAt`, which swaps the two in one step and keeps the old file when it fails. The swap cannot cross volumes — measured in the probe below, `EXDEV` ("Cross-device link") under a Cocoa error 512 — so a copy the fallback staged on another volume still removes and then moves; `IndexDatabaseExporter.crossesVolumes` reads that shape.
- **Nothing guarded the hero's VoiceOver label.** `HubRemovalRoutingTests.heroDashReadsAsItsSentence` reads both hubs' `SettingsHeroCard(` arguments for `valueAccessibilityLabel: hero.valueAccessibilityLabel` and the card's value for its `.accessibilityLabel(Text(valueAccessibilityLabel ?? value))`.

**Measured: #1538 under the sandbox, by a probe.** A scratch Mac app (not in the repository; `~/Library/Caches/frus-lanes/w49/STOR/sandbox-probe/`), ad-hoc signed with `com.apple.security.app-sandbox`, launched through LaunchServices so it runs in its own container. Its only write grant outside the container is ONE literal file path, a temporary-exception entitlement standing in for the save panel's grant. It compiles `IndexDatabaseExporter` verbatim, from `origin/v2` and from this branch, and exports a real index, a 426 KB `frus.db` copied from the iPad simulator, into a folder of its own:
- **`origin/v2`**, switch on and off: `backupFailed("unable to open database file")`, and a 0-byte file left at the destination — #1538 exactly. Run over an earlier good copy, it left that copy 0 bytes too.
- **This branch**, switch on (fresh), off (over the first) and on again (over the second): `OK`, no integrity problems, 425,984 / 376,832 / 425,984 bytes. `sqlite3 -readonly` reads each copy as journal mode `delete`, integrity `ok`, `my_writing_included` 1 / 0 / 1. The staging directory was the container's `tmp/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_…`, and it was left empty.
- **To another volume** (a mounted APFS disk image, its file granted the same way), switch on and off: `OK` both times, the copy staged in that volume's own `.TemporaryItems`.
- **The hand-over itself**, with the probe's replica of the sequence: from the item-replacement directory, a remove-and-move and `replaceItemAt` both succeed under the one-file grant, fresh and over a file. Forced to the fallback (the container's `tmp`) with the destination on the other volume, remove-and-move succeeds and `replaceItemAt` fails with `EXDEV` and leaves the old file — which is why the fallback keeps the remove.

So the export's file sequence works under a sandbox that grants one file and nothing beside it, and the code it replaced fails there as the owner saw. What the probe cannot show is the save panel's own grant, a sandbox extension rather than an entitlement; the export from a signed, sandboxed build stays owed by eye.

## Session 2026-10-01 — A page reference opens the document its footnote names, heading-only containers leave the index, and a second pagination answers no page of the volume (lane PAGE; #1509, #1510, #1511; index v63)

**The question.** Lane PAGE of the 2026-09-28 plan of record. Three page-citation defects found by #1503's lane, and one fold-in:
- **#1509** — of several documents beginning on a cited page, a `pg_N` reference was stored against, and its link opened, the first, though the footnote often names a later one (1,825 times by #1509's count).
- **#1510** — a compilation, chapter or subchapter holding promoted sections was indexed as a pseudo-document beside them; in `frus1919Parisv13`, 740 pages named several sections at once. Owner decision D1 (§0) settles the rule.
- **#1511** — a second pagination's digit breaks (`frus1871`'s `pg-seq1_`, the President's messages) were read as the volume's pages.
- ◦ #1370's left-open persons-list item: "until his resignation on April 22, 1959" read 1959 as a start year.

**What was measured.** Corpus `HistoryAtState/frus` at `8e5da08c1`, whose `volumes/` are identical to `550a8c5c5` (empty `git diff`), so every #1503-era figure reproduces; `tools/page-citations` reproduced `xrefs_f.py`, `sections_by_volume.py` and `brackets.py` byte for byte before anything changed.
- **#1509, the cue.** Among the 12,761 references to a page several documents name, a document number given as a document's (`Doc. No. 497`, `document 131`) named exactly one 10 times by the exploratory pattern (11 by the shipped one) and never disagreed with the date; a bare `No. N` disagreed (`frus1934v01` d397's "Telegram No. 391, July 7" cites d390, dated July 7, beside d391) and was refused. Abbreviated months (`Oct. 9, 1909`) named a candidate the full-month pattern missed 723 times; day-month order ("5 June") 8 times, not taken. Taking a named day from the words just before the reference instead of the whole footnote lost "telegrams of December 11 and December 14, pp. 413 and 419", so the whole innermost footnote is the hint.
- **#1510.** An ElementTree pass and the replica agree: 201 containers, 169 heading-only (162 compilations, chapters and subchapters; 3 appendices; 4 historical documents) and 32 with text of their own, all in `frus1919Parisv13`, all printing that text before their first section.
- **#1511.** Digit breaks with a non-`pg_N` id, comments stripped: 185 with a `pg-seq` id in 7 volumes (`frus1871` 119, `frus1862` 20, `frus1865p1` 17, `frus1863p1` 14, `frus1866p1` 13, and the typos `frus1949v05` `pg-seq-1004` and `frus1950v01` `pg-seq-938`, both in `<back>` outside every AST), plus `frus1977-80v13`'s `pgg_655` and `frus1884`'s `pg_13` on `n="12"`, which are the volumes' own pages. The rule keys on the `pg-seq` shape, which reads the two typos as another pagination (no answer reads them) and keeps the other two as pages.

**What changed.**
- **#1509.** `PageSpanResolver.citedDocument(among:facts:citing:)` is the one tie-break, run whenever the page names several documents (several begin on it, where none does several are printed on it, or, in a volume that numbers its pages per document, several print a page of that number — the last named in review round 2): a document number the footnote gives exactly one of them, else the first whose day it names (a printed year must agree; a day counts only at day precision), else the first. `IndexingPipeline.resolvePageBasedCrossReferences` calls it with the footnote's `PageCitationHint` (carried on `CrossReferenceRow.citing`, keyed by `rowid`) and now runs after `document_dates` is written; the reader's page link calls it through `PageRangeStore.document(forPage:inVolume:citing:)`, the hint built from the same footnote AST by `ASTToRenderNodeConverter`, carried on `.crossRefLink`'s new `citing`, written into the link's query by `FRUSRenderNodeHTMLSerializer` and read back by `FRUSURLSchemeHandler`. Both readers run one row query (`arabicPageRowsSQL`) and one facts query (`citedDocumentFactsSQL`).
- **#1510 (D1).** `TEIParserDelegate` marks a frame that holds a promoted section (`holdsPromotedSection`, passed up through wrappers). Such a compilation, chapter or subchapter holding only a heading and breaks is not emitted and its heading goes nowhere; one with text keeps the breaks within it. The breaks either leaves go, in `finishParse`, to the section whose div opens first after them (`FRUSDocumentAST.carriedPages`, written as that section's `page_ranges` rows), and are dropped when that is a document, whose start page already covers them. Appendix and historical-document containers are unchanged.
- **#1511.** `PageNumber.otherPagination`: a digit break with a `pg-seq` id, stored as `other-pagination`, read by no page lookup, drawn with its number.
- **Persons.** `endEventCueRegex`: "until"/"till", one to six words, "in"/"on", then the date — an end. "to" and "before" are excluded on purpose (fixtures pin both).
- `currentDateIndexVersion` 62 → 63, with the v63 note; `currentPersonRollupVersion` is not bumped (the date-index stamp already rebuilds the rollup after the re-index; `rollupBuiltMidReindexIsRebuiltAfter` pins it).
- **Tools.** `replica.py` replicates v63 by default and v62 with `RULE=v62` (byte-identical to the old replica); `simulate.py` gains rule G; `scan_corpus.py` records each document's `@n` and winning date attribute and each reference's text and offsets (every scan-reading script's output unchanged); `v63.py` measures v63 against v62, and since review round 1 also counts the references made inside sections and refuses swapped replicas. README updated.
- **Docs.** Four proposals in `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md` (Mac §8.5 and iOS §8.6 page references, Mac §6.3 and iOS §6.5 active years), seven since review round 1 (Mac and iOS §11.4, iOS §15.4); seven EditableContent `lines:` ranges re-pointed and logged; `SimilarityModel`'s `frus1919Parisv13` count (170 → 153 indexed).

## Session 2026-10-01 — A stopped sync now shows and names its cause, Fix iCloud Sync warns before discarding unsent changes, and a Debug build keeps its own store (lane SYNC, #1531)

**The question.** #1531's outage ended with the owner's Production deploy of `CD_GeneratedSummary.CD_sourceContentHash` on 2026-09-28. Lane SYNC had to make the next one visible and diagnosable on the device, and stop a Debug build from setting it off again: the plan of record's seven items (§2, §3a D13), with no retry control, and the fold-in for an active project deleted on another device.

**What was measured.**
- `xcrun cktool export-schema` on this Mac (Xcode 27.0) exits 64 with "No management token found in arguments, CLOUDKIT_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN environment variable, or built-in methods. (See: save-token)". So the gate below fails here, as designed, and Production's schema was not read.
- A process can read its own system log on the iOS 26.5 simulator: a test writes an error-level line under a `com.apple.coredata.*` subsystem naming `CD_FRUSTestRecord` and `CD_frusTestField`, and `OSLogStore(scope: .currentProcessIdentifier)` returns it (the test passes in about 3 s).
- The schema's to-many relationship sides, which CloudKit holds on the to-one side: 3 (`CD_ArchiveVisitPlan.CD_documents`, `CD_ArchiveVisitPlan.CD_targets`, `CD_Collection.CD_documentEntries`).

**What changed.**
1. **The observer exists before the container.** `SyncEventMonitor` (`SyncDiagnosticsLog.swift`) is installed by `makeFRUSContainer()` immediately before it builds the CloudKit container. It files every ended event's Sync Log row and keeps the remembered failure without `AppState`, and holds events (up to 500) until `bootDownloadManager` attaches, which replays them in order. The late observer in `bootDownloadManager` is gone. A replayed first import now also sets `hasInitialProjectSyncSettled`, which a missed one never did.
2. **A failed upload is remembered across launches.** `SyncExportFailureMemory` keeps one `UnrecoveredExport` per build configuration in `UserDefaults` (never SwiftData). A failed export starts or extends it, keeping its first date and launch; only a successful export, or a Fix iCloud Sync reset that removed every store file it found (since review round 1), ends it. `ICloudStatusSummary` resolves it after local-only, the account and the zone. Begun in an earlier launch, it is `.stopped`: the banner reads **iCloud Sync Stopped** / "Sync stopped on this device; your changes are kept here.", promising no retry, and the Settings row and the Mac chip read **Sync Stopped** with since when and a diagnostic. Begun in this launch, it is `.failed` (lane WB's line, unchanged) until an upload succeeds; a successful import no longer quiets it.
3. **After a failed event the app reads its own system log.** `SystemLogSchemaScan` (`CloudKitErrorInspector.swift`) takes Core Data and CloudKit lines within 5 s of the event, at error or fault level or carrying the server's rejection, through the existing `CD_…` allow-list, the names on a line carrying the server's rejection ranked before the rest under the twelve-name cap (since review round 1). The row shows "└ system log: …" (or "no schema names" or "could not be read"), and an export's names join the remembered failure, so its Diagnostic line names the record type and field; a name already remembered is never evicted by a later one. One read per 30 s.
4. **Fix iCloud Sync warns.** While an upload is unrecovered, the confirmation opens with a warning naming when uploads stopped, before the owner's message (unchanged); the row reads "Would discard changes not yet in iCloud"; the ladder's footer stops calling it the rung that deletes nothing. A real container fallback reads the remembered failure too.
5. **No retry control**, and no Check Again (the decision below).
6. **The release gate.** `Scripts/check_cloudkit_schema.py` exports Production's schema with cktool and fails (exit 1) when Production lacks any identifier the inventory says a record can carry: `installedIdentifiers` less `identifiersAwaitingWriter` and the new `identifiersNotStoredAsFields`. No token, or any cktool failure, is exit 2 with the fix. `--schema-file` checks an exported file; `--self-test` runs 32 checks offline (18 before review round 1). A live read of Production also records what it held in `.cache/cloudkit-schema-gate/production-schema.txt`, and EVERY archive checks that record: the archive-only phase **Check CloudKit schema**, first on both app targets (review round 1), runs the script's `--archive-phase` mode and fails the archive when the record is missing or lacks an identifier the inventory can write. So a TestFlight or App Store archive from Xcode is gated as `notarize.sh`'s DMG is (notarize.sh runs the live read first). The inventory's 1.7 note is corrected (the 09-03 promotion carried eight identifiers, not nine) and the marker moves to build 48, 2026-09-28; the baseline count and digest do not move.
7. **A Debug build keeps its own store.** `FRUSStoreConfiguration` names the Debug store `FRUSExplorerDebug.store` (and `FRUSExplorerLocalDebug.store`), keeping the bundle id. The shipped build still opens `default.store`. A Debug Fix iCloud Sync clears only the Debug files, and since review round 1 each build reads and clears only its own Fix iCloud Sync request (`PendingStoreReset.requestKey(for:)`; the shipped build keeps the old key). Each Sync Log row records "Debug" or "Release".
- **Fold-in.** `ProjectAdminService.clearActiveProjectIfDeleted` runs in the import-settle debounce and returns the device to Global Context when its active project is gone from the settled store — in a shipped build only, since review round 1: a Debug build shares `activeProjectId` with the shipped app but not its store. A project merged on another device lands this device in Global Context too, not in the merge target, which nothing synced names.
- **Docs.** Ten EditableContent blocks; 38 ranges re-pointed; five proposals in `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md` under "SYNC — #1531".

**Decisions the lane text did not settle.**
- No **Check Again**: the plan allowed "at most" one, and the outage's own record shows the health check reporting "zone ok" throughout; only an upload ends the stopped state.
- A failure begun in THIS launch stays `.failed` over later events, so an unrecovered upload is never quiet.
- The Debug switch is the compile-time `DEBUG` flag, not the signing environment, because a runtime reading that misread a TestFlight build would open an empty store.
- The 09-03 attestation is corrected, not re-listed in `identifiersAwaitingDeploy`: the field was deployed on 2026-09-28. What confirmed it is that exports which had failed on that field succeeded afterwards, in the Mac's system log and the iPhone's Sync Log. That is evidence for this one field only; Production's schema was not read, so the rest of the baseline is still the owner's attestation.
- The gate requires `identifiersAwaitingDeploy` of Production and exempts the to-many sides, which the inventory lists but CloudKit is not expected to store; that exemption is from the mirroring design, not measured against an exported schema.
- The active-project reconcile waits for a settled store, so a UI test's dangling `activeProjectId` (no CloudKit, no import) is left alone, as `ToolbarOverflowAccessibilityTests` needs.

**How it was verified** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A36F4C02`):
- **A/B by mutation**, restored from a snapshot each time. Round A put the pre-#1531 behaviour back behind the new APIs: one store file, the observer after the container, no buffering and no memory, the status ignoring it, no warnings, no scan rules, no reconcile. "✘ Test run with 149 tests in 15 suites failed after 7.772 seconds with 82 issues". Round B took the mutations round A would mask: a naive log tokenizer, the stopped check above the account and zone, the reset's list built apart from the container's, a renamed release store, Global Context treated as a project, the owner's message altered, and `record` dropping the new fields. "✘ Test run with 53 tests in 7 suites failed after 2.315 seconds with 18 issues". Every new test failed in one round or the other.
- **The lane's suites** with `EditableContentKeyTests`: "✔ Test run with 170 tests in 16 suites passed after 5.128 seconds".
- **The full unit target:** "✔ Test run with 6034 tests in 718 suites passed after 199.554 seconds".
- **The gate:** `--self-test` 18 of 18 (32 of 32 after review round 1); a real run here exits 2 naming the missing token.
- **macOS build:** `FRUSExplorerMac` "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **" (Xcode 27.0, signing off), with no warning beyond the two known residues.

**Not verified.**
- On a device: the plan's Development-device A/B with an unpublished field, and the Mac and iPhone system logs. Whether Core Data logs a rejected export at error level on hardware is unmeasured; the scan is best-effort and records "no schema names" when it finds none.
- That an export event runs on every launch, which is what ends a recovered failure. The outage's logs show export rows on most launches, not all.
- The gate against Production itself: no management token is saved on this Mac. Nor a real archive through the new phase: it was measured in a sandboxed probe project with the same layout (review round 1, below).
- An offline device: if an export fails for want of a network, the failure is remembered and shows until an upload succeeds.

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

The two-lens review confirmed seven findings, which are five distinct issues because both lenses found two of them, and offered eight nits. All are resolved; no nit is left.

**The gate guarded only the Mac DMG.** `Scripts/check_cloudkit_schema.py` had one caller, `notarize.sh`. TestFlight and App Store archives are made in Xcode, which is how builds 45–48 reached testers. Now every archive runs it. A new archive-only phase, **Check CloudKit schema**, runs first on both app targets, so a refused archive fails before the Release compile, and it calls the script's `--archive-phase` mode. The phase is declared in `project.yml`. The `project.pbxproj` phases are XcodeGen's own output for that spec, generated into a scratch directory and copied in, so a later `xcodegen generate` writes the same phases. The phase runs under `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING`, which keeps it from the keychain token and the network. So a live read (run by hand, or by `notarize.sh`) records what Production held in `.cache/cloudkit-schema-gate/production-schema.txt`. The phase compares the inventory being archived with that record, and fails the archive when the record is missing, is not a read of the app's Production container, or lacks an identifier the inventory can write. Production's schema is append-only, so a record never goes stale where it matters. An identifier added to the inventory after the read fails the archive until the script is run again. The deploy checklist in `CloudKitSchemaInventoryTests` now has the gate as step 5, and the baseline advice requires it to pass. The suite header and the inventory say the claim is now checked outside the app. `CLAUDE.md` was not edited; the proposed text is in this round's open items.
- Measured with `xcodebuild install` of a sandboxed probe project with the same `SRCROOT` layout (Xcode 27.0, `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES`, the final script):
  - With no record: "error: CloudKit schema gate: no live read of Production has been recorded on this Mac (… is missing)." and "** INSTALL FAILED **".
  - With #1531's record (the field missing): "error:   CD_GeneratedSummary.CD_sourceContentHash" and "** INSTALL FAILED **".
  - With a complete record: "CloudKit schema gate: Production, as read …, holds every identifier this build can write." and "** INSTALL SUCCEEDED **".
  - A plain build: "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **", with the phase not run.
  - With the record present but left out of the phase's inputs: "[Errno 1] Operation not permitted … this is the script sandbox". So the sandbox is real here, and the declaration is what admits the record.
  - The app itself was not archived.
- `--self-test`: 32 checks, 14 of them new.

**A Debug run cleared the shipped app's active project.** `ProjectAdminService.clearActiveProjectIfDeleted` now does nothing in a Debug build. `activeProjectId` is one `UserDefaults` key that both builds read, and UI tests pin it by that name, so keying it per configuration was not an option. The function takes `configuration: FRUSStoreConfiguration = .current`, and the reconcile tests name `.release`. `FRUSStoreConfiguration`'s doc no longer calls the shared `UserDefaults` harmless.

**Three monitor rules were untested.**
- The arrival order while a failed row waits on the system log: `aWaitingFailedRowKeepsItsPlace` files a failure, whose row waits 500 ms, and then a success.
- The 30 s limit on system-log reads: `systemLogReadsAreSpaced` sends failures at 0, 10 and 31 s, which must read, not read, and read.
- The export-only absorb: `importScanDoesNotJoinTheRun`.

**Line references in `Manual-Revisions-Pending.md`.**
- WB's `DataRecoveryView.swift:142` is now `:284`, in two places.
- WB's `AppState.swift:897` is now `:914`: 14 lines from the lane and 3 from this round.
- The lane's `SyncDiagnosticsLog.swift:324` is now `:325`, in two places.
- Every other reference into a file this lane changed was checked, and lands on its line.

**Nits.**
- Fix iCloud Sync's request is kept per build configuration (`PendingStoreReset.requestKey(for:)`). The shipped build keeps `frus.pendingStoreReset`, so a request made before an update still runs after it.
- A reset forgets the remembered failure only when it removed every file it found (`ModelContainer.performRequestedReset`). `makeFRUSContainer()` calls it, and no longer forgets on its own.
- The system-log scan ranks the names on a rejection line before the others under the twelve-name cap. The remembered list never evicts a name it already holds; later names fill only the room that is left.

- Inventory note 1.9 and `deployedThroughBuild`'s doc claim only what was seen: one field confirmed, and Production's schema not read.
- The two test helpers that made `UserDefaults` suites now remove them when each test ends.

**Docs.** No EditableContent text changed. One ranged block is re-pointed: `cloudkit.account.noAccount` in `09-Settings-and-App.md`, from `AppState.swift` 579–580 to 582–583. Earlier paragraphs of this entry are corrected in place.

**How it was verified** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A36F4C02`). Every mutation was applied by a script and undone by copying back a snapshot, never with git.

## Session 2026-10-01 — A Department of State series, the State FOIA reading room and the Nixon materials are no longer filed as RG 59 central files; a central-file note stores the Subject-Numeric file it cites; the packet's crib and divided-lot lines say what is true (lane NOTE; #1514, #1515, #1404, five fold-ins and one fix from the plan's §4)

**The question.** Lane NOTE of the 2026-09-28 plan of record. #1514 (decision D2, "wide"): `SourceNoteParser.matchesCentralFiles` took every narrative citation that names the Department of State in its first sentence, so the Department's own series that are not the central files — the INR/IL and INR–NIE files and the like — the State FOIA reading room, two Nixon Presidential Materials notes and a lot printed without the word were filed as RG 59 central files. Source Explorer drew the Central Files panel and NARA's RG 59 guidance for them, an Archives Visit counted a College Park central-file target, and the provenance counts filed them under the decimal file. A Subject-Numeric file with no number (`POL CHICOM -US`) stored no file at all. #1515: eight `Vol. N` notes stored no file, and the packet's crib printed `IRAN-U.S` for `DEF 15–3 IRAN-U.S.`. #1404: the mirror-gated footnote parity test failed on two volumes without guarding anything. The §2 row's five fold-ins: title-case and hyphenated designators (`Def 12 NATO`), the rows under a full-name library heading (`Princeton University Library`), the pre-1906 classifier's "department of state" cue, the crib's choice of example, and the divided-lot denominator. One more item was taken as extra scope, from the plan's §4 list of unfiled fixes rather than from §2: the live NARA decoder's series dates (`Plan-Of-Record-2026-09-28.md` §4, "the live NARA catalog decoder misreads series dates").

**What was measured, and how.**
- **The instrument.** A `SourceExplorerExportGenerator` run on `origin/v2` 95bfc706 (corpus `550a8c5c5`, 553 manifest volumes, 264,552 document source notes) gives the app's own parse of every note. The notes were then driven through a probe compiled once from v2's SourceNoteKit and once from the lane's. The v2 probe reproduces the export's kind and central-file identifier for 264,552 of 264,552 notes, so the diff is the parser's.
- **The census behind "wide".** Of the central-file notes that name neither the central files nor RG 59, 605 lead with the Department (and 5 name it later). Grouped by the segment after the lead: the INR/IL Historical Files 283 (in its spellings), INR–NIE 101, the Bureau of Intelligence and Research 31, INR Historical 25, the Electronic Reading Room 23, Bundy 15, INR Files 14, INR/IL Files 13, Har-Van 11, INR/IL Historical Records 11, USUN 5+6, the Executive Secretariat 5, IO 6, STARS 5, and a tail. What stays a central file is a note that names a file: a Central Files label in its misprints (`Central File`, `Centrals Files`, `Central piles`, a bare `Central`), a file number in the first segment, a Subject-Numeric designator, a dotted decimal number later (`Conference Files, 396.1–GE/7–1855`), or STARS, the Department's electronic central record system of 1989–92. Of the 605, the new strategy makes 555 named series and 1 a lot; 28 are publications (the reading room, the press releases); 21 stay central files.
- **What moves.** 1,175 notes change parse:
  - **601 leave `.centralFiles`**: 567 to `.namedFileSeries` (`Department of State, <series>`; the 555 above and 12 abstracts led by `DOS`), 31 to `.previouslyPublished` (26 reading-room notes, the Department's press releases and its *Dispatch*), 2 to `.presidentialLibrary` (the Nixon materials) and 1 to `.lotFile` (`OAS Files: 60 D 665`). Central-file notes 194,807 → 194,206. By series: INR/IL Historical 335, INR–NIE 109, INR Historical 25, Bundy 17, INR Files 14, Har-Van 13, INR/IL Files 13, USUN 11, the Executive Secretariat 9, IO 6, 15 others. They sit in 112 volumes; any change at all reaches 139.
  - **10 more move**: 6 Nixon-materials notes from `.unrecognized` to `.presidentialLibrary`, and 4 reading-room notes to `.previouslyPublished` from `.cfpfFile` (3, each read off a remark's film number) and `.ciaCollection` (1).
  - **564 central-file notes change identifier**: 429 Subject-Numeric files with no number are now stored (`POL GER W–US` ×46, `POL CHICOM -US` ×46, `POL US USSR` ×17, …, 144 distinct); 87 classifications run on without a stop are cut off (`POL 26 S VIET Top Secret; Emergency` → `POL 26 S VIET`, 11 volumes), 12 of which had stored none because the run-on segment passed sixty characters (`SOC 14-1 S VIET` ×8, `POL 26-1 S VIET`, `POL 15-1 S VIEI` and `POL 2-4 S VIET`, frus1961-63v03; `POL 26 S VIET`, frus1961-63v04/d258); 38 title-case designators are respelled (`Def 12 NATO` → `DEF 12 NATO`, all frus1961-63v13); 5 hyphenated ones too (`POL-1 S AFR` → `POL 1 S AFR`); the stop of `U.S.`/`U.S.S.R.`/`E.T.` is kept (3); and `ORG 7 S` and `POL 1 US–VIET S` are read from frus1964-68v01 d111 and d229, whose citations are split at stops.
  - **Neighbours** (each note's `archivalNeighborKey`; two notes are neighbours when the key is shared): notes with a neighbour 237,505 → 237,929; 445 gain one; 21 lose one. Every one of the 21 was grouped on a folder title or a fragment (`5412 Special Group` ×9, `S.G. 2/4/15` ×7, the `US` of `US/A/M(SR)/1`, `303`, `TIN 980643000012`), and a named series has no neighbour route.
- **The pre-1906 cue** (the input: a regex census of the first `<dateline>` of 46,710 documents in the 81 manifest volumes whose span opens before 1906, joining each dateline's pieces as the index stores it; a few of those documents are dated after the classifier's 1906 gate and are counted where they fall — corrected in review round 1, which re-ran it): 41 datelines name a department of state that is not the U.S. one — the Confederate department at Richmond 12, a foreign ministry styled `Department of State for Foreign Affairs` or `… and (of) Foreign Relations` 21 (Paraguay 11, Portugal 7 with no place, Mexico 2, Haiti 1), and a foreign department at its own capital with no style 8 (Madrid's Palace and its bureau ×7, Monrovia). Three more print a foreign capital after the Department and are U.S. letters: Frelinghuysen's two instructions datelined `Department of State, Mexico` (frus1884/d254, d262) and Denby's despatch `Department of State, Peking, … (Received December 5.)` (frus1885/d119). 37 U.S. datelines are spelt otherwise (33 inside the gate), and the old cue read 5 of them (`State Department` ×3, `Dapartment of State` ×2); the rest are misprints — `of` misread (`op` ×7, `oe` ×2, `or`, `in`), letters dropped or added (`Deparment` ×3, `Department of Stats` ×4, `Departmrnt`, `Stpte`, …) and stray punctuation (`Department.of`, `of’State`). 57 documents have the Secretary's surname as sender and no Washington, Department, legation, embassy or consulate in the dateline; the sitting Secretaries among them wrote from Auburn, Bar Harbor, Falmouth and Wilmington, Del.
- **The crib.** Over the same notes on the new parser: of 188,777 central-file identifiers opening with a digit, the new decimal test refuses 50 (Numerical File numbers with a dash after the slash, OCR-damaged classes); of 5,222 opening with a letter, the Subject-Numeric test refuses 1,558 (every `Paris Peace Conf.` number, the STARS record numbers) and admits 3,664 (3,516 handbook designators, 138 organization files, 10 slips).

**What changed.**
- **`SourceNoteParser`** (SourceNoteKit 1.16):
  - `tryDepartmentSeries`, tried before `matchesCentralFiles`, reads a Department-led citation (`Department of State`, `… Files`, the misprint `States`, the abstracts' `DOS`) that names no central files, no file number and not STARS. It makes `.namedFileSeries(seriesName: "Department of State, <series>", fileIdentifier: <the folder>)`: an office printed before its series joins the name (`Bureau of Intelligence and Research, INR/IL Historical Files`), and a colon tail opens the file. A lot printed without the word is `.lotFile`.
  - `leadsWithReadingRoom`: an agency's FOIA reading room at the head of a citation is `.previouslyPublished`, ahead of the CIA and CFPF strategies. Four publication leads are added: the Department's press releases and its *Dispatch*.
  - A note led by `Nixon Presidential Materials` takes `tryNixonPresidentialMaterials`, which only a National Archives lead used to reach.
  - `extractFirstIdentifier` admits a Subject-Numeric designator with no number by its handbook category (`ParsedSourceNote.subjectNumericCategories`, the 60 categories of the two shipped schedules, pinned to `subject-numeric-labels.json` by a test). It respells a title-case or hyphenated lead (`normalizingSubjectNumericLead`), cuts a classification run on without a stop (`cuttingRunOnClassification`), keeps an initials stop (`withoutClosingStop`), and reads the sentence after a citation that ends on a bare Central Files label.
  - `subjectNumericFileLocation(of:)` routes a designator with no number, so it has neighbours.
  - `CollectionKeying.identity` keys no authority collection for a Department series (its leading segment is the holder). `CollectionKeying.bridgedRepository(ofHeading:)` is the full-name bridge both Sources parsers now inherit.
- **The app.**
  - Source Explorer's named-series panel names the holder when the series' name opens with an agency (`NamedFileSeriesRouting.explainer`/`macNote`, two new keys). It used to say the repository was not stated, which was false for the Department's series, and for the National Security Council's and other agencies' since #353.
  - `SourcesParserDelegate` and its generator port inherit a full-name heading's repository (`Princeton University`, `Reagan Presidential Library` → Reagan Library), so the rows under it are keyed as the authority keys them.
  - `TripPacketBuilder.centralFileDesignation` keeps an initials stop. `TripPacketExporter.cribExamples` takes the first designation that passes `isDecimalFileDesignation` / `isSubjectNumericDesignation`. The coverage report's access block opens on divided lots as well as the triage, and prints its all-clear only when every claimant of every divided lot is measured and unrestricted — and not at all when nothing resolved.
  - `CentralFilesClassifier.isUSDepartmentDateline` and `sittingSecretarySender`: a Confederate or foreign department is not the Department (a foreign ministry's letter takes the despatch fallback, as an enclosure; a Confederate one takes none), the U.S. Department spelt otherwise is (round 0 read the two spellings the old cue already knew; review round 1 reads every misprint the census found), and the sitting Secretary's letter is the Department's from wherever he wrote it, by a 1860–1909 tenure table.
  - `NARACatalogClient.seriesDateRange(in:)` reads NARA's date objects and both pairs, and takes their union.
- **#1404** is test-only: `RealTEIFootnoteParityTests` keys a class row as a class (`class:<key>`), and the generator side carries the class channel through `FootnoteIbidGapWalker.shippedAdmissionVerdict` — direct candidates, then bare-`Ibid.` inheritances.
- **Index v63 → v64** (`currentDateIndexVersion`, header 4.26), numbered after lane PAGE's v63 and 4.25.
- **Regenerated artifacts** (corpus `550a8c5c5`, `GENERATED_DATE=2026-10-01`, in CLAUDE.md's run order; each first regenerated to scratch at its committed stamp, so a diff against the bundle is the change and nothing else):
  - **`collection-authority.json`**: 4,083 → 4,051 records (lot-keyed 1,718 and with a NAID 1,014, both unchanged). The full-name heading bridge files the Sources rows under a library or university heading that a volume nests inside another holder's list under that library — frus1981-88v41 prints its libraries inside the Department of State's list, frus1981-88v13 and frus1969-76v10 theirs inside the National Archives'. Rows move in 12 volumes; 57 records go, 25 come, 36 change; the report's unmerged ambiguous clusters fall 419 → 391. `collection-authority-report.txt` is regenerated with it. The re-routed Department series add no record (`CollectionKeying.identity`). Four tests pinned the old artifact and follow it: `CollectionAuthorityStoreTests`' and `ArchivesArrangementTests`' record count; `ManuscriptRepositoryBridgeTests`' Bandow citation, which now resolves on the Reagan Library's own key instead of reaching a Department of State cluster through the alias step; and `ArchivalNetworkLabelTests`' pinned label counts over the Whitman File's real neighbourhood, 7 and 5 → 6 and 6 at 1000 × 640 and 700 × 420 (the first full unit run after the regeneration failed exactly those two cases, "placed 6 of 19").
  - **`collection-usage-index.json`**: the categories move exactly as the probe measured (central files −601, named series +567, publications +35, presidential libraries +8, unrecognized −6, CFPF −3, CIA −1, lots +1); 50 volumes lose every central-file note they had (410 → 360 volumes), each of those notes a Department series or the reading room, frus1964-68v32's 52 INR/IL notes the largest. Notes in a collection 75,028 → 75,037 (the eight Nixon-materials notes and the lot); notes with a class 190,429 → 190,427, the two INR/IL folders of the 303/40 Committee no longer read as decimal class 303; authority reached 1,834 of 4,051.
  - **`external-citation-index.json`**: references joined 18,852 → 18,968, units 1,254 → 1,258, pairs 3,075 → 3,107. 116 of the new joins are footnotes citing the Reagan Library's President's Daily Diary, which had no Reagan record until the bridge gave frus1981-88v13's row one; the rest are the Reagan rows' ids moving. The decimal channel and its vocabulary digest are unchanged.

It moves 486 where `document_sources` moves 601 because this generator parses each `type="source"` element's whole text: a `[Source: …]` wrapper or a cover-sheet remark quoting the Director of Central Intelligence already sent some of those notes elsewhere, before and after (frus1958-60v19's fourteen INR–NIE notes are `intelligence` or `unrecognized` here).
  - Each committed artifact equals its scratch twin but for the `generated` stamp. CLAUDE.md's entries for the five generators carry the new figures.
- **`SourceNoteKit/eval-baseline.txt`** (`SourceNoteEvalGenerator` over `citations.csv`'s 267,663 notes): unrecognized 5,469 → 5,465, central files 194,944 → 194,358, named series 6,232 → 6,785, previously published 950 → 985. `ProvenanceSource`'s doc and the `provenance.parseResidual.disclosure` editor's note quote the new overall figure; the bands the shipped sentence rounds are unchanged.

**How it was verified** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`; Xcode 27.0):
- **SPM A/B, by copying v2's `SourceNoteParser.swift` and `CollectionKeying.swift` over the fixed ones** (with a stub giving the new API names v2's behaviour, so the new tests compile) and restoring them by copy, checked byte for byte with `cmp`. Over the five suites in `DepartmentSeriesTests.swift`, `CitationSentenceIdentifierTests` and `SiblingHeadingExtractorTests`, A: "✘ Test run with 50 tests in 6 suites failed after 0.027 seconds with 66 issues." and "✘ Test run with 14 tests in 1 suite failed after 0.014 seconds with 2 issues."; B: "✔ Test run with 50 tests in 6 suites passed after 0.021 seconds." and "✔ Test run with 14 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.013 seconds." Twenty-three tests fail on A. The ones that pass there are controls — a reading room or the Nixon materials named only in a remark, a classification marking after a stopped label, a capitalised pair that is no designator, the category pin — and each has a mutant that kills it: fourteen mutants (the identity guard, the Central Files label check, the designator check, STARS, the two lead anchors, the category membership, a dotless class admitted, the later-segment category rule, the run-on follower lookahead, the next-sentence classification guard, the abbreviation stop, any-lead respelling, the lower-case refusal) each failed at least one test.
- **App A/B, by the same method over eleven app and kit files** (v2's, with a stub for the classifier's new helpers) and v2's `ExternalCitationTests.swift`: "✘ Test run with 116 tests in 7 suites failed after 4.547 seconds with 46 issues.", #1404 reproduced among them (frus1955-57v19 one mismatch, frus1958-60v03 nine, and an extra `lib:Department of State||` row); B, with the TEI mirror: "✔ Test run with 191 tests in 9 suites passed after 48.285 seconds." `TripPacketExporterTests.cribFormTests` pins the two new crib predicates, which v2 does not have, so it has no A side; the crib behaviour it serves is guarded by "A plan holding only titles and record numbers gets neither central example", which failed on A.
- **After the regeneration**, the lane's suites with the TEI mirror, plus the suites that read the docs and the regenerated authority: "✔ Test run with 203 tests in 11 suites passed after 43.424 seconds." (the footnote parity test ran, 5.2 s).
- **The full unit target:** the first run after the regeneration, "✘ Test run with 6006 tests in 712 suites failed after 273.414 seconds with 2 issues." — the two `ArchivalNetworkLabelTests` cases above; after them, "✔ Test run with 6006 tests in 712 suites passed after 252.769 seconds." and "** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **". `build-for-testing` printed no warning beyond the known `GeneratedSummary` and AppIntents residues.
- **SPM:** `swift test` over the package, every target: 37 runs, 1,577 tests, every one "✔ … passed", exit 0, after the regeneration.

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

Ten confirmed findings and six nits, each resolved below; the paragraphs above that stated a figure the review found wrong are corrected in place.

- **An Archives Visit placed the re-routed Department series at College Park, and Source Explorer offered NARA's State records page for them.** `ResearchFacilityResolver.facility` takes the series name (`seriesName:`, ResearchFacility 1.2) and resolves a named series whose stored name opens with the agency holding it to `unknown`, so the packet lists it under *Confirm before you travel* instead of heading a College Park chapter with it. The rule reads `SourceNoteParser.namedSeriesHolder`, so it covers the Department's own series (567 notes) and the other agencies' since #353 (514 the National Security Council's, 90 six more agencies'): 1,171 notes in 144 volumes. The citation places those series with an agency, frus1964-68v07's Sources describes the INR/IL Historical Files as "still under Department of State custody", and whether any was accessioned since is not something a citation states — #353's own reason for parsing them as named series. `TripPacketModel.build` passes a named-series group's label, which is its stored series name. Both Source Explorer views gate the link "Department of State records at the National Archives" on `NamedFileSeriesRouting.offersStateRecordsLink` (iOS 1.14, Mac 1.13), which withholds it for the same series. Tests: `ResearchFacilityTests` (three holders, one control per conjunct), `TripPacketBuilderTests.departmentSeriesGroupIsUnplaced` (through the real builder), `NamedFileSeriesRoutingTests` (below).
- **Number-less designators the rule refuses still store no file, and the manual proposal said they all do.** Documented, not parsed: `digitlessSubjectNumericRegex` refuses lower case after the category to keep `POL Files` and prose out, and admitting a title-case element needs a word list and a corpus re-measure, and would move notes `tryDepartmentSeries` reads. Round 1 counted 31 in 7 volumes; review round 2 corrected that to 126 in 11 volumes, in four shapes, all listed under *Still open*. The Mac and iOS §14.8 proposals keep the caveat (next item).
- **The §14.8 proposal deleted a caveat that is still true.** It keeps "none for some notes that do name a file", with two examples that hold: a note cited under the National Archives' own name and record group (`TripPacketBuilder.fileDesignation` gives none for any `naraCollection` note; 5,951 cite `RG 59, Central Files` that way) and a number-less designator whose country is not printed in capitals (`POL Laos`).
- **A flagged plan-level count left divided lots out.** When a resolved series is flagged, the access block now adds "That count leaves out divided lots, which resolve to no single series: N of this plan's M divided lots have a claimant series that is restricted or has no stated status." (TripPacketExporter 2.5). `flaggedCountNamesTheDividedLots`, one fixture per conjunct of an unclear lot, and its control.
- **The pre-1906 cue read 5 of the U.S. Department's misspellings; the census finds 37.** `usDepartmentNamePattern` reads all of them — `of` misread (`op`, `oe`, `or`, `in`), letters dropped or added (`Deparment`, `Stats`, `Departmrnt`, `Stpte`, …), stray punctuation (`Department.of`, `of’State`) — and nothing the census holds that is not a department of state. Four U.S. letters no rule read are now the Department's: Hunter to Biddle (frus1872p1/d411), Adee to Pauncefote among the Samoan papers (frus1894app1/d591), Hill to Beaupré (frus1902/d267) and the Secretary to the German chargé (frus1905/d687).
- **The census in `isUSDepartmentDateline`'s doc and above was wrong in three places.** Re-run, it reads 41 departments of state that are not the U.S. one, not 44; the "foreign departments at their own capital" were 8 (Madrid ×7, Monrovia) plus 3 U.S. letters — Frelinghuysen's two instructions datelined `Department of State, Mexico` and Denby's despatch from Peking; the unplaced foreign ministries are Portugal's 7, not six; and the U.S. Department is spelt otherwise 37 times, not 5. `mexico` leaves `foreignDepartmentPlaces` (its only effect was on the two U.S. instructions, which the sender rule happened to rescue), and so do `luque`, `asuncion`, `asunción` and `port au prince`, whose datelines all carry the `… Foreign Relations` style the regex reads. `peking` stays, and its doc says why: its one dateline is the U.S. minister's despatch, which the despatch fallback places.
- **No fixture isolated the three new dateline clauses, and frus1884/d254's fixture invented its sender.** `departmentSpeltOtherwise` drives six verbatim headers and datelines whose senders no rule reads — it asserts that `sittingSecretarySender` is false and the chapter is no legation's (where `secretaryOfStateSender` reads Adee and Wharton as the Department, which is why `State Department` decides no corpus document in its own chapter, and frus1894app1/d638 is placed under Germany here); `departmentMisprints` pins 19 spellings through the predicate; `foreignDepartmentIsNotTheDepartment` adds Portugal's unplaced style and one fixture per place (Palace, Madrid, Monrovia, Peking). d254 is its real header now, `Mr. Frelinghuysen to Mr. Morgan`, read as the instruction it is (`frelinghuysenAtMexico`).
- **#1460's pipeline test guarded nothing.** `reprintYearIsNotAnIdentifier` leads d1, d2 and d4 with the Central Files (constructed; the notes they were are Department series now) and replaces d3 with frus1955-57v01/d168, verbatim, whose drafting remark carries no classification, so #1514's run-on cut cannot stand in for the citation-sentence bound. ## Session 2026-10-01 — The app checks its language analysis again each time it comes back to the foreground, never starts it in a background launch, logs every step in release builds, and says in Settings what works (lane LANG, #1539)

**The question.** On the owner's iPhone and iPad (iOS 27.0, build 48) Search's Collocates refused for want of a lemmatiser, and after a force-quit and relaunch it worked on both (plan of record §0, 2026-09-29). So the assets were on the devices, and the refusal came from a verdict fixed earlier in a long-lived process: #1373 made it once per process, as a `static let`, started in both `FRUSExplorerApp` inits — which a background launch also runs — under one 30 s budget shared by the three asset requests, with the canary run as soon as that budget ran out. Steps A–C of the lane: log the warm-up in release builds and show the verdict in Settings; re-check on the next foreground and adopt a better verdict; never start the warm-up in a background launch, and do not tag while a request is in flight.

**What was measured.**
- Every consumer of the verdict was read for a stored copy. All six (`WordFrequencyService.topTerms`, `WordCloudView.load`, `WordCloudExport.collectionCloudImage`, `SemanticSharedTerms.sharedTerms`, both hosts' `rebuildCollocation`, `SearchService.collocation`) await `verdictWhenReady()` per operation. One cache did not follow: `WordFrequencyService`'s in-memory cache served any entry, on a comment saying the process's verdict could not change.
- Every tokenizer is reached from a view, an export or a search. So the one way a tagging surface could run in a background launch is a view the system runs there without the reader — a scene restored in a background launch, whose `.task` reaches `verdictWhenReady()` — and whether iOS 27 does that was not measured. Review round 1 closed the path instead of measuring it (below).
- A release-build log line from a real process, on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.5), launched, sent to the background and brought back: `warm-up started; trigger=firstForeground app=active age=1.222s`, then the verdict (`canary lemmas=false classes=false names=false`; the iOS 26 simulators tag nothing), then on the return `re-check trigger=recheck … kept the earlier verdict`, all at the default level, so kept in the unified log.
- On the iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) simulator (iOS 27.0) the test host's verdict line read `trigger=firstForeground app=active age=10.491s took=0.191s listed=[Language,Lemma,Script,TokenType] assets LexicalClass=available@0.023s NameType=available@0.014s Lemma=available@0.016s; canary lemmas=true classes=true names=true`.

**What changed.**
- **The verdict is replaceable (B).** `NaturalLanguageReadinessEngine` (in `WordCloudKit/NaturalLanguageReadiness.swift`) holds the verdict behind a lock, with the framework behind injectable seams; `NaturalLanguageReadiness` is a facade over one built from the live calls. When the app becomes active and the verdict lacks a capability, the engine lists the schemes, asks again for the assets of the schemes the verdict lacks, and runs the canary with fresh taggers over every scheme whose request is not in flight — if those include one it lacks — adopting the result only if it keeps every capability the old one had and adds one (`NaturalLanguageHealth.improves(on:)`). A request that answers after the engine stopped waiting for it starts the same check (`NaturalLanguageWarmUp.Trigger.lateAnswer`). A fully working verdict is never re-checked. (As first built a re-check asked for all three schemes again and ran the canary only if all three answered; review round 1 made both changes.) `revision` counts replacements; `status` says where the gate is; `verdictDidChangeNotification` announces each change.
- **No warm-up in a background launch (C).** The iOS init now installs `LanguageAnalysisLifecycle` (appended to `FRUSExplorerApp.swift`) as its first statement, and the first `UIApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification` starts the warm-up. Installing on iOS first calls `NaturalLanguageReadiness.deferWarmUpToFirstForeground()`, so a tagger or the verdict asked for before then — a restored scene in a background launch — waits for that foreground instead of starting the warm-up, and the release log says one did (`Event.deferred`); that half came in review round 1, before which a first use started the warm-up whatever the lifecycle. The Mac init still starts it at launch, then installs the lifecycle for the re-check, and is the app's one `beginWarmUp()` call.
- **A request in flight (C).** No tagger is built with a scheme whose asset request is in flight, from the request until any request for that scheme answers (review round 2 named the two narrow cases that rule leaves out, below). Each scheme has its own 30 s budget (worst case three, where it was one shared). A budget that runs out after the app entered the background keeps the whole verdict pending and runs no canary; the engine waits for the answer or the next activation, and asks again with a fresh budget (`AssetRequest.reasked`). A budget that runs out with the app in the foreground throughout **withholds that scheme**: the canary tags only the schemes whose requests answered, the verdict settles for those with the withheld one read as not working (`NaturalLanguageWarmUp.withheld`), `tagger(tagSchemes:)` leaves it out of every tagger it builds until a request for it answers — a word walk that asked for `.lemma` then walks by `.tokenType` and counts printed forms (`NaturalLanguageReadiness.wordWalkScheme(of:)`, read by both tokenizers) — and its answer, if it comes, starts a check. As first built, a foreground timeout was recorded `timedOut` and the canary then ran over every scheme, the lemma scheme with its request still in flight; the lane took that against the lane text's wording, so that classes and names would not be held back and nothing would hang. Review round 1 replaced it with the per-scheme rule, which keeps both of those and builds no tagger with a scheme while its own request is in flight. The rule is per scheme: whether tagging lexical classes while the lemma request is in flight harms the lemmatiser was not measured; the measured loss was a lemma walk made while the lemma request was in flight.
- **The release log (A).** Every start, first use deferred to the first foreground, pending request, verdict and re-check is written at the default level to subsystem `bottsywattsy.FRUS-Explorer`, category `NaturalLanguageReadiness`: trigger, where the app was, process age, schemes listed, each request's answer, seconds and re-asks, the schemes withheld, and the canary's three flags. A `pending` line is written only while the app is in the background; one that left and came back before the deadline is asked again without one (review round 1). Enums, scheme names, counts and seconds only (`NaturalLanguageReadiness.logLine(for:)`).
- **The Settings row (A).** Data & Recovery ▸ Diagnostics shows **Language Analysis** — *Checking*, *Working*, or *Limited* naming what is not working and saying the app checks again — one shared view, so iPhone, iPad and Mac show it (`LanguageAnalysisRow`, `LanguageAnalysisSummary` in `DataRecoveryView.swift`), read from `LanguageAnalysisMonitor`, an `@Observable` the lifecycle refreshes on the main actor.
- **The refusals now say what happens.** Collocates, Distinctive and the two unavailable-lens messages said only "Quitting and reopening FRUS Explorer may restore it." They now say the app checks again each time you come back to it and that the panel or cloud updates if it recovers, with quitting and reopening as the fallback. That promise is kept by keying Collocates' rebuild on both platforms (`CollocationRebuildKey.language`), the Word Cloud's load (`TaskKey.language`) and, since review round 1, each comparison column's load (`WordCloudComparisonView`'s `TaskKey.language`) on the monitor's `revision`, and by the memory cache's new rule: a count not made as designed is reused only under the verdict it was counted under (`WordFrequencyService.isReusableInMemory`).
- **Docs.** EditableContent: the four refusal blocks amended with #1539 notes, ten new ranged blocks for the row, 30 ranges re-pointed, the 09 header and README row 182 → 192 blocks, one Amendment-Log bullet. Six manual proposals in `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md` under "LANG — #1539". The printed-form fallback (D) was not built; it stays the optional tail item.

**How it was verified** (round 0's figures; review round 1 reworked the engine tests and re-ran everything, below).
- **A/B, engine** (`swift test` on the macOS host, by re-editing `NaturalLanguageReadiness.swift` and restoring it, diffed identical to a snapshot). The 13 new engine tests passed on the fixed engine ("✔ Test run with 23 tests in 2 suites passed after 3.617 seconds", with #1373's ten). Round A put back the unfixed semantics behind the new API (one shared deadline, a budget that never pends, no re-check): "✘ Test run with 23 tests in 2 suites failed after 10.645 seconds with 20 issues", seven tests. Round A′+B (the first foreground starting nothing new, re-checking a working verdict, a re-check that tags with a request in flight and adopts any change, a log without `reasked`, `improves` without its lemma clause): "✘ Test run with 23 tests in 2 suites failed after 5.022 seconds with 15 issues", six tests. Round C (`improves` without its other three clauses): "✘ Test run with 1 test in 1 suite failed after 0.001 seconds with 3 issues". The two controls, the foreground timeout and the first-use start, pass in every round by design.
- **A/B, app** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A36F4C02`, by re-editing seven app files and restoring them, each diffed identical). Round 1, the unfixed behaviour behind the new API: "✘ Test run with 39 tests in 10 suites failed after 1.069 seconds with 27 issues", every new app test. Rounds 2 and 3 each kept one clause of the memory rule: "✘ Test run with 7 tests in 1 suite failed after 0.094 seconds with 1 issue" and "… after 0.108 seconds with 1 issue". The same-verdict clause is isolated only where the verdict lacks lemmas, as it does on iOS 26.5; on a working host that test is a control.
- **The lane's suites with the EditableContent and coding-standards audits** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5): "✔ Test run with 113 tests in 12 suites passed after 41.327 seconds". On the iPad Pro 11-inch (M5), iOS 27.0, `27A97343`: "✔ Test run with 29 tests in 8 suites passed after 1.240 seconds", `WordCloudLensTests` among them.
- **The full unit target** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5): "✔ Test run with 6000 tests in 716 suites passed after 286.836 seconds", "** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **".
- **SPM:** `WordCloudKitTests` "✔ Test run with 31 tests in 3 suites passed", `SemanticVectorsGeneratorTests` 65 in 10, `CloudVectorsGeneratorTests` 31 in 3, all passed.
- `build-for-testing` printed no warning beyond the known `GeneratedSummary` and AppIntents residues.

**Still open.**
- The owner's devices: whether a late answer or a re-check restores a lemmatiser on hardware, and how often the verdict fails at all on a foreground launch. The release log answers both; the optional step D waits on it. On the iOS 27.0 iPad simulator neither restored one: review round 1 measured that a lost lemma request never answers in that process (below).
- The Settings row was not checked by eye on any device or simulator.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s `WordCloudLensTests` paragraph, which still said the warm-up started at launch in both inits and named a renamed test, was corrected in review round 1.

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

The review's verified findings, each resolved in code, tests or docs; nothing is handed back to the owner except the per-scheme reading of step C noted under the first.

- **Step C held back no tagging after a foreground timeout** (the review's lead finding, raised twice). As first built, a lemma request still unanswered after its 30 s in the foreground was recorded `timedOut` and the canary then tagged every scheme, the lemma scheme with its request in flight — the order the type's own docs say was measured to lose lemmas — and the lane argued for that against the plan's "no tagging while a request is in flight". The engine now withholds such a scheme instead (`NaturalLanguageWarmUp.withheld`): the canary tags only the schemes whose requests answered (`runCanary(tagging:)`), `tagger(tagSchemes:)` leaves the scheme out of every tagger until a request for it answers (`NaturalLanguageReadinessEngine.taggingSchemes(for:)`, with `.tokenType` in its place so both tokenizers still find every word through `wordWalkScheme(of:)`), and its late answer starts a check (`Trigger.lateAnswer`). Classes and names still settle at once, and nothing waits on a spinner, which were the lane's reasons. **This is the review's suggested middle course, a per-scheme reading of the plan's sentence**: lexical classes and names are tagged while the lemma request is in flight, which no measurement says is safe or unsafe; the owner may want to confirm that reading on the PR.
- **A first use in a background launch could still start the warm-up.** `LanguageAnalysisLifecycle.install()` now first calls `NaturalLanguageReadiness.deferWarmUpToFirstForeground()` on iPhone and iPad, so a tagger or the verdict asked for before the first foreground — a scene restored in a background launch — waits for that foreground rather than starting the warm-up, and the release log says so once (`Event.deferred`). This is stricter than the review's suggestion to seed the lifecycle from `UIApplication.shared.applicationState`, and does not depend on what that property reads in an `App.init`, which was not measured.
- **The control the lane did not run, on the simulator.** On the iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) simulator, iOS 27.0 (`27A97343`), the app was launched about 10 s after a fresh boot (`simctl boot` without waiting for `bootstatus`), left 45 s, sent to the background by opening Settings, brought back and left 45 s, and its `NaturalLanguageReadiness` log read with `log show`. **Round 0's code, 6 cycles:** the lemma request went unanswered in all 6 (`LexicalClass=available@11.3–11.8s NameType=available Lemma=timedOut@30.0s; canary lemmas=false classes=true names=true`), and each re-check on the return asked all three again and got no lemma answer in 30 s (`canary not run, a request is unanswered; kept the earlier verdict`). **Round 1's code, 4 cycles,** each then quit and relaunched without a reboot: the same loss in all 4, now `withheld=[Lemma]`; the re-check asked only for `Lemma` and got no answer (`canary not run, every missing scheme's request is unanswered`); in the one process kept alive four minutes after its re-check no late answer came; and every relaunch got all three at once (`Lemma=available@0.011–0.019s; canary lemmas=true classes=true names=true`). A launch 17–21 s after the boot (with an install between) lost nothing, in both builds (1 each). So on the simulator the loss is a lemma request that never answers in that process, and nothing within it — round 0's re-check or round 1's — restores the lemmatiser; a new process does, as the owner's force-quit did on the devices. Whether a device's late answer or re-check does is what the release log will show.
- **`CLAUDE.md` named a renamed test and the old launch rule.** Its `WordCloudLensTests` paragraph now says the Mac starts the warm-up at launch and iPhone and iPad on the first foreground, names `initsInstallTheLifecycleBeforeAnythingCanTag` and `onlyTheMacInitStartsTheWarmUp`, and says what a launch that loses the lemma request prints (`withheld=[Lemma]`).
- **No test covered the live notification.** `liveStatusChangePostsTheNotification` calls `Dependencies.live.statusDidChange()` and requires the notification on `NotificationCenter.default` under `verdictDidChangeNotification`, counting only deliveries on its own thread so the process's real engine cannot pass it.
- **The step C guard read only the iOS init.** `onlyTheMacInitStartsTheWarmUp` scans every file the app compiles and requires exactly one `beginWarmUp()` call, in the macOS init; `initsInstallTheLifecycleBeforeAnythingCanTag` (renamed from `lifecycleIsInstalledFirstInBothInits`, whose name and title claimed an order the Mac's init does not have) again requires exactly one init per platform; and on iOS `NaturalLanguageReadinessWarmUpTests` requires the host's warm-up not to have started from `launch` or `firstUse`.
- **Docs that claimed the wrong thing.** `LanguageAnalysisLifecycle`'s doc said it was installed first in both inits; it now gives each init's order. `LanguageAnalysisSummary`'s doc said "parts of speech" was the refusals' own wording; it now says only "dictionary forms" and "names" are, and why the third is not. The `menu.find.search` and `menu.find.search.mac` blocks' `ships at:` fields now name their keys' lines. (They were not the only ones the lane left stale: review round 2 found and fixed a third, `wordcloud.scope.corpus`.)
- **Nits taken.** The Word Cloud's comparison columns key their load on the revision (`WordCloudComparisonView`'s `TaskKey.language`, a fourth row in `LanguageAnalysisWiringTests.rebuildSites`), so a column's "Counted as printed" note goes when a check adopts lemmas, and the two manual proposals that promise it now name the column. The `pending` log line is written only while the app is in the background (`aReturnBeforeTheDeadlineIsNotPending`). A re-check asks again only for the schemes the verdict lacks, so no working scheme is ever in flight while other surfaces tag. The engine tests give every budget a second or more of slack, act between a request and its deadline in one test only (with 3 s for it), and wait on the event they assert rather than on `revision`. The "sticky within a process" title is now a control's, and the suite's doc and version history describe #1539. **None was left.**

**How it was verified.**
- **A/B, engine** (`swift test` on the macOS host, by re-editing `NaturalLanguageReadiness.swift` and restoring it from a snapshot, `cmp` identical after each round). Round A put round 0's behaviour back behind the new API (every scheme tagged and handed out after a foreground timeout, no late-answer check, a word walk that always goes by `.lemma`, no deferral, a re-check that asks for all three and the round-0 guard, `pending` logged whenever the app went away, the log without `withheld`, `works(_:)` always true, an empty `.live` `statusDidChange`): "✘ Test run with 39 tests in 3 suites failed after 10.363 seconds with 40 issues", the 12 new or changed tests each among the failures. Round B put back the pre-#1539 timing (one shared deadline, a budget that never pends): "✘ Test run with 39 tests in 3 suites failed after 11.039 seconds with 13 issues", the four timing tests round 1 widened among them. Fixed: "✔ Test run with 39 tests in 3 suites passed after 6.110 seconds".
- **A/B, app** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A36F4C02`, by re-editing `FRUSExplorerApp.swift` and `WordCloudComparisonView.swift` and restoring both, `cmp` identical). ### Review fixes, round 2 (2026-10-01)

The read-only check found one blocking problem, a stale `ships at:` field, and four nits. All five are resolved; nothing is handed back to the owner.

- **A third stale `ships at:` field (blocking).** `wordcloud.scope.corpus` in `Docs/EditableContent/09-Settings-and-App.md` named `WordCloudView.swift:2365` and `:2506`, two lines above where the key now sits, because round 0 added two lines to `WordCloudView.swift` above both. It now names `:2367` and `:2508`. The block has no `lines:` range, so `EditableContentKeyTests` does not check it, and round 1 had fixed only the two fields the review named. A scan of every `ships at:` entry in `Docs/EditableContent/` against the source now finds no other that misses its key.
- **Two manual proposals pointed at the wrong line.** `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md`'s Mac and iPhone/iPad Word Cloud proposals named `NaturalLanguageReadiness.swift:1041` for `NaturalLanguageReadinessEngine.applicationDidBecomeActive()`, which is the doc comment of `deferWarmUpToFirstForeground()`. They now name the method's own line, `:1058` after this round's edits.
- **`CLAUDE.md` overstated two things.** The `WordCloudLensTests` paragraph said the printed line "ends" `withheld=[Lemma]`; the verdict line goes on to the canary's three flags, so it now says "contains". And it said a lemma request that does not answer within 30 s withholds the scheme; that holds only in the foreground, so it now says so and that a trip to the background keeps the whole verdict pending instead.
- **"No scheme is tagged while a request for its assets is in flight" was slightly absolute.** It is a rule about building a tagger: taggers are built per text, so a tokenizer whose tagger was built just before a re-check asks again for a scheme keeps that scheme for the rest of its text; and when the warm-up's late request and a re-check's are out for one scheme at once, the first answer takes the scheme out of flight while the other is still out. Both cases concern a scheme the verdict already reads as not working. The type's "A request still in flight" section now states the rule as "no tagger is built with a scheme whose asset request is in flight" and names the two cases; the `timedOut` case, the "Every `NLTagger`" section, the re-check bullet, the `inFlight` field's doc and this entry's "A request in flight (C)" paragraph say the same. No code changed for this one.
- **A timeout could be recorded for a request that had answered.** `answered` took the scheme out of flight under the engine's lock and the request's completion delivered the answer to its waiter's box after the lock, so a waiter whose deadline fell between the two found the scheme out of flight and its box empty and recorded `timedOut`. Only the record was wrong: the canary still tagged the scheme, which was no longer in flight. `answered(_:_:into:seconds:)` now delivers to the box under the same hold of the lock that takes the scheme out of flight, so such a waiter finds one or the other. It finds neither only when another request for the scheme answered first, and then its own request really is unanswered; the comment at the timeout path, which said an answer that arrived meanwhile "is read here rather than lost", now says that. The window lay between two statements on the answering thread with no seam, so no runtime test reaches it; `NaturalLanguageReadinessScanTests.anAnswerLeavesFlightAndReachesItsWaiterTogether` pins the delivery where it is written, as `taggerReadsTheVerdictBeforeItBuilds` pins the gate: the engine's one `.deliver(` must be inside the `state.withLock` closure of `answered`, beside the removal from `inFlight`. The engine's version history is at 1.2 and the type's at 1.4.

**How it was verified.**

On the fixed source: "✔ Test run with 6 tests in 1 suite passed after 1.738 seconds". With round 1's order put back in `NaturalLanguageReadiness.swift` (`box.deliver(answer)` after `answered` in `ask`'s completion, and not in `answered`): "✘ Test … recorded an issue at WordCloudTests.swift:1286:9: Expectation failed: held.contains(\".deliver(\")", then "✘ Test run with 6 tests in 1 suite failed after 1.733 seconds with 1 issue". The file was then restored from a snapshot, `cmp` identical.
