## Session 2026-10-01 — Graph labels hold still while the layout settles, a drag on empty canvas pans, a long-pressed node or word opens its menu beside it, and the iOS node menu says what it opens (lane GRAPH; #1434, #1517, #1518, #1481)

**The question.** Four graph defects, one lane: partner labels flickered while the co-mention and volume layouts animated (#1434); a drag or double-click on empty canvas started nothing in the graphs (#1517, the owner's D8: a click there still clears nothing); four context menus were written after `.position`, so iOS anchored them to the whole canvas (#1518); and on iOS the node menu's *Open in Main Window* pushed the document inside the graph (#1481, D9: the text must describe the control).

**What was measured** (before any change, `v2` @ `284f52c8`, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator `9AB3A0C9`, iOS 27.0, with `frus1964-68v01` and `v02` copied into the container and indexed).
- A drag across empty canvas moved neither the document graph (in its own window) nor the volume graph (in its sheet). A drag that began on a node panned both.
- A long press on a document-graph node dimmed the whole canvas and opened the menu at the canvas's top-left corner. On an archival-network node it opened at the top-right corner. On a word-cloud word it lifted the word drawn about 120 pt to the left of where it sat.
- In the archival network, a drag outside the outer ring did nothing.
- The screenshots are kept in the session's durable folder, `durable/w49/work/GRAPH/shots/`.

**What changed.**
1. **#1434, settle-only placement.** `GraphNodeLabels.place(_:settling:)` places only the first label (the centre's, whose node is pinned) while `settling` is set. Both view models gain `isLayoutSettling`: set when `rerunLayout` starts an animated layout, cleared in the same main-actor change that publishes its last pass (`layoutSteps`, 15), and false for a layout settled at once (Reduce Motion, or three nodes or fewer). The canvases read the flag in body, where Observation registers it, and hand it to the placement. Hysteresis was not chosen: the next lane, ARCH (#1438), adds a second slot to the same function, and a carried-over slot would have to survive it.
2. **#1517, a hit-testable empty canvas.** `GraphEmptyCanvas` (a clear, shaped view with no gesture) is laid as a `.background` after the pan offset and before the gestures in the document graph, the co-mention network and the archival network, on both platforms. The volume graph's #1471 canvas now uses it on iOS too, keeping its Mac-only clearing click. A click or tap on it clears nothing (D8).
3. **#1518.** The context menu comes before `.position` at all four sites. A word-cloud word also writes its menu after its rotation, with a `preview:` that draws the word level (`cloudWord(_:)`). Both orders were measured. With the menu before the rotation, a long press away from a vertical word's centre found nothing. With it after the rotation and no preview, iOS lifted the vertical word cut to its unrotated box.
4. **#1481.** The node menu's open item is `openDocumentActionName`. The Mac keeps `graph.contextMenu.openDocument`, "Open in Main Window". iOS has the new `graph.contextMenu.openDocument.ios`, "View Document", the node panel's own words for the same push. WB's owner-confirmed touch help ("…or open it…") stays true and is unchanged. *(Corrected in review round 1:)* round 0 relabelled the node menu only; the reference list's row menu, which calls the same `openDocument`, still declared the Mac key unconditionally and read "Open in Main Window" on iPhone and iPad until round 1 gave it `openDocumentActionName` too.

## Session 2026-10-01 — In the Archival network a partner never reads like the focus or like another partner, the custodian names sit in their quadrants' corners clear of every node, labels keep off the captions and the Central Files outline and fall back to a place above their node, and a long collection is named by its printed title with its panel buttons in view (lane ARCH; #1437, #1438, #1468, #1470)

**The question.** Lane ARCH of the 2026-09-28 plan of record, after GRAPH (which is not yet on `v2`; both lanes edit `GraphNodeLabels.place`). #1437: in Archival Analytics ▸ Network a partner could draw exactly like the focus — a same-named record held elsewhere, which `disambiguate` never compared with the focus, or two names the 26-character cut from the end made alike, most at a lot number. #1438: few labels fit on a small canvas (owner decision D10: a fallback place above the node), and nothing kept a label off the custodian captions or the Central Files box ("JCS Records" ran into "OTHER INSTITUTIONS"). #1470: the captions were drawn first, at 45° and 0.93 × the outer radius, under the discs, class squares and box drawn after them (D12: reserve their space in the layout). #1468: selecting Indexed Central Files drew its 2,150-character front-matter paragraph as the panel's bold heading, with the buttons below the 168 pt dock (D11: a display-name rule for names over 100 characters with a printed `<hi>` title, the full text exempt from the 12-alias cap, and the layout fix).

**What was measured, and how.**
- **#1437, over the 200 most widely cited foci × both measures at the default threshold, collapsed** — the population #1437 was measured over. A macOS probe compiled from the worktree's own `ArchivalNetworkData.swift`, `GraphNodeLabels` and SourceNoteKit, over the bundled authority and usage index (`/Users/jbotts/Library/Caches/frus-lanes/w49/ARCH/probe`, scratch). On `v2` f5625ca2's code: 377 graphs with a node; a node drew exactly like the focus in **40** (17 a same-named record, 23 a cut) and two nodes alike in **74**. On the lane's: **0 and 0**, and `ArchivalNetworkLabelTests.noNodeDrawsLikeTheFocusOrAnother` holds the same sweep on the device.
- **#1470, why the issue's arc split cannot reserve the caption.** The captions measure 78–119 pt wide at 9 pt semibold on the Mac (`STATE LOT FILES` to `PRESIDENTIAL LIBRARIES`); at 390 × 300 a wedge's outer radius is 106 pt, and the 119 pt caption on its diagonal comes within the 3 pt clearance of a node of the default threshold's weakest strength anywhere from 32° into the wedge to its far edge at 82° (computed from the layout's constants), so a gap around the diagonal would leave the nodes 24° of the wedge's 74°. The captions therefore move outside the node band, into their quadrants' corners.
- **#1468, the data rule on the real generator.** The unchanged generator, built from `git archive origin/v2`, reproduces all four committed artifacts and the report byte for byte on corpus `8e5da08c1` (XML identical to NOTE's `550a8c5c5`). With the rule: **10 names change** (11 in the 2026-09-28 research, on the pre-NOTE authority, which also counted 46 if every item opening with a `<hi>` were named by it), every id stays, top-level names over 100 characters fall **280 → 271**, over 1,000 **2 → 0** (the longest left, 818, prints no title), and names of 80 characters or fewer are 3,635 of 4,051. Nine of the ten had names over 100 characters; the tenth, Subject-Numeric Central Files, had a 96-character one, which its longer items now outvote with their printed title, since the rule is per item and a name is its items' vote. Four titles are another record's name or alias: `Agency for International Development` and `Subject-Numeric Indexed Central Files` a name, `FOIA Electronic Reading Room` (the CIA's record) and `DEF 18–3 SWITZ (GE)` (the Department of State's) an alias. A first version exempted every titled item's paragraph and gave Indexed Central Files 18 aliases; a second exempted the most-voted paragraph by item and kept the wrong one, because the name vote also counts each sub-series reference. The shipped rule exempts the record's former name, the same front-matter vote cast with each titled item's whole text: Indexed Central Files keeps its 2,150-character paragraph as its one alias past the cap (12 → 13), and no other record exceeds 12.
- **The app's match window.** `IndexingPipeline.collectionMatchClause` folds a record's first 13 name forms into the local-count and Neighbors query. Over the new artifact against the old, it changes for 7 records: six gain titles as forms — among them the repository-less `DEF 18–3 SWITZ (GE)` and `DEF 18–3 USSR (MO)` records, whose new forms no repository or record group narrows — and Indexed Central Files swaps its 2,150-character paragraph, which no source note's series begins with, for the 1955 paragraph: its name and 13 aliases are 14 forms, and the paragraph, alphabetically last, falls outside the 13. `collectionMatchFormCap` is unchanged, and its doc comment now says the one record exceeds it.

**What changed.**
- **#1437** (`ArchivalNetworkData.swift`). `disambiguate(_:in:focus:)` seeds the repeated names with the focus's, so a node that carries it is qualified by its repository, or by its id; `focusLabel(_:nodes:)` qualifies the focus by its own repository when a node shares its name ("Whitman File · Eisenhower Library" beside the repository-less "Whitman File"). `identifierKeepingCut(_:limit:)` keeps a trailing lot, FRC or file number whole ("Conference F… Lot 64 D 559"), drawing the identifier alone ("…FRC 66 A 3542") in a qualified label's fifteen-character name half. `drawnLabels(in:)` re-cuts any node whose label still reads like the focus's or another node's to show the end of its name ("National Securi… (H-Files)"), never the focus's. The panel sentence, the export title and its provenance name the focus by its label.
- **#1438** (`GraphNodeLabels`, shared). `place(_:avoiding:)` tries each partner label under its node, then above it (`labelRectAbove(for:)`, D10), and keeps it clear of every obstacle. The place above is the shared rule, since D10 "also answers the older decision" #1384 measured on the person and volume graphs. The archival canvas passes its four captions, the box's caption and the box's border as four 1 pt rects (`labelObstacles(_:)`), so a class label sits inside the box or outside it, never across its line.
- **#1470** (`ArchivalNetworkData.layout`). The layout reserves each caption (`ArchivalNetworkLayout.captions`, `hullCaption`): on the ray from the centre toward its quadrant's canvas corner, at the first point whose rect, kept inside the canvas, clears the farthest a node can reach (`nodeReach(outerRadius:)`: outer + 21.06, the corner of a selected class square of no strength on the outer ring, from the drawing constants the canvas draws with; a disc reaches 16.75), the class box and its caption, and the captions before it; else the point that comes closest. The box's caption stays centred 8 pt above the box and slides sideways only to clear a custodian's. The captions stay on the bottom layer, are drawn in `captionFont` and measured in the same 9 pt semibold system font (`captionPointSize`), and a tap on one selects its wedge.
- **#1468, data** (`CollectionAuthorityGeneratorCore`). `ReferenceBuilder.printedTitle(of:)` names a textual item over 100 characters, whose text opens with a `<hi>` and goes on after it, by that title; a lot item keeps its text, so its name keeps its lot number. ### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

Five confirmed findings — two of them the same missed import path — and eight nits, all taken. The paragraphs above are corrected in place where they had become untrue (the 240 rule, the import paths, #1464's reach, the plate).

**What changed.**
- **The third import path indexes too.** `FRUSExplorerApp.importOpenedCollection` — a `.fruscollection` opened from Files, Mail, AirDrop or a Finder double-click, the way a shared file most often arrives — saved and never called `indexImportedNotes`, so its notes waited for the next launch, and the doc comments, this entry and two manual proposals said "both import paths". It now indexes after its save. `ImportedNoteIndexTests.everyImportPathIndexes` replaces `bothImportPathsIndex`: it finds every function in the app that calls `NativeCollectionSerializer.apply(` or `.importCollection(from:` instead of naming two files, and requires a save and then the index call in each.
- **What a file name's limit counts, measured.** On APFS (the build Mac's temporary directory, where the iOS simulator writes too) a name may take 255 UTF-16 units of its decomposed form, not 255 bytes: 255 `a` and 251 `外` with `.pdf` (757 bytes) are written, one more of either fails with errno 63; 118 `ǖ` (U+01D6) with `.pdf` is 240 bytes as typed, so the old cap let it through, but 358 units decomposed, and the write failed. A file URL also hands its last component back decomposed (`appendingPathComponent` returned three `ǖ` and `.pdf` as 19 bytes, not 10). `ExportFileName.length(of:)` now counts the UTF-8 bytes of the decomposed form: never less than the units APFS counts, the same for every normalization of a name, and what a byte-limited file system would receive (reasoned, not measured). `maxBytes` is `maxLength`. The fixtures that could not reproduce #1498 — `外` ×120 and the flag ×40, 124 and 164 units with `.pdf` — are now ×260 and ×70, and `ǖ` ×118 joins them as the fixture that tells a typed-byte budget from the file system's. The naming tests assert `length(of:) <= maxLength` (240), not 255, so the suffix and the extension the cut reserves are pinned.
- **The Archives Visit packet's PDF name** is cut through `ExportFileName` (`TripPacketPDFRenderer.fileName(title:)`); a long project name made `render` return `nil` and the Share PDF control vanish.
- **#1464's reach.** The word cloud's Collection scope and Compare ▸ Collection menus printed their own "Untitled", tested untrimmed (one key, `wordcloud.compare.untitled`, is gone); they, the unpresented `GlobalContextView`'s row, and the Archives Visit picker's "from the collection" line (three call sites, which also name the plan after the trimmed name) now go through `listName`. `CollectionEditorNaming.listOrder` and `sortedByListName` order the lists that print `listName` by it: the Research sidebar's By Collection, its rows' collection chips, the change review's quotations, Project Home's Manage sheet, both word-cloud menus and the rail.
- **PV-1 and the embedded cloud.** `CollectionColophon.sourceLines(for:embedsWordCloud:)` adds `.appWordLists` when the export drew the collection's word cloud; each of the three renderers passes whether it holds the image.
- **Docs.** The manual proposals: an untitled heading leaves "every PDF, HTML and Word export" (a `.fruscollection` keeps it); the method appendix's formats "say", not "close on", what the counts were drawn from; the Importing entries cite the third path; the #1498 entry states the measure. The plate's doc comments name HTML and word the dark-appearance premise as a risk the pin removes, since the test injects a dark environment and nothing measured the exporter's default. `CollectionListNameTests`' doc no longer says Project Home spelled "Untitled collection" at this lane's base (lane WB had capitalized it). ## Session 2026-10-01 — The Mac Collections window caps a long name in its picker, rests the popover's Note like the Introduction, keeps a selected row's chips legible, and edits only the field you change; an unnumbered document reads "Unnumbered (d710a-1)"; Mac List footers wrap; Section defaults saves each edit (lane MACCOL; #1446, #1448, #1449, #1477, #1493, #1475, two fold-ins)

**The question.** Six Mac Collections polish issues and two fold-ins from the plan of record's §2 row: the toolbar picker's unbounded name (#1446); the resting cap after a formatting change and beside a legacy scroller (#1448); the popover's Note, a fixed-height `TextEditor` beside a capped Introduction (#1449); a stale caret in a block that lost focus, and accent-on-accent chips on a selected row (#1477); an unnumbered document's id printed as its number (#1493, decision D5: "Unnumbered (d710a-1)"); List footers cut to one line on the Mac (#1475); the detail pane's `saveMetadata()`, which wrote all seven fields from stale copies on every edit (#1413's shape); and whether Section defaults saves each write.

**What was measured.**
- **#1475, the footer idiom, in an offscreen harness** (`work/MACCOL/harness/footer.swift` in the session's durable folder; a `List` of the sheets' shape hosted at 420 pt, macOS 27, rendered to PNG). The bare footer, the footer with `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` (#600's failed first attempt) and the footer with #1096's per-text `fixedSize` and full-width frame each laid out **14 pt** tall — one line, cut with an ellipsis, as the issue saw. With `.lineLimit(nil)` added the text grew (56 pt for the Topic sheet's three sentences) but the footer's row did not, so the render showed its middle two lines. The text as a row of its own section (#600's idiom) wrapped: **39 pt** and **26 pt** for the two footers. So in the harness #1096's idiom does not wrap a `List` footer and #600's does; the two sites that carry #1096's (`ArchiveVisitEditorView.swift:1245`, `ArchiveVisitListView.swift:91`) were left as they were, and review round 1 converted them with the rest (below).
- **#1448, in a Mac harness that compiles the real `CollectionRichTextEditor.swift`** (`work/MACCOL/harness/editor/main.swift`; a resting `.proseBlock` block whose first paragraph wraps to four lines plain and five bold, and an edited block beside a legacy scroller). On `v2`: after bolding the resting block's first paragraph through the formatting bar's own `shouldChangeText`/`didChangeText` bracket, the block drew **6** lines where a fresh count gave **5**; the edited block beside a **17 pt** legacy scroller was sized **60 pt** while its text needed **76 pt**. With the fix: 5 and 5; 76 and 76. (The harness sets the scroll view's style to legacy itself; this Mac's preferred style is overlay, where the scroller takes no width and both versions measure alike.)
- **#1477's caret could not be reproduced.** The harness app, launched from a shell, never becomes active (an accessory or regular app both stay inactive, even off screen and borderless), and an inactive app draws no insertion point — no `NSTextInsertionIndicator` existed in either block. The fix is the issue's reading; the check stays by eye.
- **#1477's prompt colour**: a probe confirmed a `TextField`'s `prompt:` `Text` keeps its `foregroundStyle` on macOS 27, so the heading's prompt can be recoloured. **The prominence the fix switches on was not observed**: the probe (`harness/prompt.swift`) hosted a `List(selection:)` with its first row selected, but its app was inactive, so the selection drew an unemphasized grey and a `backgroundProminence` reader printed and drew "standard" on the selected row too. Apple documents a selected list row as `.increased`; whether SwiftUI delivers it to these rows, and so whether the chips turn white, rests on owner check 4.

**What changed.**
- **#1446** — the picker's name keeps to one line, cut at the tail within `MacCollectionManagerView.collectionNameMaxWidth` (260 pt, the Archives picker's measured cap), and its counts — label, menu rows, and Manage Collections' rows — print `.formatted()`.
- **#1449** — `RichTextEditor` gains `plainText`: no formatting bar (the Mac's, iOS's keyboard bar), a text view that takes no formatting, and on the Mac a view the formatting controller never holds, so the shared colour panel cannot colour it. The popover's Note is that editor capped `.noteInPopover` (six lines at rest, 60–140 pt editing, the old frame's bounds), committing its plain text. No stored property was added: `Collection.note` stays a `String?`.
- **#1448** — a change to a block at rest schedules the same deferred recount a width change does (`scheduleRecount(in:)`); a capped block is measured at the width its text wraps at (`RichTextRestingLayout.textWidth(of:frameWidth:)`, the scroll view's `contentSize(forFrameSize:…)` with its own scroller and style; `scrollView.contentSize.width` on a text change).
- **#1477** — a block that loses focus rests on the next main-actor turn, and not if focus came back (`scheduleRest(in:)`), instead of editing its storage inside `resignFirstResponder`. `ConfigurePill`, `EntryStatusChip` and the heading field's prompt read `backgroundProminence` and draw through `CollectionChipStyle`: white on a white tint, and a lighter white prompt, at `.increased`; the theme's colours and the field's own placeholder colour otherwise.
- **#1493** — `CitableDocumentNumber.unnumberedLabel` gives "Unnumbered (d710a-1)", or "Unnumbered (d710a-1, frus1945Berlinv02)" across volumes (the volume after the id, as a numbered token's follows its number). The Mac row's label and every generated block's list use it for a document whose stored `@n` is the editors' bracketed description. A Persons list keeps "Document(s)" when it names at least one number and drops it when it names only unnumbered documents. A document with no stored number and an id that is not one (`eta_d1` unindexed) keeps its id: nothing the device has read says the volume prints no number, and the lane does not infer it from the id's shape. So **#1493's defect remains for a Potsdam document whose volume is not indexed on the device**: the Mac row reads "d710a-1", and a block that still lists it — a Thematic Index built from the reader's own tags, say — reads "Document d710a-1", because with no stored number `referenceToken` takes the id as the number. Review round 1 drew the Mac section only when the footer draws something and converted the other 39 `List` footers the Mac reaches, with a tree-wide gate (below).
- **Fold-in: the detail pane.** `saveMetadata()` and its seven `onChange` handlers are gone. Each popover control binds `committing($field) { CollectionEditorCommit… }`, writing only its own field and saving when it wrote; the Note commits through `commitNote`; and the pane applies the iOS editor's `FrontMatterModelSync` over all seven copies, so a change another writer makes is followed and never written back. The sheet's composition rows and the section's own export defaults still leave the save to autosave; the manual proposal promises nothing for them.

## Session 2026-10-01 — On iPhone and iPad the reader's colours, Excerpt, Look Up in NARA and Note open the system edit menu, which can no longer cover them; the floating selection bar stays on the Mac only (lane SEL, #1540)

**The question.** The owner's screenshot (#1540) showed the system edit menu (Copy, Look Up, Translate…) drawn over the reader's floating selection bar on iOS. The bar always anchored below the selection (`DocumentView.swift`, `below: true, gap: 22`) on Research-rail decision D3 (2026-07-18), which assumed UIKit keeps its menu above; UIKit also puts it below, and the bar flipped above near the bottom edge, onto the menu's usual spot. The app had no `buildMenu` hook, so it neither knew nor controlled where the menu went. The owner chose option (a) on 2026-09-29: put the app's actions at the start of the system edit menu, retire the iOS bar, keep the Mac's, and call "Look Up" **Look Up in NARA** everywhere.

**What was measured.**
- **The iPad half, which the triage had only inferred, reproduces.** On v2's code (iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 26.5, `9F3D84A4`), long-pressing "content" in the UI-test fixture drew the bar under the selection and, a moment later, the edit menu (Copy, Find Selection, Look Up, Translate, ›) on top of it, the bar's dots showing through the menu's glass.

Read from the menu's accessibility tree by the new UI suite on both devices.

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

The review's five verified findings and the nits taken, each resolved in code, tests or docs. Nothing is handed back to the owner; what stays open is listed at the end.

- **A selection ending at the end of a text node lost its offsets** (the review's lead finding: the defect measured above, which the plan's own "drag the lower handle" check hits). `rangeEndpointToOffset` (`frus-selection.js`, version 1.7, and its `kSelectionJS` twin, byte-identical) now maps an endpoint just past a MAPPED text node's last character to the offset after that character — the endpoint `buildRanges` in `frus-highlights.js` already gives a highlight ending there, so the reverse mapping accepts what the forward one produces. A footnote's text is not in the map, so its end still maps to −1 and a drag into a footnote stays a footnote selection. The Mac gains it too: its bar drew the colours and Excerpt dimmed for such a selection. Pinned by the new `TextNodeEndSelectionTests` (four tests, the production bridge's payload): a selection ending just before a footnote marker, one ending at a paragraph's end, one STARTING at a node's end (the next character in the flat text, the marker adding nothing), and the guard that the end of a Footnotes-list text node stays unmapped.
- **Nothing guarded the clear after a menu item.** `SelectionEditMenuItemTests.choosingAnItemClearsTheSelection` loads a page into the reader's own `_FRUSEditMenuWebView` (the test harness now builds that subclass and wires it to its coordinator, as `makeUIView` does), selects a word through the real bridge, builds the group from that report, chooses Highlight Yellow, and requires the verb performed, a clear reported by the page, the coordinator's live selection gone and `getSelection().isCollapsed`. The UI colour test's message no longer claims the clear, and the suite's oracles say why UIKit's dismissal of the menu cannot show it.
- **Excerpt and Note were reached by no test.** `SelectionEditMenuTests.testExcerptAndNoteFromTheEditMenuOpenTheirSheets` chooses Excerpt (from the row, or the list › opens) and requires "Add Excerpt to Collection", then selects again, chooses Note and requires "New Research Note".
- **"Both tests fail"** in the UI suite's doc now gives the three tests that failed before #1540 and how the fourth and the new first-page check were measured.
- **Comments that still described an iOS consumer of the bar's geometry**: `SelectionPayload.rect` and `.scale`, the coordinator's comment, the `selectionGeometry` and scroll-signal comments in both script copies, `frus-selection.js`'s header, and `ListLabelSelectionTests`' doc, which now says the Mac's bar dims the colours and the iPhone and iPad menu leaves them out.
- **Nits taken.** (1) `performSelectionVerb` drops `webKitSelectionRange` and `lastValidSelectionRange` after a verb, so the iPad's Highlight Selection (⌘⇧H) no longer stays enabled and highlights the handled passage again; the blur-surviving fallback still holds for every other clear. (2) `webViewGroupAfterAClear` holds its coordinator to the end, like its siblings. (3) `_FRUSEditMenuWebView`'s doc states the asynchronous-report race: a menu UIKit builds before the page's report arrives has no app items, or items gated on the previous selection, until it is shown again. (4) The manual proposals no longer name a device for what fits before ›: the iOS §3 step 4 and §4.3 sentences say "if it is not on the menu's first page" and "depends on the device and the text size", and the section's preamble says only two devices were measured. (5) The first-page assertion also requires the row's first item to be "Highlight Yellow", since its prefix comparison passed vacuously when the row opened with anything else. (6) `SelectionEditMenuItemTests`' doc names the three `selectionGroup()` guards it pins instead of "every guard", and says what no test reaches. (7) `CLAUDE.md` gains the suite's iPhone and iPad commands, and the suite's doc says `-only-testing …/ResearchReadingStaysInTabTests` runs none of it.
- **Docs.** Three ranged blocks on `DocumentView.swift` in `Docs/EditableContent/08-Reading-Research-Collections.md` move six lines down for the lines `performSelectionVerb` gained (one Amendment-Log bullet). The line references in the SEL manual proposals are re-pointed to the moved declarations.

**How it was verified.**

The guard was then measured against a mutant that moved any text node's end to the next mapped character (`firstOffsetAfter(node)`): it failed, "a footnote endpoint must stay unmapped: start 5, end 57".
- **A/B, the other new and changed tests**, by re-editing the fixed `DocumentView.swift`, `FRUSDocumentWebView.swift` and `FRUSWebViewConfiguration.swift` and restoring all three from a snapshot (`cmp` identical, no mutant string left). One build carried four mutants: no `clearSelection()` after a verb, no `liveSelection = nil` on a clear, an extra "Probe" item at the start of the group, and the Excerpt and Note branches swapped. Unit: `choosingAnItemClearsTheSelection` failed ("choosing Highlight Yellow reported no clear: the page kept its selection", "the page still holds a selection after Highlight Yellow") and `webViewGroupAfterAClear` failed, with the guard above: "✘ Test run with 3 tests in 2 suites failed … with 5 issues". Navigation bars: ["New Research Note", "UI Test Document One"]", and `testTheEditMenuLeadsWithTheReadersActions` failed at the new first-item check, "("Optional("Probe")") is not equal to ("Optional("Highlight Yellow")") … ["Probe", "Highlight Yellow", "Highlight Green", "Highlight Blue", "Highlight Pink"]", the prefix check before it having passed.

## Session 2026-10-01 — Citation Lookup loses its never-run nearest-document strategy and the manifest's empty document count, Batch hides the fields it never reads and counts best guesses apart, side-loading says citation lookup leaves the volume out, and the app cites Potsdam's unnumbered documents as its exports do (lane CITE; #1504, #1506, #1523, #1524, #1491)

**The question.** Five Citation Lookup follow-ups from build 48, three of them with an owner decision recorded in the plan of record's §0 (D6, D7, D17): #1504 (D6, delete the nearest-document strategy, the manifest's `documentCount` and the OpenAPI text), #1506 (D17, hide Parsed Fields in Batch and give best guesses their own bucket), #1523 (D7, keep refusing side-loaded volumes and tell the reader at side-load time), #1524 (the title fragment's volume-numeral strip, measure first), and #1491 (cite the Potsdam volume's bracketed `@n` in the app through `CitableDocumentNumber.resolve`, as the exports do).

**What was measured.**
- **#1504.** All 553 bundled manifest rows carried `"documentCount" : 0`, and the only reader of the field was `matchByFuzzyDocumentNumber`, which returned at its `maxDoc > 0` guard: the strategy never answered in the app. `ParsedTEIHeader.documentCount` (TEIHeaderKit) was always 0 and fed only the manifest and the side-load catalogue.
- **#1524, through the #1505 harness** (the real `CitationParser`, `CitationMatchingEngine`, `CitationFormatter` and `CountCopy` sources over the bundled manifest, manifest-only; rebuilt in the lane's cache with current stubs). On `v2` the app's own citations of all 553 volumes in history.state.gov, Chicago and Turabian form, marked and plain, round-trip 551 of 553 in each of the six forms (the 1877 and 1894 appendices, as before). Two candidate fixes were measured against that, #1505's 2,492 synthetic citations and the 30,204 footnote clauses naming the series:
  - **whole word everywhere** (the numeral stripped as a whole word wherever it stands): round trip unchanged, 2,492 unchanged, but it still took the title's own numeral out of `frus1872p2v2`'s "Part II, Volume II" and `frus1873p1v1`'s "Part I … Volume I", leaving "Part";
  - **the phrase, else the first bare numeral** (shipped): the first volume phrase that stands whole is removed (`Volume V`, `vol. 5`, `v. II` — a phrase running into a word is not one, so it need not be the phrase the numeral was read from, as the Williamsburg note below shows), or with no such phrase the first whole-word occurrence of the bare numeral (`FRUS, 1969–76, I`). Round trip 551 of 553 in all six forms, byte-identical to `v2`; 2,492 synthetic citations identical; 30,204 clauses: **2 differ**, and neither answer was right before or after — a quoted Balfour letter whose "I have much pleasure" the parser reads as volume I (`frus1917Supp01v01, Supp02v01` → `Supp02v01`, both plain) and a Williamsburg note whose "this volume. Documentation" the parser reads as volume D (`frus1981-88v13, v38` → `v38`, both best guesses; the note is v38's own, and "Debt" no longer loses its D). Of the app's own 3,318 citations, 2,592 fragments change (the maimed "olume", "ietnam", "ran" are gone, and "Part II" keeps its numeral), and no top-three answer moves.

**What changed.**
- **#1504 (D6).** Deleted: Strategy 4 in `match(input:)`, `matchByFuzzyDocumentNumber`, `ConfidenceLabels.fuzzyDocument` and `.fuzzyDocumentNote`, `MatchStrategy.fuzzyDocumentNumber`, its badge colour and icon in `CitationLookupView`, and its arm in Batch's and Add Documents' strategy switches; `documentCount` from both `VolumeManifestEntry` declarations (the app's and `ManifestGeneratorCore`'s), the generator's two writers, `ParsedTEIHeader`, `LocalVolumeCatalog`, the 553 manifest rows, and the OpenAPI spec (two sentences of `/citation-lookup`, the `VolumeManifestEntry` required list and property, the `MatchStrategy` enum value). 36 test construction sites and four helpers drop the argument; the tests that drove the strategy on fixtures with a count now pin that a number past a volume's last finds nothing once indexed, and the not-yet-indexed row before.
- **#1506 (D17).** `CitationLookupMode.showsParsedFields` is false for Batch only, and the form mounts the Parsed Fields as its own section where it is true. `CitationLookupFocus.initial(for:)` (lifted out of the view's private `LookupField`, with a `batch` case) focuses the paste field, the footnote editor or Subseries, and the opening nudge and every mode change use it; the footnote editor had no focus binding, and entering Batch focused Subseries, raising the iPhone keyboard over a field Batch ignores. `BatchCitationOutcome.bestGuess` is a lone row the engine labels a best guess (`CitationMatch.isBestGuess`, since review round 1): a document under `.bestGuess` — a volume the citation does not name, or not the cited page — a volume row (to download, or not yet indexed) whose volume fails a cited field, which keeps `.manifestOnly` and is marked `CitationMatch.volumeIsBestGuess`, and the `.bestGuess` row a citation whose subseries no volume has gets. (As first built only the first counted, and the other two stayed ambiguous beside their own "Best guess — …" label.) It sorts after failed and missing and before ambiguous, and `BatchCitationOutcome.summary(of:locale:)` counts it apart: "12 citations · 7 resolved · 2 ambiguous · 2 best guesses · 1 unresolved", every bucket named, the citation and best-guess counts through `CountCopy` (the replaced format string printed "1 citations" ungrouped and was in the count scan's baseline, which goes 294 → 293).
- **#1523 (D7).** `ManifestStore.citableEntries` names the volumes citation resolution answers for, the bundled catalogue, and both engine sites read it (they read `bundledEntries` before; the behaviour is unchanged). `SideloadCatalogueNotice` decides from the same list whether an import added a volume outside it, and both storage hubs show `SideloadCatalogueNoticeRow` — "Not in the bundled catalogue", in the warning state — under the import's own result. A file named after a catalogue volume is that volume and draws no notice. New copy, with its EditableContent block.
- **#1524.** As measured above, `CitationParser.extractTitleFragment`; `volumePhrasePatterns` is the one list `extractVolumeNumber` reads and the fragment strip removes, the strip alone requiring the phrase to end where its numeral does.
- **#1491.** `FRUSDocumentMetadata.init(citing:printedNumber:)` resolves the number through `CitableDocumentNumber.resolve`, and every in-app route builds its metadata there: `DocumentViewModel.citedDocument` (Copy Citation, its share message, BibTeX, RIS and Zotero — the last three read the entry's number alone and dropped the parsed one), the Mac `DocumentExportSupport.docMeta` (both popovers' citation, share, BibTeX, RIS and Zotero; the popover's unused `docMeta` property is gone and its **Document no.** row shows the cited number), and the Research-notes Markdown export. `CrossReferenceTargetLabel`'s not-downloaded form names a number only where the id spells one (#1492's hardening). One citation changes for a numbered document too: with neither the entry nor the parse holding a number, the reader's Copy Citation, BibTeX, RIS and Zotero printed none on `v2`, and now the id stands in where it spells the number ("Document 12"), as rule 3 has had every export do since #1406. Since review round 1 the captions that name a document by its number — the citation popover's identity line, the Mac reader's header, previous and next buttons, position and toolbar centre, the Mac Search row and the breadcrumb — name a document printed without one "Unnumbered (d710a-1)", D5's form (`CitableDocumentNumber.captionLabel`, `.headerLabel`, `.unnumberedLabel`), and `FRUSDocumentMetadata.init(_:)`, the unresolved route left with no caller, is deleted. (As first built they were "left to lane MACCOL (#1493, D5)", which leaves them out.)
- **Docs.** EditableContent: `citation.match.fuzzyNote` deleted, `settings.hub.sideload.notCatalogued.detail` added, two notes corrected, 78 ranges re-pointed, README rows 282 → 281 and 206 → 207, one Amendment-Log bullet. Seven proposals in `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md` under "CITE — #1504, #1506, #1523, #1524, #1491".

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

The review's eight verified findings and nine nits, each resolved in code, tests or docs; nothing is handed back to the owner.

- **#1491's captions were not fixed, and the hand-off to MACCOL had no taker** (raised by both lenses). #1491 names the citation popover's "Doc …" label and the Mac document header among the routes that print the bracketed `@n`; round 0 left them to lane MACCOL, whose #1493 and decision D5 cover only a generated block's list token and the Mac collection row, and whose branch changes none of these files. They are fixed here, in D5's form. `CitableDocumentNumber` gains `isUnnumbered(printed:)` and `unnumberedLabel(documentId:)` — the same key and text MACCOL declares, so whichever lane lands second keeps one copy, MACCOL's, which adds a volume variant — and two caption rules over them: `captionLabel(printed:documentId:)` ("Doc 12", "Unnumbered (d710a-1)", or "Doc" and the id when nothing stored or spelled names a number) and `headerLabel(printed:documentId:)` ("Document 475" or "Unnumbered (d710a-1)"). They name the document in the citation popover's identity line (`SupportingViews.swift`), the Mac reader's header, previous and next buttons and the position between them (`MacDocumentView.swift`), its standalone window's toolbar centre (`MacDocumentTitle.principalLabel`), the Mac Search row (`SearchSheet.swift`) and the breadcrumb (`BrowserBreadcrumbBar.swift`). ## Session 2026-10-01 — Cross-Reference Analytics draws its Most-Referenced bars at the Mac window's 720–820 pt and on a phone, an E-volume's matrix column reads its E-number, no short volume label says an E-number twice, and a phone's matrix row label no longer breaks a word across its lines (lane XREF; #1472, #1473, one fold-in)

**The question.** Lane XREF of the 2026-09-28 plan of record. #1473: on the Mac, at the Cross-Reference Analytics window's 720 pt minimum and its ~820 pt default, Most-Referenced Documents drew document titles running off the right edge and no bars. #1472: the heat matrix's column code for every 1969–76 E-volume read "’69–76 Volume", the first word of its title, and every short volume label said an E-volume's number twice. The fold-in (#1379's "seen on the iPhone"): in the phone's 150 pt matrix label column a long tag left the topic a sliver, and its first word broke over the two lines — "Microfi" over "che S…".

**What was measured** (`v2` @ `0591a2df`; iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A9FCCA50`; Xcode 27.0). Each figure is from a test run on `v2`'s behaviour put back behind the new API (below), not from reading code.
- **#1473.** The chart drawn by `ImageRenderer` with the #1379 fixture's fifteen volumes, each named as a not-downloaded document is ("Document 1 — <volume title>"): **0 bars** at 720, 820 and 402 pt. In the app on the iPhone, with `FRUS_UI_TEST_SEED_CROSSREF_MATRIX=1`, every bar's accessibility element was **1 pt wide at x 977** of the 402 pt window, and **5 of the 12 rows on screen drew no title** (Swift Charts dropping labels that collide); the screenshot is `durable/w49/work/XREF/shots/ranking-iphone17-red-v2.png`. The issue's "blank row" is that, and it went with the fix. The chart has no platform branch, so the phone had the Mac's bug, worse.
- **#1472.** Over the bundled manifest's 553 volumes, **22** titles print "Volume E–N", all `frus1969-76ve*`. Each one's column code alone was "’69–76 Volume", and no other volume's code read "Volume"; all 22 together escalated to "’69–76 Volume 12", "’69–76 Volume 13", …; `ve05p1` and `ve05p2` fell to the id-suffix fallback, "’69–76 ve05p1" / "’69–76 ve05p2". All 22 topics began "Volume E–N, Documents on …", so the joined label read "Volume E–13, Documents on China · 1969-76 vE-13".

Both cut forms left the bars 341 pt.

**What changed.**
- **#1473** (`CrossReferenceAnalyticsView.swift`, `RankingChartLabels.swift`). The chart is its own view, `CrossReferenceRankingChart`, moved whole from the view's `rankingChart` (its id-keyed bars, domain, audio-graph descriptor and VoiceOver labels unchanged), so a test can draw it at a width. Its axis label is set in `RankingAxisLabelLayout`: at most `RankingChartAxis.labelWidth(chartWidth:)` wide — 40% of the chart, raised to 120 pt, capped at 320 pt, then lowered so the plot keeps 160 pt, never negative — on up to two lines, cut at the tail. The chart reads its width with a `GeometryReader`, not a measurement kept in `@State`, because the exported figure renders it once at the plate's width and a stored screen width would size the figure's labels for the window. `InDegreeRow` is internal so the chart and its test can take one.
- **#1472** (`RankingChartLabels.swift`, `ChronologyViewModel.swift`). `firstVolumeNumeral` takes an E-designator verbatim (`Volumes?\s+(E[–-][0-9]+|[IVXLCDM]+)\b`), so ve13 reads "’69–76 E–13". `volumeTopic` removes "Volume E–N" as it removes a Roman "Volume N", so every E-volume's topic starts "Documents on …" on every surface that reads the short label (the Chronology legend, banner and card, the Mac document window, the iPad compilation line, Corpus Analytics, the matrix rows). `matrixTopicWords` skips a leading "Documents on" when a word follows (only the E-volumes' topics open with it), so ve05's parts read "’69–76 E–5 Sub" and "’69–76 E–5 North"; it is internal now so its branches are tested. The column input moved from the view into `HeatMatrixColumnAxis.column(volumeId:entry:)`, unchanged, so a test can sweep it over the manifest.
- **Fold-in** (`CrossReferenceAnalyticsView.swift`, `RankingChartLabels.swift`). The row label is its own view, `HeatMatrixRowLabel`, laid out by `HeatMatrixRowLabelLayout`. The tag sits beside the topic, on its last line's baseline, only where `HeatMatrixRowAxis.tagSitsBesideTopic` says so: the room beside it is at least half the column (two lines beside hold at least one line across) and holds the topic's first word (`firstWord(of:)`, measured as a hidden third text). Elsewhere the topic takes one line of the whole column and the tag the next. The layout decides from the width it is offered, not the bounds it is placed in; a prototype that read the bounds set every tag below its topic, "China" included.

## Session 2026-10-01 — Developer hygiene: three unit tests stop failing on an iPad host, a semantic map pass that will refuse does so before the vectors are written, the packet sheet is built over its plan and nothing else, four screens nothing presented are deleted, and the Mac's Search tooltip and hint name ⌥⌘F (lane HYG; #1412, #1439, #1423, #1450, #1484, eight fold-ins)

**The question.** Lane HYG of the 2026-09-28 plan of record: five developer-only issues and the planning audit's eight fold-ins, in one PR. Nothing here changes what a reader's data says. Two strings on the Mac's main window change, and one packet-sheet empty state no screen could reach is deleted.

**What was measured** (`v2` @ `dc17d945`; Xcode 27.0; iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A9FCCA50`; iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 27.0, `9AB3A0C9`).
- **#1412, reproduced.** `v2`'s `SplashDriftTests.swift` and `OnboardingDockMetricsTests.swift` on the iPad: **"✘ Test run with 19 tests in 2 suites failed after 0.107 seconds with 4 issues"** — the three tests and four expectations the issue names (`OnboardingDockMetricsTests.swift:102`; `SplashDriftTests.swift:202`, `:236` and `:303`, a line above the issue's numbers since #1529). On the iPhone the same files pass.
- **#1439.** Whether a document count can be had before the vectors are pooled: each volume's `head.json` states `docs`, and over the shipped store (`~/frus-semantic-raw`, 553 volumes) it equals the row count the committed index records for that volume in all 553 — 314,571 by either sum, which is also `layout-meta.json`'s `documents`.
- **Dead code, by declared symbol.** A scan of every type `FRUSExplorer/` declares against every code line, comments dropped: 1,769 types, 7 named on no code line — `PromptsListView`; four that only tests or tools name (`BundledArtifactProvenance`, `CollectionFootnoteStyle`, `ProjectContextViewModel`, `SemanticMapFrameSequence`); and two private views nothing constructs, `FilterChip` and `CrossProjectNoteIndicator`. `GlobalContextView` was not among them only because `DiscoveryTips.forbiddenAnchors` spelled its path in a string. The lane's Swift scan, with strings blanked too: 483 files, 401 types whose header names `View`, 4 unnamed — those two, `GlobalContextView` and `PromptsListView`.
- **What each named deletion took with it.** `PromptsListView.swift` declared the view and a private `PromptRow`. `GlobalContextView.swift` declared the view and two private rows; its view model's file declared `GlobalContextViewModel`, `ProjectBreakdownEntry` and `VolumeBreakdownEntry`, none named outside those two files and two test files. `BrowserView.splitLayout` was the only constructor of `SubseriesListView`, and that of `SubseriesRowView`. The four-argument `updateNoteText` had one caller, a test. With `TripPacketSeed.documents` and `.collection` gone, `UnavailableReason.smartSearchUnavailable` and its two strings are unreachable.
- **The Mac's shortcut text.** Six string literals in the app name a ⌘ shortcut. Two were wrong about Search, which `FindMenuContent` registers as ⌥⌘F: the toolbar tooltip said (⌘F), which is Find in Document, and the main window's empty-state hint said (⌘S), which the app binds to nothing.
- **License headers.** 1,174 Swift files in 110 directories — the app 480, the unit tests 339, the UI tests 21, the widgets 2, and 332 in the 106 directories `Package.swift` names as a target's `path:` — and `Package.swift` itself: every one carries the "Licensed under" line and the license URL in its first 20 lines. The scan read the first two directories.
- **Package targets.** `Package.swift` declares 38 libraries, 31 executables and 37 test targets; `CLAUDE.md` said 37, 30 and 36.
- **#1450, the route the lane's two devices could not reach.** Neither of them folds the collection editor's ＋ Add into the toolbar's overflow. Showing the tab sidebar to narrow the editor was tried on the iPad in portrait: the content area read 752 pt while it showed, but the sidebar is an overlay there, the first tap on the Collections list dismissed it, and the editor opened at full width with ＋ Add in the toolbar. The device #1450 names, iPad Air 11-inch (M4) on iOS 26.5, was installed on this machine all along; review round 1 ran the suite there (below).
- **A host crash on the iPad, not this lane's.** The full unit target on the iPad ended "** TEST EXECUTE FAILED **" under a passing summary line: `RichTextRestingCapTests` ("Editing lifts the cap within the editing height; ending it restores the cap, scrolled back to the top") terminates the test host with `NSInvalidArgumentException` from UIKit's keyboard assistant ("NSLayoutConstraint for … TUIInputAssistantHostView … A constraint cannot be made from … to a constant"), and the relaunch's summary counts only what ran after it. It did so in the full run and in a run of that suite alone. The suite passes on the iPhone.

**What changed.**
- **#1412** (`SplashDriftTests.swift`, `OnboardingDockMetricsTests.swift`; no app code). `LaunchSplashView.identityZones` already took `metrics:`, defaulting to this device's. Every fixture now passes the metrics its canvas belongs to, and no test reads `LaunchSplashView.tileSize`, `.blockSpacing` or `.identityBlockMinimumHeight`, which are this device's too. The pure-geometry tests run per idiom (`SplashDriftTests.Idiom`: iPhone 393 × 852, iPad 834 × 1210, Mac 560 × 540; the iPad's read 834 × 1194, an older 11-inch model's height, until review round 1), so an iPhone host tests the iPad's block and the reverse; the drift sweep runs for the phone and the iPad. The phone-only bound, "less than the 340 × 260 rect the two zones replaced", is its own test. The onboarding fixtures stay an iPhone 17's and say so: their two dock heights were measured on a phone. `geometryFixturesNameTheirIdiom` reads every Swift file in the unit-test target and refuses a call without `metrics:` (it read a list of the three files that build identity zones until review round 1).
- **#1439** (`SemanticVectorsRunner.swift`, `SemanticMapPacker.swift`). `run()` hands the process's environment and tagger verdict to `run(environment:languageAnalysis:)`, so a test can drive the run. When `LAYOUT_DIR/layout.bin` exists, the run reads every manifest volume's head, sums their `docs`, and calls `SemanticMapPacker.preflight` before it creates a directory: the tagger verdict, `layout-meta.json`, the layout's document count against that sum, `layout.bin`'s length, at least one clustered row, and the two word-cloud payloads — every `throw` in `pack`. The manifest's coverage dates (`loadVolumeEras`), which the run's map block decoded after the vectors were written, are read there too since review round 1. `pack` keeps its own checks, on the count the vector pass really pooled. With no layout the verdict is never asked for.
- **#1423** (`TripPacketSheet.swift`, `ArchiveVisitEditorView.swift`). The sheet takes `plan: ArchiveVisitPlan`. `TripPacketSeed` keeps its name and the two static functions the three collection menus call, and has no cases. The count-copy baseline loses two entries (293 → 291) and `macTapExceptions` one (7 → 6). App tree: 25 files, +169 −1,147 lines.
- **A gate for the class** (`UnconstructedViewAuditTests`, in `ToolbarAccessibilityAuditTests.swift`). A type under `FRUSExplorer/` whose header names `View` must be named by code besides its own declaration and extensions, comments and strings blanked, every `#if` branch kept. After the deletions: 480 files, 394 such types, 2 unnamed, both in its exact `knownUnnamed` list.
- **Mac shortcut text** (`MainWindowView.swift`). The Search tooltip reads "Open the full-text search window (⌥⌘F)". The empty-state hint, a bare `Text`, is keyed `mainwindow.placeholder.hint` and reads "Use Search (⌥⌘F) or open the Corpus Browser (⇧⌘B)". Nine comments in five files that said ⌘F or ⌘S for Search say ⌥⌘F, `FindMenuContent`'s doc among them (`AppState.swift` 1, `FRUSExplorerApp.swift` 3, `MainWindowView.swift` 2, `SearchSheet.swift` 2, `CitationLookupView.swift` 1). The Browse button's comment, which gave ⇧⌘B to the window scene, names the Find menu since review round 1.
- **`SearchView`'s Archival Neighbors sheet is `#if os(iOS)`**, like the one action that sets its target; `ArchivalNeighborsSheet` leaves `pendingMacChecks`, which now holds the two entries checked on a Mac.
- **`SemanticVectorsGenerator`: `DIMS` defaults to 512** (`defaultShippingDims`), held to the committed index's width by a test. The default is validated like a typed width, so on a store narrower than 512 an unset `DIMS` is refused; the lane's own test for that failed first ("✘ Test run with 78 tests in 12 suites failed after 0.080 seconds with 2 issues") and the validation followed.

**Decisions the plan did not settle.**
- **The whole `GlobalContextViewModel` went, not its reading analytics alone.** The view was its only app caller, so the plan's "its VM's reading analytics" would have left a view model only tests construct. Its seven tests and two `AboutViewTests` cases went with it.
- **The packet sheet takes a plan; `TripPacketSeed` stays as a namespace.** The triage allowed "a plain namespace or keeping only `.plan`". A one-case enum would have kept an optional plan that is never `nil`, unwrapped in four places. A new entry point makes a plan (`ArchiveVisitPlan.make`) and presents the editor's sheet.
- **The two smart-search strings and their EditableContent blocks are deleted, not marked RETIRED**, as lane CITE did with `citation.match.fuzzyNote`.
- **`forbiddenAnchors` is empty and kept**, with its two audits and a fixture that drives the rule, for the next view kept unpresented.
- **The license scan went wider than the UI tests** (the widgets, `Package.swift`, 106 package directories) **and tighter** (the URL as well as the first line, at the top). Every file passed both before the change.
- **The hint under "Select a document to begin" was fixed with the tooltip**, though the plan named the tooltip alone: it said ⌘S, on the same window.
- **`PROJECT_ONLY` with a store for some planned groups is not refused.** It rewrites the run-wide artifacts over the groups it finds, as a subset run does; the plan's item was the no-store case.
- **The preflight counts by the store's heads.** `pack`'s exact check stays, so a store whose heads misstate its documents can still refuse after the vectors are written.
- **The runner templates got a banner and a test, not corrected prompts**: they are the record of what C-0 and C-2 ran.
- **`build_layout.py`'s `DIMS` comment** now says its 256 is the width the shipped map was projected from, not the vectors' shipping width: with the packer's default at 512 the two tools read one variable name and mean different things.
- **#1450 has no test that forces its overflow branch on a wide iPad.** One was written (it showed the tab sidebar to narrow the editor) and removed when the measurement above showed it could not reach the overflow on this lane's iPad. The branch is reached by running the suite on iPad Air 11-inch in portrait, which review round 1 did.

### Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01)

Seven confirmed findings, all resolved; five nits, all taken. The paragraphs above are corrected in place where they said otherwise.

- **#1450 was never run where it fails, and the device was installed** (correctness). `CollectionEditorTitleTests` on **iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5** (`4973970C`), in portrait, which the suite sets: **"Executed 8 tests, with 3 tests skipped and 0 failures"**, the four heading tests each printing `[CollectionEditorAddMenu] opened from the toolbar's overflow menu`. ⚙ Collection stays in the bar at that width — the three pushed-settings tests skip on the sheet route, and `testTheEditorIsTitledWithTheCollectionsName` opens the sheet from the button — so `settingsControls()` needs no overflow branch there. `CollectionProseRowRestTests`, which calls the same helper, ran with it: **"Executed 13 tests, with 3 tests skipped and 0 failures"** for the two suites, its two default-size note-block tests from the overflow (`testALongNoteBlockRestsOnItsOpeningWords`, `testTextColorKeepsALongNoteBlockOpenWhileItsPickerIsUp`) and its two AX3 tests from the toolbar's ＋ Add, as lane K3 measured; its fifth, `testALongIntroductionRestsOnItsOpeningWords`, opens no Add menu. `CLAUDE.md` names the Air as the suite's third destination, with its command.
- **"Four tests failed" was reasoning, and is now a measurement** (tests-claims). Lane K3's run, the only one on that device before this round, saw **one** failure: `testContentAloneDoesNotNameANewCollection`, the one test that then added a heading; #1413 added the other three. `CLAUDE.md`, the suite's doc, the helper's doc and this entry said four had failed. A/B on the Air with `addSectionHeading()` re-edited to the bar-only lookup: **4 failed** (`testADescriptionSetInSectionDefaultsSurvivesAToggleInTheSameSheet`, `testASubtitleSetInSectionDefaultsSurvivesTheEditorsNextEdit`, `testContentAloneDoesNotNameANewCollection`, `testTheEditorShowsASubtitleSetInSectionDefaults`, each at `CollectionEditorTitleTests.swift:358`, "The editor has no Add menu"), 3 skipped, 1 passed, "** TEST EXECUTE FAILED **". The docs now say which was measured when.
- **One map-pass throw was still reachable after the vectors were written** (correctness, and the same fact as a tests-claims finding). `run` called `try loadVolumeEras(manifestPath)` at the top of its map block, after every vector artifact and shard was on disk. It decodes `dateRange` as `{earliest: String, latest: String}`; the pre-write read of the volume list never reads `dateRange`. So a manifest entry with a one-sided or non-string `dateRange` passed the first read and threw at the second, leaving new vectors beside the old map. Latent: all 553 shipped entries carry a two-string `dateRange`. The eras are now read inside the pre-write `if packsMap` block, beside the head count and the preflight. Two tests: `MapPassRefusesBeforeTheVectorsTests.undecodableDateRangeRefusesBeforeAnyWrite` drives the run over a one-sided `dateRange` with a layout (a `DecodingError`, neither output directory created) and, as its control, the same manifest with no layout (the vectors pack, since a run with no map never reads the dates); `RunWriteOrderTests.mapBlockThrowsOnlyFromThePackAndItsWrites` requires that the eras are read once, before the first write, and that the block after the vectors holds exactly three `try`s — `SemanticMapPacker.pack` and its two writes. `CLAUDE.md`, `preflight`'s doc and `run`'s doc, which each said the preflight covered every refusal, name the eras read.
- **The no-lemmatiser refusal still described the state #1439 removed** (correctness). `ClusterLabeller.LabelError.languageAnalysisUnavailable` read "refusing to write the map. The vector artifacts do not read the tagger. Re-run in a new process." It now says the run refused before its first write, that nothing was written, neither the vector artifacts nor the map, and that `LAYOUT_DIR` pointed at a directory with no `layout.bin` packs the vectors alone — `storeCountMismatch`'s workaround. `noLemmatiserRefusesBeforeAnyWrite` pins "Nothing was written" and "LAYOUT_DIR".
- **The geometry-fixture scan read a list of three files** (tests-claims). `SplashDriftTests.geometryFixturesNameTheirIdiom` now enumerates every Swift file under `FRUSExplorerTests/` (339, the two subdirectories included), keeps the 10-call floor, and requires that the callers it finds include the three known ones, so a scan that stops reading the target fails.
- **`TripPacketSheet`'s header cited a test for "nothing else presents it" that read two files** (tests-claims). `TripPacketEntryPointParityTests.onlyTheEditorPresentsThePacketSheet` walks every Swift file under `FRUSExplorer/`, comments stripped, and requires exactly one `TripPacketSheet(` or `TripPacketSheet.init(`, in `ArchiveVisitEditorView.swift`. The header is unchanged and is now true of the test it names.
- **Nits taken.** Three comments gave the Corpus Browser's ⇧⌘B to the wrong owner — `MainWindowView.swift`'s Browse button ("owned by the `frus.corpusBrowser` scene"), and two in `FRUSExplorerApp.swift` the review did not list (the scene's "lives on the Research-menu item", and the Research menu's "Corpus Browser lives in the WINDOW menu … ⌘⇧B stays on this Button"); all three name the Find menu, where `FindMenuContent` registers it. `TripPacketExporter`'s four doc lines about an "ephemeral packet", which no screen can build, say what a `nil` overlay and unset deliverables do. `CLAUDE.md`'s license rule says every built target and names what is outside it, where it said tree-wide. ## Session 2026-10-01 — A document's figures show their images in the reader and in PDF, Word and HTML exports, fetched with the volume and removed with it; "[Figure]" prints only when the image is absent, a film links to its page, and a space between two inline elements is drawn (lane READ; #1516, one fold-in)

**The question.** Lane READ of the 2026-09-28 plan of record, owner decision D3 option (f)4. A figure printed only its file's name — "figure_1162" in the reader, "[figure_1162]" in a PDF, "[Figure: figure_1162]" in Word — and neither its head nor its captions, and the app had no image to show. The lane: fetch each volume's figure images from history.state.gov beside its XML (never a page's scan), remove them with the volume, count them in Volumes & Storage, draw them in the reader and embed them in PDF and Word; treat a figure's head and paragraphs as captions with no re-index; print "[Figure]" only when the image is absent and nothing for an empty `<figure/>`; give the 20 Public Diplomacy films a "Watch on history.state.gov ↗" link and their head; and, folded in, stop the reader dropping the whitespace between two inline elements (`frus1861` d2 read "Washington,February 28, 1861"). And measure the real corpus image total.

**What was measured** (corpus `8e5da08c1`, the 553 manifest volumes, 2026-10-01; the scripts and their output are in the session's folder outside the repository, `durable/w49/work/READ/`).
- **The image total.** By HEAD request to `https://static.history.state.gov/frus/<volume>/<url>.png` for each of the 968 distinct (volume, `<graphic url>`) pairs the figures name (`measure_images.py`; no image was fetched there — review round 1 read each served image's first 24 bytes, below): **553 are served, 140,994,857 bytes (141.0 MB, 134.5 MiB), in 96 volumes**, every one as `image/png`; 415 answer **HTTP 403**, which is what the host says for a file it does not have. Of the 415, 402 are title-page figures (one in each of 402 volumes; none is served) and **13** are names in the text: `Appendix A.1`–`A.3` in `frus1917-72PubDipv06` and again in `v07`, `figure_0283` and `figure_0318` in `frus1945Malta`, `figure_1163` in `frus1946v01`, `figure_0284` and `figure_0285` in `frus1950-55Intel`, `figure_0001` in `frus1952-54v04`, and `genassemblybldg` in `frus1969-76ve09p1`. Per volume that has a served image: median 328,492.5 bytes (the mean of the 48th and 49th of the 96; this entry first gave 337,027, the 49th), mean 1,468,696, the largest `frus1943CairoTehran` at 25,443,143; the largest single image is its `figure_0383.png`, 3,556,499 bytes. In documents alone: 486 names, 480 served, 112,077,086 bytes. `.png` is added to every name, whatever it ends in: `OpenPitMine.jpg` is served only as `OpenPitMine.jpg.png`.
- **The figures.** 1,035 `<figure>`s: 532 in a `<div type="document">` (426 a graphic alone, 50 a head and a graphic, 32 a graphic and paragraphs, 20 empty, 2 a `figDesc` and a graphic, 1 paragraphs alone, 1 a head and paragraphs) and 503 outside one: 403 on title pages, one in each of 403 volumes (402 name a graphic; `frus1865p4`'s is an empty `<figure/>`, which is why the title pages give 402 names); 20 video players; and 80 elsewhere — 45 in `section` divs, 33 in `chapter` or `subchapter` divs, and 2 directly in `<front>`, outside every div (`frus1931-41v02` `figure_0007`, served, 284,620 bytes; `frus1952-54v04` `figure_0001`, one of the 13 refused). No figure names two graphics.
- **A page's scan is a `<graphic>` too.** 1,143,043 of them, in `<facsimile><surface>`, in 551 of the 553 volumes (`scan_graphics.py`), against 992 in figures and none anywhere else. So "the figures' graphics" is not "the graphics", and the name scan takes a `<graphic>` only inside a `<figure>`. A first draft of the doc comment said a scan was a `<pb facs>` and no `<graphic>`; the fixture now carries the real `<surface>` shape.
- **The films.** 20 video figures (`scan_videos.py`): 12 `<object>` players in `frus1917-72PubDip` (appendix-5 and appendix-11), 5 `<iframe>`s in volume VI (appendix-1 to -3) and 3 in volume VII (appendix-1 to -3; these three have no head). Every one sits in an `online-supplement` div inside a `section`/`historical-document` the parser promotes to a document. The eight pages their links name each answered HTTP 200, and an invented `appendix-zzz` 404.
- **The whitespace.** 54,025 whitespace-only runs between two inline elements inside documents (`scan_seams.py`): 14,193 a `<placeName>` then a `<date>` in a dateline, in 9,884 documents; 4,439 a `<gloss>` then a `<persName>` in a paragraph. 7,337 more follow a `<note>` before an inline element, and 6,387 have a `<pb>` on one side and an inline element on the other.

**What changed.**
- **Fetch, keep, remove, count** (`DownloadManager.swift`, `DownloadModels.swift`, `ResetService.swift`, `FRUSExplorerApp.swift`). When a download finishes, `DownloadManager` scans the volume's XML for the graphics of its figures outside the title page (`FigureImageLibrary.graphicNames`) and fetches each into `{Volumes}/<volume>.figures/<url>.png`, dropping any image an update's text no longer names. A 403 or 404 is remembered for the session and not asked for again; a failed transfer, an error status, or a 2xx that is not a PNG (a network's sign-in page) is not kept and is asked for again. Requests follow Allow Cellular Downloads. A whole-volume run is keyed by the volume and which of its texts it read, so an update that lands mid-run stops the old text's names and starts a run over the new one; an image that lands after its volume was removed is removed. `deleteVolume`, `cancelDownload` and Reset Local Data remove the folder. `storageReport` counts the images per volume and in total; `StorageReport.totalVolumesBytes` stays the XML alone, because the index estimate is derived from it.
- **A volume downloaded before this build** is brought up to its images by a pass over the library at launch and on reconnect (`DownloadManager.fetchMissingFigureImages(among:)`, added in review round 1, below; as first committed, such a volume got an image only when the reader or an export asked for one). Until the pass reaches a volume, the reader and the PDF, Word and HTML exports fetch the image they need (`FigureImageStore`, one per process, configured at boot): a catalogue volume's only, and only while online (`FigureImageStore.mayFetch`). The first image fetched that way starts the rest of the volume's.
- **Volumes & Storage** (`SettingsComponents.swift`, `StorageHubModel.swift`, both hubs). The storage bar has a **Figures** segment after XML; a volume's row shows its text and images together; Free Up Space's estimate adds the images once, outside the 2.8× index factor.
- **The figure itself** (`FRUSRenderNode.swift`, `ASTToRenderNodeConverter.swift`). `.figureBlock` carries a `FigureBlock`: the image's name and volume, the head (a second head on a line of its own), each `<p>` and `figDesc` as a caption line, and for a video player its page's address. An empty figure converts to nothing. A player's own elements and hidden text print nothing.
- **The reader** (`FRUSRenderNodeHTMLSerializer.swift`, `HTMLTemplate.swift`, `FRUSURLSchemeHandler.swift`). A figure is a `<figure>` — a `<span>` inside a line, so a paragraph is not split — holding its head, an `<img src="frusexplorer://figure/<volume>/<file>">` and its captions. The scheme handler answers with the bytes, or fails at once so the placeholder shows, fetches the image, and then has the page ask again; the page's second request starts no fetch of its own. "[Figure]" is shown only while the image is absent.
- **Exports** (`PDFCollectionExporter.swift`, `DocxCollectionExporter.swift`, `CollectionItemHTMLRenderer.swift`, `HTMLCollectionExporter.swift`, `CollectionContentResolver.swift`). A PDF, Word or HTML export first fetches the images its full-body documents lack; the live preview does not, nor — since review round 1 — a BibTeX, RIS or Zotero export, which prints none. PDF sets an image under its head at two pixels to the point, never wider than the 468 pt column or taller than 560 pt; Word stores it once as `word/media/figureN.png` and draws it in the paragraph under its head (a figure that is an image alone stays a run of its line, so a mark in a table cell stays in the cell; in a footnote the image prints as its placeholder, since the footnotes part has no relationship to it); HTML embeds it as a `data:` URL. A film prints its head and a link — in the PDF, the address in print.
- **No re-index, and no stale highlight.** A figure's head, captions and placeholder, and the drawn space below, are under `data-skip` in the page and are not flat text in either Swift walk, so `renderingVersion`, `body_hash` and `body_text` are what they were. **The index stays at v64.** The selection bridge (`kSelectionJS` and `frus-selection.js`, kept identical) treats a figure and a drawn space as drawn parts, so a selection that starts or ends on one still maps to offsets.
- **The fold-in** (`FRUSDocumentParser.swift`, `FRUSASTNode.swift`, `IndexingPipeline.swift`). The parser keeps a whitespace-only run as `.elementSpace` where the element before it is inline and the one after is not a block (`keepsElementSpace`): never directly inside a container that holds only blocks, and across a page break only when text precedes it. It is drawn as one space, outside the flat text; `PrintedText` skips it, because the index's printed join already spaced these seams and appending a space would move stored text.
- **Docs.** `CLAUDE.md` gains a Key Data Flows entry. Thirteen manual proposals under "READ — #1516" in `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md`. EditableContent: no block's text changes, 10 ranged blocks re-pointed, one Amendment-Log bullet.

**Decisions the plan did not settle.**
- **Where the files go:** `{Volumes}/<volume>.figures/`, a folder beside the XML, excluded from backup as the XML is. Everything that sweeps the volumes directory looks for `.xml` files, so the folder is none of theirs.
- **Title-page figures are not fetched or drawn.** All 403 sit outside every `<div>`, so in no document the parser returns, and the host serves none. The two figures directly in `<front>` are outside every `<div>` too, and the name scan, which leaves out only `<titlePage>`, does fetch those: see Still open.
- **A sign-in page is not a refusal.** A 2xx that is not a PNG is treated as a failed transfer and asked for again, where the first draft remembered it for the session: behind a captive portal that would have marked every image of the volume as missing until relaunch.
- **Side-loaded volumes** get images only when their id is a catalogue volume's (#777: the app has no address for any other).
- **The HTML export embeds images too.** The lane named PDF and Word; an HTML export that printed "[Figure]" beside them would have been the odd one.
- **Pre-download sizes do not count images.** A volume's stated size, the bulk download's total and onboarding's "≈ 3.5 GB" are the manifest's XML sizes (and match files); the manifest carries no image sizes. With images the whole series is 3,338,778,538 + 162,354,028 + 140,994,857 = 3,642,127,423 bytes, which rounds to 3.6 GB. Onboarding's figure is the owner's text and was left alone; see Still open.
- **Figures in footnotes** (6 in the corpus, all empty `<figure/>`s in `frus1881`) print nothing; an image in a Word footnote would print its placeholder.
- **The run bookkeeping was simplified during mutation testing.** Three checks removed a late image after its volume was gone; each survived alone, since the first does the work, and one of the others would have deleted the images of a volume removed and downloaded again mid-run (read from the code, not run). Two were deleted. Run-level de-duplication has no test: with per-image de-duplication under it, removing it changes no file and no request, only how often a volume's XML is scanned.

**How it was verified** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`; Xcode 27.0). 60 new tests in 9 suites: `FigureCaptionTests`, `ElementSpaceTests`, `FigureImageMarkupTests`, `ElementSpaceRuleTests`, `FigureExportTests`, `FigureImageExportTests`, `FigureImageDownloadTests`, `FigureStorageDisplayTests` and `FigureReaderTests`, the last in a real web view.
- **A/B on unfixed code.** The 13 tests that need no new API, built and run in a copy of `v2`'s tree at `dc17d945`: **"✘ Test run with 13 tests in 3 suites failed after 0.059 seconds with 27 issues"** — 12 failed; the 13th, that the drawn spaces are no flat text, holds on both sides by design and is killed by mutant batch 2.
- **A/B by mutation**, for the tests that cannot compile against `v2`: 68 mutants in 8 batches, applied and reverted as exact text edits by `mutate.py`, the tree checked clean after each. Batch 1 (reader, serializer, converter, parser, bridge): "✘ Test run with 58 tests in 10 suites failed … with 56 issues", 26 tests. Batch 2 (figure and space as flat text): 55 tests, 31 issues, 8 tests. Batch 2b (drawn outside `data-skip`): 36 tests, 28 issues, 5 tests. Batch 3 (exports, storage, manager): 29 tests, 34 issues, 17 tests. Batch 4: 42 tests, 22 issues, 14 tests. Batches 5–7, after the run rework, one mutant per expectation: 9 mutants and 9 tests; 6 and 5; 5 and 10. Of the 60 new tests every one fails in the unfixed run or under a mutant (`killed.py`).

Full unit target (`-only-testing FRUSExplorerTests`, on the final build, after every doc but this entry): **"✔ Test run with 6381 tests in 756 suites passed after 315.146 seconds"**, "** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **"; the test build's only warnings are the two known residues. `CodingStandardsAuditTests` and `EditableContentKeyTests` again with this entry in place: 80 tests in 2 suites passed.
