**Still open.**
- **By eye, owner.** On the Mac: a document with a figure (`frus1946v01` d587's maps, after the table), Volumes & Storage's Figures segment and a row's size, and a PDF and a Word export of that document. The Mac app was not run: a development build shares the owner's store. On an iPad nothing was run, and a real image from history.state.gov was never fetched, until review round 1 (below): every transfer in the tests is injected, and this entry's by-eye image was a stand-in.
- **The images' bytes were not read** by the survey, which was HEAD requests; a file served as `image/png` that is not a PNG would fail the app's signature check, print "[Figure]" and be asked for again. Closed in review round 1: all 553 open with the PNG signature.
- **Onboarding's "≈ 3.5 GB"** (`OnboardingView.swift:609`) and the manuals' corpus size are 141 MB short of a full download now. The owner's text; not changed.
- **`body_text` of the 12 `frus1917-72PubDip` film sections** holds the player's hidden text and script (`298x530`, `brightcove.createExperiences();`), because the index walks a figure's children. Fixing it changes stored text and needs an index version; read from the code, not from an index.
- **An image in flight when an update drops its name** is stored after the update's run has pruned, and stays until the volume's next update or removal.
- **Two things read in passing, not verified:** `DownloadManager.cancelDownload` removes the XML at the destination even when it cancels an Update of a volume already on the device; and `PDFCollectionExporter.drawFrameWithHighlights` takes line origins from `CTFrameGetLineOrigins` without adding the frame path's origin, which the new image drawing does add.

**Review fixes, round 1 (2026-10-01).** Fifteen confirmed findings, all resolved in code, tests or this entry, and three of the four nits taken. The scripts and their output are in the session's folder outside the repository, `durable/w49/work/READ/r1/`.
- **The installed base had no images, and a failed fetch was never tried again** (correctness; a deviation from D3). The fetch started only from a finished download and from the first image the reader or an export asked for, so a library downloaded before build 49 had none until a figure was looked at while online, and a transfer that failed, or a run cut short, was never resumed. `DownloadManager.fetchMissingFigureImages(among:)` is a pass over the catalogue volumes on the device, in id order, one at a time; the app starts it at launch and each time the device comes back online, once downloads are resumed (`FRUSExplorerApp.fetchMissingFigureImages(with:appState:)`). A volume whose run ended with nothing failed is recorded in `{Volumes}/.figure-images-complete.json` against its XML's size and modification date, so the library's XML is read once and not at every launch; whatever replaces the file changes the stamp. The pass stops when the manager is suspended and after three volumes in a row whose transfers all fail, so a launch that cannot fetch (offline, or cellular with Allow Cellular Downloads off) does not read the whole library to find that out. Side-loaded volumes are not read. The reader's and the exports' fetch of one image stays, for a volume the pass has not reached.
- **BibTeX, RIS and the Zotero send fetched images they never print** (correctness). The fetch was keyed on `purpose == .export` alone. `ExportFormat.printsFigureImages` is true for PDF, Word and HTML only; the export sheet passes it to `resolve(…printsFigureImages:)`, and `resolveDocuments` (RIS, Zotero) never fetches. The fetch moved out of `loadBatchContext` to one place after the items are resolved, so the smart and the static path cannot be wired apart, and it asks only for the images of documents resolved at full body depth. While it asks, the export sheet's status line reads "Fetching figure images…" (a new string, `collection.export.status.fetchingFigures`), and `FigureImageStore.fetchAbsent` stops between images when its task is cancelled.
- **The real host, an iPad, and real exports** (correctness, test gap). Three things were run. (1) **Every served image's first 24 bytes** were read by range request (`read_signatures.py`, 2026-10-01): all 553 answered 206 and open with the PNG signature, `OpenPitMine.jpg.png` among them (500 by 378 pixels). Widths run 89 to 19,043 pixels (`frus1958-60v03mSupp` `eq_03.png`), heights 18 to 5,536 (`frus1946v01` `figure_1166.png`, 10,568 wide); 72 of the 553 are wider than 936 pixels — the PDF's 468 pt column and Word's 6.5 inches, at two pixels to the point — so 72 are scaled down in an export; the 13 taller than Word's 1,152 pixels are all among them. (2) **The app fetched real images on an iPad** (iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 26.5, `9F3D84A4`, 2026-10-02 00:03 EDT; the container saved first and put back afterwards): four real volumes cloned into the container, the app launched, and 13 seconds later the launch pass had stored `frus1946v01`'s 2 images (569,273 bytes), `frus1951v03p1`'s 15 (2,879,080) and `frus1958-60v03mSupp`'s 36 (7,926,523) — each total the HEAD survey's to the byte, all 53 files PNGs — made no folder for `frus1917-72PubDipv06`, whose three names the host refuses, and recorded all five volumes on the device complete. By eye: `frus1946v01` d587's Annex "A" facsimile under its title and above its table; `frus1951v03p1` d289's photographs, each over its caption with the name still a link; Volumes & Storage's bar with an orange **Figures 11.4 MB** segment between XML 34 MB and Index 33.5 MB, and the rows reading 10 MB and 12 MB where the XML alone is 9.4 and 9.1 (`shots/`). (3) **A PDF, a Word file and an HTML page were exported with those images** by a one-off test, not committed, that loaded d587, d289 and `frus1958-60v03mSupp` d444 through `DocumentViewModel` and ran the three exporters over the iPad's figures folder. The PDF's 15 pages, rendered to pixels and read: the facsimile, "[Figure]" for the refused `figure_1163`, the 10,568-pixel world map at the column's width, nine photographs over their captions, and d444's four equation images, the 19,043-pixel one at the column's width. The Word package passes `unzip -t`, holds 15 `word/media` parts each byte-identical to its fetched file, and draws them at most 6.50 by 4.58 inches (the map 6.50 by 3.40, the widest equation 6.50 by 0.27) with one placeholder; the HTML embeds 15 images and one placeholder. Not run: the Mac app, and Word itself — see Still open.
- **A late image moved a revealed footnote out of view** (correctness, and a comment that was no longer true). The reveal's comment said the page has no images. An image on the device is answered before `didFinish`, so layout is settled; one that is not is fetched and laid out after the reveal's scroll, and a map pushes the footnotes down by its height. The reveal now records the entry it brought the reader to (`FRUSURLSchemeHandler.revealedFootnoteGlobal`), the retry script brings it back into view when its image has loaded, and the reader's own wheel, touch, click or key forgets it first.

- **Tests that could not fail** (tests-claims; seven gaps, each closed by a test driving the code the gap named). The reader's own load (`FigureReaderTests.theReadersLoadNamesImagesByItsVolume`, through `DocumentViewModel.load` and a real web view); Word's fit-to-page clamp (`docxFitsALargeImage`, the corpus's widest and tallest images and two through the exporter); the export header's dateline (`theExportedDatelineKeepsItsSpace`, `frus1865p4` d493's own dateline through the resolver); a link in a caption or a figure's head (`aLinkInACaptionResolvesWhenTapped`, registered and dispatched); both storage hubs (`bothHubsCountTheImages`, a scan of each hub's bar and row); the smart-collection export and `cancelDownload` (`aSmartCollectionsExportFetchesAbsentImages`, `cancellingADownloadRemovesItsImages`); and the parser's left-hand clause (`ElementSpaceRuleTests.notKeptAfterABlock`: a block before, an inline element after).

Measured (`scan_dateline_parents.py`): of the datelines holding a whitespace-only run between two inline elements, 43 are a document's own child, 13,692 sit in an `<opener>` (9,494 documents), 742 in a closer and 9 in an attachment. The opener's dateline prints with the body, where the space was already drawn.

Full unit target (`-only-testing FRUSExplorerTests`, iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`, on the final build): **"✔ Test run with 6398 tests in 756 suites passed after 384.652 seconds."**, "** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **"; the test build's only warnings are the two known residues. `CodingStandardsAuditTests` and `EditableContentKeyTests` again with this section in place: "✔ Test run with 80 tests in 2 suites passed after 42.595 seconds.". macOS: `FRUSExplorerMac` "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **" (Xcode 27.0, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`), with no warning beyond the two known residues.
- **Decisions for the owner that this round made or met.**
  - **The pass is automatic.** A full library downloaded before build 49 fetches up to 141 MB of images at its first launch on this build, without being asked, under Allow Cellular Downloads (on unless turned off). That is what D3 says a volume's images are; the alternative is the semantic vectors' — a switch and a button in Volumes & Storage — which needs copy and both hubs.
  - **Nothing on screen says a volume's images are incomplete**, and there is no control to fetch them. The pass tries again at each launch and reconnect.
  - **A quotation taken across a drawn space keeps the glued text.** `.elementSpace` is no flat text, by design, so that no highlight offset moves and nothing re-indexes; a highlight's stored passage and a collection excerpt are cut from flat text, so one taken across any of the 54,025 seams reads "Washington,February 28, 1861" beside a body that now prints the space. Closing it changes flat text and needs a rendering-version bump.
  - **The side-load notice** shown after an import (`settings.hub.sideload.notCatalogued.detail`) names Citation Lookup and Add Documents and does not say a side-loaded volume's figures read "[Figure]". The manuals' proposals say it; the in-app wording is the owner's.

## Session 2026-10-01 — The report to the Office of the Historian is compiled: 47 missing documents, 19 structural edits, and five more defect classes, each re-checked at the corpus head by a script (lane OH; #1309)

**The question.** Lane OH of the 2026-09-28 plan of record (decision P4: one post, each defect class documented). #1309 held the Malta diagnosis and three comments on pagination; the structure sweep (2026-09-20), the broken-reference report (2026-07-10) and the 2026-09-27 audit's list had never been put together, and nothing had been re-checked since. The lane was to compile one report, lead it with `frus1952-54v09p1`'s missing documents, re-check every item at the corpus head, and post nothing.

**What was measured.** Corpus `HistoryAtState/frus` at `8e5da08c1` (also the upstream `master`, by `git ls-remote`); `git diff 550a8c5c5 HEAD -- volumes` is empty, so `550a8c5c5` is the revision named. Every figure below is from `tools/oh-report/build_oh_report.py` over all 744 files, each of which parses.
- **The lead item holds.** `frus1952-54v09p1` ends at d899 on p. 1660 and Part 2 begins at d947 on p. 1743. The corpus' own history has the text: the parent of `d7c15c90c` (2016-10-31) holds 946 documents to p. 1741, and that commit's file 899 to p. 1660. ## Session 2026-10-02 — The Subject-Numeric File is its own filing era: an eleventh provenance category, a stored citation form (index v65) and a Source Explorer panel, placed by what the citation gives (lane CFPF; #1543, two fold-ins)

**The question.** #1543: "Subject-Numeric files need to be pulled out of the Central Foreign Policy File and treated as a distinct filing era", in archival analytics and Source Explorer, with NARA's page on the central files' eras as its reference. The lane was added after Tier 3 on the owner's word. Its specification was written first, from seven readers' reports, and the owner answered four questions on it (2026-10-02): the full split; it ships in build 49; the decimal numbers cited through the National Archives move to Central Decimal File; the collection records stay as they are and the help text explains them. Every other decision took the specification's default and is listed in the PR for review.

**What was measured.** Corpus `HistoryAtState/frus` at `8e5da08c1`, 553 manifest volumes. Two note grains: every `type="source"` element (269,242; `source-provenance-index.json`) and one note per document (264,552; `collection-usage-index.json`, Source Explorer, the packet, the live index).
- **The issue's premise does not hold in the data.** Of the 9,443 documents that cite the Subject-Numeric File, 22 were in the Central Foreign Policy File category. 3,844 were in Central Decimal File and 5,577 in Other NARA Collections, by how each note is worded: through the Department (`Department of State, Central Files, POL 27 VIET S` parses as `.centralFiles`), through the National Archives (`National Archives, RG 59, Central Files 1964–66, POL 27 VIET S` parses as `.naraCollection`), or with a remark naming the Central Foreign Policy File (`.cfpfFile`). At the source-element grain: 3,824, 5,468 and 5 of 9,297.
- **The control run.** Before any code change, both generators at the shipped `GENERATED_DATE` (2026-10-01) into scratch: each output byte-identical to the shipped file (`cmp`; SHA-256 `a0e3563a…` and `a57f3920…`).
- **The rule over the corpus**, by a scratch program linking the worktree's `SourceNoteKit` over the specification's two note files. It read every note exactly as the specification's probe did: 0 of 207,600 central-files-shaped parses differ at the source-element grain and 0 of 208,851 at the document grain.

| Central Decimal File | 194,243 → 190,767 | 194,206 → 190,718 (360 → 340 volumes) |
| Subject-Numeric File | 0 → 9,297 (104 volumes) | 0 → 9,443 (112 volumes) |

| Other NARA Collections | 10,179 → 4,363 | 10,551 → 4,618 |

**What changed.**
- **The rule** (`SourceNoteKit/CollectionKeying.swift`, 1.6). `centralFilesReading(parsed:note:)` reads the form of an RG 59 central-files citation — `.decimal` or `.subjectNumeric` — with what decided it and the file designation.   - Evidence, first that applies: the class key (letter-led is Subject-Numeric, digit-led decimal); a stored identifier or a segment after the anchor that opens with a handbook category or one of seven organization leads (`AID`, `UN`, `NATO`, `SEATO`, `CENTO`, `EEC`, `OECD`), in capitals or in title case of three or four letters; a block of years with both ends in 1964–1973, unless a later segment opens with `Entry`, `Records of` or `Lot`.

**Where the code departs from the specification, and why.**
- **Three more functions than the five it lists.** `centralFilesReading` returns the evidence and the lead beside the form, because the audit above needs them from the real code and not from a second implementation; `subjectNumericLead(ofCandidate:)` and `printedSubjectNumericBlock(inCitation:)` are public so their rules have tests of their own.
- **One of its fixtures contradicts its own rule.** It lists `…Central Files 1970–73, Inter-American Affairs.` as giving no form, to show that a five-letter title-case lead is refused. The lead is refused, and the block then decides: by rule 3 the note is Subject-Numeric, as a folder title under a 1970–73 block is. The tests pin both halves: the same note with no block gives no form, and with the block it is `.subjectNumeric` by `.block`.
- **The basis line follows the route.** The specification gives the new line to every citation worded through the National Archives that has a class key. 192 National-Archives-led Subject-Numeric notes (179 in `frus1964-68v34`, which prints "RG 59, Records of the Department of State, Central Files, 1964–66, …"), 173 of them with a class key, store a series that does not name the central files, so their neighbours come from the collection route. ### Landing (2026-10-02)

`origin/v2` was still `6ab2afc1`, the commit the lane was developed on, so there was no merge. The landing made one code change and two corrections, and ran the gates on the result.

**The Archival Neighbors empty state under the Subject-Numeric panel** (round 1 left it as owner copy; the session's orchestrator decided it is fixed here, with wording the owner can edit in review, because the screen contradicted itself). Both views printed "This source note doesn’t cite a recognized lot file, central file, or presidential library, so related documents can’t be matched" (`source.explorer.related.empty.unmatched`) under the panel that names the note's central file, whenever `supportsArchivalNeighbors` was false and the list was empty.

*When a Subject-Numeric citation gets no neighbours*, read from `IndexingPipeline.relatedDocuments`, `archivalNeighborsWithCohort`, `relatedByDecimal`, `relatedByDecimalClass` and `ParsedSourceNote.archivalNeighborKey`, and counted over the 264,552 document notes by a scratch program linking the worktree's `SourceNoteKit` (9,443 Subject-Numeric documents):
- **3,842 have a parse-level key** and already read "No other indexed documents cite this archival source" when the list is empty: 3,657 Department-led notes whose designation the parse stored (`relatedByDecimal`, on the stored file number), 182 National-Archives-led notes whose series does not name the central files (`relatedByCollection`), and 3 whose remark carries a film number. Unchanged.
- **4,083 have no parse-level key and are matched all the same**: worded through the National Archives, the stored series names the central files, and `SourceNoteParser.decimalClassLocation(inCitation:)` reads a class key, which `relatedByDecimalClass` matches against the stored `decimal_class`. `archivalNeighborKey` is nil for them by design, so an empty list read as "unmatched". 399 of them cite a class no other document in the corpus stores; the rest are empty only while the volumes that share the class are not indexed.
- **1,518 have nothing to match on**, and no arm of `relatedDocuments` serves them: 1,302 worded the same way with no class key (902 designations with no subject number, `POL FR-US`; 393 with one that the class grammar still refuses, `ORG 4–COMM`, `SP 1–1 US– USSR`; 7 that give only their block), 184 Department-led with no stored identifier (`AID (US) S VIET`), 3 Department-led with an identifier the file-number route cannot read (`POL/7 US/ Harriman`), 19 parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File, and 10 National-Archives-led notes whose parse kept no series (`RG 59 Central Files 1967–69, …`, no comma after the record group). Round 1's "about 1,500" is this figure. The collection authority's alias fallback can still fill a list for some of them, by collection name and not by file; that needs a live index and was not measured. (It no longer can: round 2, below.)
- **"A designation with no subject number cannot be matched" is not what the code does**, so no sentence says it: a Department-led `POL US–USSR` is stored and matched whole, and 393 designations that have a number are not matched.

*The fix.* `SourceExplorerView.relatedEmptyState(for:note:)` is the rule both views ask, static so a test drives it: a key gives `.noNeighbors`; a Subject-Numeric citation (`CollectionKeying.isSubjectNumericCitation`) with no key gives `.subjectNumericNoNeighbors` when the class route has a key and `.subjectNumericUnkeyed` when nothing does; any other note gives `.unmatched`. Each view's `relatedEmptyMessage` prints one sentence per state, the same key and text in both:
- `source.explorer.related.empty.subjectNumeric`: "This source note cites the Subject-Numeric File. No other indexed document was matched to the same file. Index more volumes to surface related documents."
- `source.explorer.related.empty.subjectNumeric.unkeyed`: "This source note cites the Subject-Numeric File, but not in a form the app can match on, so documents from the same file can’t be matched."

Two keys and not one, because only the first state changes when more volumes are indexed. The other two sentences are unchanged. EditableContent: two blocks added beside the unmatched one in `06-Archives.md` (267 blocks), 38 ranged blocks re-pointed, one Amendment-Log bullet. `Planning/Manual-Revisions-Pending.md`: one entry in the lane's section, for both manuals' Archival Neighbors paragraph, which says an empty list always means no other document cites the source.

*How it was verified.* iPhone 17, iOS 26.5 (`A36F4C02`), Xcode 27.0; every A/B by re-editing the file and writing the saved text back, never `git checkout`; `-only-testing FRUSExplorerTests/SubjectNumericExplorerTests` on both sides.
- **A/B.** With the rule answering as the screen did (a key gives `.noNeighbors`, anything else `.unmatched`) and both views' `relatedEmptyMessage` as on `c79ff1f4`: "✘ Test run with 16 tests in 1 suite failed after 0.107 seconds with 9 issues." — `emptyNeighbourStates` on each of its seven fixtures, and `bothTwinsSayWhyTheListIsEmpty` once per view. With the fix: "✔ Test run with 16 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.086 seconds." `otherEmptyStatesAreUnmoved` and the scan's own test, `emptySentenceScanReadsEachArm`, pass on both sides, by construction.
- **Eight mutants, one at a time**, each failing the test named for it: the series conjunct dropped (the note with no series, 1 issue); the class-key conjunct dropped (the three notes with no class key, 3); any parse with a class key (the no-series note and the Central Foreign Policy File note, 2); the Subject-Numeric guard dropped (`otherEmptyStatesAreUnmoved`, 2); the key test moved after the Subject-Numeric test (`otherEmptyStatesAreUnmoved`, 3); the two states traded (7); and two scan-only mutants with no rebuild, the Mac view handing the rule another note (1) and the iOS view printing the unmatched sentence for an unkeyed file (3).
- **Not looked at on a screen:** either new sentence. The by-eye list above has them in its Source Explorer item, and the plan of record's release list in its first.

### Landing, round 2 (2026-10-02)

Before the push the lane's build was looked at on an iPhone (iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`; five real volumes indexed by the app itself — `frus1961-63v03`, `frus1961-63v25`, `frus1964-68v01`, `frus1969-76v30`, `frus1969-76ve09p2`, 1,784 documents). It found five defects. This round fixes three, leaves two with their reasons, and corrects three slips in the documents. `origin/v2` was still `6ab2afc1`, so there was again no merge.

**What the pass saw and found right.** The Subject-Numeric panel on seven documents (Type, Record Group, File Designation, File Years — "1963" for `frus1961-63v25/d61`, whose note prints "1960–63" — the request note, the period row, one handbook link and the hint), with no catalog spinner and no key prompt on any. The decimal and Central Foreign Policy File panels, unchanged. The eleven-row period table in the NARA Lookup sheet. Eleven Provenance Types doors whose counts sum to the header's 264,552. The dashboard's legend, Categories menu ("Categories: 10 shown" after one is hidden), "eleven broad categories" and the caveat. The map's provenance legend and its caption ("86 of the 499 volumes"). Your Library's caption, whose 614 central-file notes are the index's 102 decimal, 434 Subject-Numeric and 78 Central Foreign Policy File rows. Both new empty-state sentences, each on a document that should have it.

**The five defects.**
1. **Archival Neighbors listed unrelated documents for a central-file document alone in its file.** `frus1964-68v01/d359` (`POL 13 VIET S`, the only document with that designation in the index) showed a count of 6: two decimal documents of `frus1961-63v25` and four 1973 documents of `frus1969-76ve09p2`. `frus1961-63v03/d10` (`751K.5/1-1163`) showed the same six under "Same decimal file — 751K.5, 1960–January 1963". So the landing's claim that a Department-led designation with no neighbour reads "No other indexed documents cite this archival source" was untrue on screen. Fixed.
2. **With a status banner showing, the eleventh Provenance Types door rests under it** and is visible only while a drag is held. Left: it is every list's last row, not this list's. See "Left".
3. **The provenance charts drew two categories alike that were not alike before.** Central Decimal File and Named File Series (6,343 notes) were the same blue; on `v2` the decimal file's twin was Foreign Archives (74 notes). Every category after the first had changed colour against `v2`. Fixed.
4. **Your Library's composition bar was a line one or two pixels high** at iPhone width. Fixed.
5. **`frus1969-76ve09p2/d84`'s footer reads "Matching archival source: CFPF film D760430"**, a film number from the note's remark. Left: it is the parser's whole-note Central Foreign Policy File test, already in the lane's out-of-scope list (426 notes).

**The charts' colours (3).** The four charts that colour by provenance category — Archival Sourcing's trend and composition, Your Library's composition and bands — gave Swift Charts a domain and no range, so each category took the default cycle's colour for its position. The cycle has seven colours, and the eleventh category sits second, so every later category moved one along. `SourceProvenanceCategory.chartColor` now states each colour and `View.provenanceCategoryColorScale()` applies the scale (`FRUSExplorer/SeriesAnalytics/SourceProvenanceDashboard.swift`, the one place); the four charts call it and state no scale of their own.
- **The ten older categories keep the colour `v2` drew them in**, by their position among the ten: Central Decimal File blue, Central Foreign Policy File green, Lot Files orange, Presidential Libraries purple, Other NARA Collections red, Intelligence Records teal, Named File Series yellow, Foreign Archives blue, Previously Published green, Other / Unclassified orange. The Subject-Numeric File is **brown**, which the cycle never uses. Brown and not indigo, pink or mint, which sit beside the cycle's blue and purple, its red, and its teal. The legend's order is still the enum's, the Subject-Numeric File second.
- **The cycle was measured, not taken from a document.** A chart with a domain and no range was drawn beside the named system colours and its pixels read (macOS 27.0, light and dark): blue, green, orange, purple, red, **teal**, yellow. The sixth is `Color.teal` (0, 195, 208), not `.cyan` (0, 192, 232). The first pass's screenshot of the iOS 26.4 simulator reads the same seven, and a `simctl` screenshot of this round's build reads those values back for the ten categories in `v2`'s order, with (172, 127, 94) for the new one.

**Archival Neighbors for a central-file document (1).** The cause, reproduced in a unit test through the real writer and query before anything was changed:
- When the direct route finds nothing, `archivalNeighborsWithCohort` resolves the note to a collection-authority record and matches the record's names against `series_name` (`aliasNeighbors`). A Department-led central-files citation with a class key resolves to the record "Central Files" (`txt:department of state|central file`, cited by 157 volumes), which the app's own help calls a filing system rather than a collection. `directKeys` gives a `.centralFiles` parse no record group, so the match is `relatedBySeriesName("Central Files")`: every row whose stored series is that name or begins with it and a comma, with no test of the file or the form. (The by-eye pass read the cause as `relatedByCollection(RG 59, "Central Files")`; that is the same match with a record-group clause, and it is the path of a National-Archives-led anchor, where the record's first name is skipped as the anchor's own series.)
- The rows it matches are the notes worded with a comma after the name: `National Archives, RG 59, Central Files, 1970–73, POL 23 Oman` parses with the series `Central Files`. On the unfixed code the test's anchor listed all five such documents with the basis "Central Files (collection authority)" and a cohort of 6.
- **The fix** is one rule at the one place the anchored path runs the fallback: `IndexingPipeline.aliasFallbackServes(_:note:)` refuses it for a `.centralFiles` parse and for any note `CollectionKeying.centralFilesReading` reads (a National-Archives-led RG 59 note; a note parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File that gives a Subject-Numeric designation). Every other note keeps the fallback as on `v2`: a lot file, a library collection, a named series, a record-group series, and a library-led note the parser read as the Central Foreign Policy File from its remark. Nothing stored changes, so there is no index version.
- **Every caller.** The fallback for a document runs only in `archivalNeighborsWithCohort`. `archivalNeighbors(forVolumeId:documentId:)` is a wrapper on it, and its callers are Source Explorer's inline list on iOS and on the Mac, the Archival Neighbors sheet and window for a document (`ArchivalNeighborsRequest.document`, `ArchivalNeighborsSheet.init(appState:docKey:)`), and Related Documents' archival generator (`SimilarityGenerators`, which calls the cohort form). So the count in the list's header, the list, the cohort chip and the Mac twin agree. `relatedDocuments(for:)`, the unanchored path, never ran the fallback. `archivalNeighborCounts(forKeys:)` leaves it out by its own documented decision and badges front-matter rows, not documents.
- **Measured** over the corpus's 264,552 document notes, by a scratch program linking the worktree's `SourceNoteKit` and reading the bundled authority (not a full index): 17,543 Department-led documents resolve to the "Central Files" record, and at least 998 of them are alone in their file (no other document stores the number before the slash; the route's year segments can only add to that). 71 documents in 23 volumes store a series that record's name matches, so on a full index each of those 998 would have listed 30 of the 71. Another 11 Department-led documents and 6 parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File resolve to a block's record (`Central Files 1967–69`, `1970–73`), whose name matches the National-Archives-led documents that spell the block that way (1,779 and 1,973 notes resolve to those two records). The rule refuses the fallback for 200,161 notes in all (194,206 `.centralFiles`, 5,933 National-Archives-led, 22 parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File).
- **The empty states are unmoved.** `relatedEmptyState(for:note:)` does not read the list, so no condition changed and `SubjectNumericExplorerTests` is as it was. What changed is that the sentences are now what a reader sees: `frus1964-68v01/d359` and `frus1961-63v03/d10` read "No other indexed documents cite this archival source. Index more volumes to surface related documents." with no count and no basis line, and no Subject-Numeric citation's list is filled from the authority. The landing left that unmeasured for the 1,518 documents with nothing to match on; it is now zero by the rule.
- **Not changed, and worth a look:** a volume's own Sources row "Central Files" still lists by that name (`archivalNeighbors(forLotFile:…)`, the front-matter path, where the row IS the filing system); and a National-Archives-led note whose stored series is `Records of the Department of State` still takes the direct series route (the 182 of the landing's count).

**Left.**

### Landing, round 3 (2026-10-02)

Before the push round 2's build was looked at a second time on an iPhone (iPhone 17, iOS 26.4, `3E028774`, the five volumes of the first pass), and `v2` was built and looked at beside it for the first time (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A9FCCA50`; the same five volumes, indexed by `v2`'s own code). The second pass found round 2's three fixes holding, and two things more. This round fixes one of them and the wording slip beside it, adds the control round 2's read-only check asked for, and records what is left. `origin/v2` was still `6ab2afc1`, so there was again no merge. It is the last fix round before the branch is pushed.

**Which of the first pass's five defects `v2` has, and which the lane caused.** Each is measured on the `v2` build's screens, not read from its code.
- **`v2` has three.** *The unrelated neighbours (1):* on `v2`, `frus1964-68v01/d359` shows a count of 6 and the same six documents, and `frus1961-63v03/d10` shows them under "Same decimal file — 751K.5, 1960–January 1963". `v2`'s index holds exactly six rows whose series is `Central Files` or begins with it and a comma, and one row in each of the two files. So round 2's gate removes a defect build 48 ships. *The banner (2):* on `v2` the tenth and last door, Other / Unclassified, rests under the "iCloud Account Issue" banner and shows only while a drag is held. *The hairline bar (4):* on `v2` Your Library's composition bar is one solid pixel row under a ten-entry legend; the lane's eleventh entry did not make it measurably thinner.
- **The lane caused two.** *The colour collision (3):* `v2` draws three pairs of categories alike, and the Central Decimal File's twin is Foreign Archives (74 notes). The lane's first build made the twin Named File Series (6,343 notes) and moved nine categories off their colour; round 2 put each back. *The chart's new holes (found by the second pass, fixed below):* `v2`'s trend chart has one white hole, where the Central Foreign Policy File's band begins. The lane's category added a larger one before 1960 and one after 1970.
- **Not compared:** `frus1969-76ve09p2/d84`'s footer (5) was not looked at on `v2`. The film number in it comes from the parser's whole-note test, which the lane did not change.

**What the second pass saw.** Round 2's fixes, on a device they had not been measured on: nothing listed and no count under `d359` and `d10`; the eleven legend entries in the stated colours on all four charts, Your Library's in dark too; the composition bar 28 points high. Its own controls still list their neighbours: a lot file (`frus1961-63v03/d105`, 25 under "Same lot file — 67 D 54", the index's 26 rows less the anchor) and a library collection (`frus1961-63v03/d19`, 12 under "Same collection — Kennedy Library"). It found:
- **White holes in "Archival provenance over time"**, the largest where the Subject-Numeric band begins. Fixed.
- **The same situation worded two ways** under Archival Neighbors. Fixed.
- **The "Central Files" collection page still presents the six documents** round 2 took out of every document's own list. Left; see "Left".

**The trend chart's holes.** Series analytics ▸ Archival Sourcing ▸ "Archival provenance over time" is a stacked area chart of each category's share of a decade's source notes.
- **The cause, confirmed in the code and by drawing the chart.** `SourceProvenanceData`'s share rows held a row only for a category with notes in the decade: the bundled `byDecade` counts omit zeros, and the unfiltered path skipped a zero count. The filtered path, which the second pass expected to be whole, skipped it too: it kept zero rows only for a decade the filter leaves with no shown notes at all (Session 3's review). Swift Charts draws a band between its own points and stacks the bands above it on what is present at each decade. So a band with no point in the decade before its first notes begins as a vertical edge, and the bands above it, already stacked on it at that decade and not at the one before, leave a white wedge between. The Subject-Numeric File has notes in the 1960s (6,842 of 24,456, 28%) and the 1970s only.
- **Measured.** The second pass's screenshot of round 2's build (`eye2/L27-sourcing-chart1.png`, 3 pixels a point): 238 of the stack's 583 pixel columns hold a background pixel between their first and last chart colour, the worst 92 of the plot's 342 rows (27%), just before 1960. The `v2` screenshot (`eye-v2/22-sourcing-chart1.png`): 173 of 583, the worst 36 of 406 rows (9%), under the Central Foreign Policy File's start. Both have more columns with a hole than the three wedges the pass named, because every category that is absent from a decade between two it has notes in leaves a sliver (Other NARA Collections has notes in the 1910s and the 1940s and none between).
- **The fix.** The share rows are dense: every shown category has a row in every decade, with a share of zero where it has no notes, on both paths (`SourceProvenanceData.init` and `shareByDecade(in:excluding:)`, `FRUSExplorer/SeriesAnalytics/SourceProvenanceData.swift`). A band now runs from zero and to zero, and the stack is closed. The chart itself is `SourceProvenanceDashboard.provenanceMixChart(_:domain:)`, static so a test draws the card's own chart. Over the bundled index the rows are 99 (nine decades of eleven categories) where they were 65.
- **What reads those rows, before and after.**
  - *The chart on screen:* holes before, none after.
  - *The exported figure:* the card hands the export the same closure it draws (`chartCard`'s `content`), so it had the holes and has none. Not exported and looked at.
  - *"View as table" and its CSV:* unchanged. `ChartInspectorAdapters.provenanceMixTable` lists `SourceProvenanceData.listed(_:)` of the rows it is handed: a zero share is left out unless every share of its decade is zero. Over the bundled index that is the 65 lines the table had, each with the share it had, and no "Subject-Numeric File, 1950, 0.0%". Under the category filter a decade with no shown notes keeps its 0.0% lines, as before. (A line that prints "0.0%" for a category WITH notes — Presidential Libraries in the 1910s, 4 of 32,043 — was there before and is there now.)
  - *VoiceOver's elements for the chart's marks:* the 34 zero rows are hidden from it (`.accessibilityHidden`), so it is given the 65 it was given. Pinned by a source scan; not heard.
  - *The Audio Graph descriptor* (`AXChartDescriptorModifier`, attached by the shared card): it reads the table's second column as its value, which for this table is the category's name and not a number, so the builder refuses and this chart had no descriptor before and has none now. Read in the code, not measured.
  - *The composition chart, the density chart and their tables:* they do not read the share rows. Unchanged.
  - *The subseries scope:* the scoped roll-up runs through the same initializer, so a scoped chart's rows are dense over the decades the scope has notes in; a decade with no in-scope notes has no rows, as before, and the dashboard's empty state (no rows at all) is reached exactly when it was.
  - *One case differs and no artifact has it:* a decade whose notes are all in categories this build does not know had no rows on the unfiltered path, and now has eleven zero rows, which the table lists.
- **After.** The card's chart, drawn in a test over the bundled index 700 points wide at 2×, has no background pixel inside its stack in any of 808 columns, with no category hidden and with Other / Unclassified hidden. On a screen (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A36F4C02`; `land3/eye3/09-sourcing-chart.png`): 0 of 583 columns. The brown band rises from zero at 1950 and falls to zero at 1980, and the table lists the 1900s with their three categories and no line for the other eight.

**One sentence per situation.** The second pass read two sentences for one situation. `frus1964-68v01/d359` (`Department of State, Central Files, POL 13 VIET S`) and `frus1969-76v30/d6` (`National Archives, RG 59, Central Files 1970–73, POL 14 GREECE`) are each the only document in their file on that index. The first read "No other indexed documents cite this archival source. Index more volumes to surface related documents." and the second "This source note cites the Subject-Numeric File. No other indexed document was matched to the same file. Index more volumes to surface related documents."
- **The cause.** `SourceExplorerView.relatedEmptyState(for:note:)` gave `.noNeighbors` to any note whose parse has a neighbour key before it asked whether the note cites the Subject-Numeric File. A Department-led designation the parse stored has a key (the stored file number, which `relatedByDecimal` matches); the same file cited through the National Archives has none, because its route reads the class key from the raw citation.
- **The rule now.** A Subject-Numeric citation whose key IS its file — a `.centralFiles` parse with a key — is `.subjectNumericNoNeighbors`, as the class route is. Each shape, with the sentence it prints when its list is empty:
  - *Department-led, a designation the parse stored* (`POL 13 VIET S`; `POL US–USSR`, with no subject number; `DEF 19–8 U.S.-IRAN`, with a stop in it): matched on the stored file number. **The Subject-Numeric sentence** ("…No other indexed document was matched to the same file…"); it was the generic one.
  - *National-Archives-led, a series that names the central files, and a class key* (`RG 59, Central Files 1970–73, POL 14 GREECE`): matched on the class key. The Subject-Numeric sentence, as before.
  - *National-Archives-led, a series that does not name the central files* (`RG 59, Records of the Department of State, Central Files, 1964–66, SCI 3 OECD`, `frus1964-68v34/d1`): matched by collection on that series, not on the file. The generic sentence, as before.
  - *Parsed as the Central Foreign Policy File, with a film number from a remark* (`frus1969-76ve09p2/d84`): matched on the film. The generic sentence, as before.
  - *Nothing to match on* (`POL FR-US` through the National Archives, `AID (US) S VIET` through the Department, a block alone): "…not in a form the app can match on…", as before.
  - *Not a Subject-Numeric citation:* its own two sentences, as before.
- **No string changes**, and the Mac view switches over the same rule, so both twins moved together.
- **Measured** over the corpus's 264,552 document notes by a scratch program linking the worktree's `SourceNoteKit`, with a copy of the rule (the rule is in the app target): 3,657 documents move from the generic sentence to the Subject-Numeric one — 3,623 designations with no stop in them and 34 with one — and no note that is not a Subject-Numeric citation moves. 185 Subject-Numeric citations keep the generic sentence (182 by series, 3 by film). Of the 9,443, 7,740 can now read the first Subject-Numeric sentence and 1,518 the second. These are the landing's own figures re-derived: its 3,842 keyed documents are the 3,657 and the 185.
- **On a screen** (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, `A36F4C02`; `frus1964-68v01` and `frus1969-76v30` copied in and indexed by the app; `land3/eye3/24-d359-se.png`, `28-v30d6-se.png`): both documents read the Subject-Numeric sentence.
- **What still differs between the two**, and is left: `d359` has the footer "Matching archival source: POL 13 VIET S" and `v30/d6` has none, because `ParsedSourceNote.archivalNeighborKey` is nil by design for the class route (the key is in the raw citation, not the parse). And the sentence says "was matched", which is what holds for both: the Department-led route finds Department-led documents of the file only (237 designations are cited both ways; one neighbour set per file is in the out-of-scope list above).

**The lot-file control.** Round 2's read-only check found that the alias fallback's gate has end-to-end controls for a library collection and a named series, and only rule-level fixtures for a lot file. `AliasFallbackCentralFilesTests.lotFileAliasFallbackIsUnmoved` is the third: `frus1947v07`'s wording of the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee's lot (`SWNCC Files, Lot 52M45`), alone in its lot on the test's index, still lists the document that cites `SWNCC Files` with no lot (22 source notes in five volumes are those two words and nothing else, six of them in `frus1945Berlinv02`), under the basis "SWNCC Files (collection authority)", and not the document of another lot. ## Session 2026-10-02 — The CloudKit schema gate's first read: fifteen fields Production never held, deployed in the twelfth promotion

The owner saved a CloudKit management token and ran `./Scripts/check_cloudkit_schema.py` for build 49. It failed.
- **The finding.** Fifteen identifiers the inventory attested as deployed were absent from Production: `CD_ArchiveVisitDocument.CD_stateData`, `CD_ArchiveVisitPlan.CD_deliverableTogglesData` and `.CD_inquiryText`, `CD_ArchiveVisitTarget.CD_stateData` and `.CD_userNote`, `CD_Collection.CD_introductionRichText`, `.CD_introductionText` and `.CD_subtitle`, `CD_CollectionEntry.CD_includeFootnotesOverride`, `.CD_includeRelatedDocuments`, `.CD_includeSourceNoteOverride` and `.CD_summaryPromptIdOverride`, `CD_DocumentHighlight.CD_noteId`, and `CD_SavedSearch.CD_dateRangeEnd` and `.CD_dateRangeStart`.
  - The first ten were in the inventory since it began (2026-07-26), the five Archive Visit fields since the eighth promotion (2026-08-26).
  - The raw `cktool export-schema` files for Production and Development were byte-identical (27,003 bytes) and held none of them. That is what a Development environment reset to Production looks like, so no deploy could have carried them.
  - A record saved with one of them set on a TestFlight build since then would have failed to upload (#1531's shape). Not measured on any device.
- **The fix.** The Development export plus the fifteen fields, each typed as the mirror types its analogues (`String`/`UUID` STRING QUERYABLE SEARCHABLE SORTABLE, `Data` BYTES QUERYABLE SORTABLE, `Bool` INT64 QUERYABLE SORTABLE, `Date` TIMESTAMP QUERYABLE SORTABLE; all fifteen are optional with no external storage).
  - `cktool validate-schema` passed, and the owner ran `cktool import-schema` into Development.
  - The gate read against Development then passed. The owner deployed to Production, and the gate's read against Production passed: 268 required identifiers held, 310 in all. It wrote the stamp the archive phase reads in the main checkout.
- **The record.** `CloudKitSchemaInventory` 2.0 records the twelfth promotion; `deployedThroughBuild` 48 → 49 and `deployedOn` → 2026-10-02. The baseline count and digest do not move.
- **Not done:** no device check that the records which failed before now upload.

## Session 2026-10-04 — TEIHeaderKit, SemanticVectorsKit and FTS5Store compile on Linux behind `canImport` guards, and Apple platforms compile what they did before

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`), the self-hosted web edition, compiles this repository's kits on Linux from a pinned submodule. Today it compiles SourceNoteKit, CrossRefKit, GeneratorKit and four pure-Swift files of FTS5Store. It is meant to compile these three kits as well, and they did not build on Linux. The owner lifted the hold on that project's pull requests here on 2026-10-04, and this is its first. Branched from `v2` @ `34a51205`. Guards only, and one named Linux skip: nothing changes on an Apple platform.

**What failed on Linux** (`swift:6.4-noble`, arm64, at `34a51205`)
- TEIHeaderKit: "'XMLParser' is unavailable: This type has moved to the FoundationXML module. Import that module to use it." (`TEIHeaderParser.swift:162`, `:209`, `:214`, `:292`), and "cannot find type 'XMLParserDelegate' in scope" (`:98`).
- SemanticVectorsKit: "no such module 'CryptoKit'" (`SemanticVectorsArtifacts.swift:15`).
- FTS5Store: "no such module 'SQLite3'" (`FTS5Connection.swift:10`); with that file guarded, "no such module 'OSLog'" (`FTS5Store.swift:10`). Seven FTS5StoreTests files import SQLite3.
- ManifestGeneratorCore, whose test target also holds TEIHeaderKit's tests (`TEIHeaderParserTests.swift`): "'URLSession' is unavailable: This type has moved to the FoundationNetworking module. Import that module to use it." (`GitHubClient.swift:44`, `TEIHeaderFetcher.swift:49`). swift-corelibs-foundation has no `URLSession.bytes(for:)` either.

**Changed**
- **Imports.** Each is inside `#if canImport`, and on an Apple platform each guard selects the import that was there before: SQLite3, else `CSQLite` (`FTS5Connection`, `FTS5Store`, `FTS5Vocabulary` and the seven test files); OSLog (`FTS5Store`); CryptoKit, else swift-crypto's `Crypto` (`SemanticVectorsArtifacts`). `FoundationXML` (`TEIHeaderParser`) and `FoundationNetworking` (`GitHubClient`, `TEIHeaderFetcher`) are imported only where they exist, which is not on an Apple platform, since Apple's Foundation holds those types itself.
- **`TEIHeaderFetcher.fetch`.** Its guard tests the Linux module first. Under `#if canImport(FoundationNetworking)` it reads the response whole with `data(for:)` and replays its bytes into the unchanged `</teiHeader>` scan. Apple platforms take the `#else`, which still streams with `bytes(for:)`.
- **`FTS5Store/LinuxLogger.swift`, new:** an `os.Logger` stand-in with the same call shape, `privacy:` interpolation included, that writes `[level] category: message` to standard error. All of it is inside `#if !canImport(OSLog)`. `xcodegen generate` put it in both app targets, the 6 lines of `project.pbxproj` it added and nothing else; the schemes were restored.
- **One named Linux skip.** FTS5StoreTests' "Database file has isExcludedFromBackupKey set after creation" is `.enabled(if: platformKeepsBackupExclusion, …)`. The constant is true under `canImport(Darwin)`. The trait itself sits outside any guard, and on Apple platforms it is true, so the test runs there as before. On Linux it skips with its reason, "Linux: swift-corelibs-foundation keeps no backup attribute, so excluding a file from backup is a silent no-op". Measured in the container: `setResourceValue(true, forKey: .isExcludedFromBackupKey)` throws nothing, and reading the key back gives nil.
- Version-history entries in the eleven touched files that carry a block. `Package.swift` is unchanged. FRUS Explorer Light is to declare `Crypto` and `CSQLite`, for Linux only, in its own package, in the pull request there that moves its pin.

**Apple platforms: nothing changes, and how that was checked**

## Session 2026-10-04 — The kit-boundary audit reads a name only where it can mean the app's declaration, so a change to the app alone cannot fail it

#1569's `FRUSCoreKitBoundaryTests` flagged every identifier on a kit code line that equalled the name of any non-private top-level declaration under `FRUSExplorer/`, and its suite check did the same against the app's and the test target's other files. So a session that only added, in an app or test file, a top-level declaration whose name the kit uses for something of its own (a local, a member, an argument label, a parameter, a nested type) would fail the audit without touching the kit. FRUS Explorer Light's sessions carry the coordination with the web edition, and an app-only change must not trip on it. Found in review after #1569 merged.

**Changed**
- **Both name checks** now go through `nameUses(in:among:except:where:)`, which skips a member right after a `.` (`IndexingPipeline.self` is still read), a name followed by `:` directly inside parentheses (an argument label or parameter, with brackets followed across lines), and every name the scanned code declares for itself (`declaredNames(in:)`: declarations at any depth, generic parameters, parameter labels and names, and what a for-in, a closure's parameter list or a tuple binding binds). The doc comment says what the checks skip, what they cannot see because of it, and that a Foundation or standard-library name the kit uses (`URL`, `max`) still reads as the app's once the app declares it, which renaming the app's declaration fixes. Two fixture tests pin the declared names and the rule: the suite has 12 tests.
- **`CLAUDE.md`.** The FRUSCoreKit entry names what #1569 made public and says the kit's other `public` declarations (348 of its 374) were already `public` in the app, so `public` alone does not mark what the web edition uses. The gate paragraph describes the narrowed name checks.

**Checked**
- **iOS 27.0**, a new iPhone 17 simulator, unsigned: `build-for-testing` "** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **", the two known residues only. The boundary and coding-standards audits: "✔ Test run with 75 tests in 2 suites passed after 63.784 seconds." The full unit target, run as for #1569: "✘ Test run with 6486 tests in 763 suites failed after 398.148 seconds with 8 issues." The 8 are the Keychain `.securityError(-34018)` failures an unsigned build also gives on `v2`, and the 19 skips (17 tests, 2 suites) are `v2`'s.
- **Mutated.** `import SwiftUI`, `IndexingPipeline`, `UserDefaults.standard` and the app's `frusSubseries(from:)` in `FRUSCanonicalURL.swift`, an unguarded file under `FRUSCoreKit/Linux/`, and `IndexingPipeline` and `makeTestPipeline` outside the guards in `ReaderRenderingTests.swift` failed the audit, each named with its file and line. Ten top-level declarations planted in `SupportingViews.swift` and `IndexingPipelineTests.swift`, each named after a local, a member, an argument label, a parameter, a nested type, a closure's parameter or a loop variable of the kit's or its suites', left it green, where the matching it replaces read them as 29 sites in the kit and 87 in the suites.
- **`swift build --target FRUSCoreKit`** "Build complete!", no warnings; `swift test --filter FRUSCoreKitTests` "✔ Test run with 393 tests in 49 suites passed".

**Owed by the owner:** run the boundary suite and the full unit target from a clone at a real path, then merge.

## Session 2026-10-04 — FRUSCoreKit, part 2: the indexing pipeline and the search service are kit code that builds and passes on Linux, and the app compiles the same files

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`), the self-hosted web edition, compiles this repository's kits on Linux from a pinned submodule; #1569 made `FRUSCoreKit` its reader's and Cite's library. Its index and search checks need the indexing pipeline and the search service, which lived in `FRUSExplorer/Search/` and read the app's bundle, its settings and Spotlight. This is part 2's first pull request; the citation matcher, the block splitter and `PageRangeStore` follow in a second.

**Changed**
- **Moves.** Fourteen files by `git mv`, with no line changed in the first commit: `Search/` `IndexingPipeline`, `SearchService`, `KWICLine`, `PersonClusterer`, `ResultSetFacets`, `DecimalFileSegment` and `IndexingStateTracker`; `Chronology/ChronologyModels`; `Models/` `DocumentKey`, `PersonMentionStore` and `PersonAuthorityIndex`; `Browser/VolumeSubjectProfiles`; and, renamed so a loader of the old name stays in the app, `RelatedDocuments/DocumentSubjectIndex.swift` and `Analytics/DecimalClassLabelTable.swift`. Fourteen Foundation-only value types moved verbatim into six new kit files, out of three `@Model` files, a SwiftUI file, `SearchModels.swift` (whose defaults read `UserDefaults`) and `SimilarityModel.swift` (whose protocols name `AppState`): `SearchParameters.swift` (`DocumentTypeFilter`, `PersonRollupAnchor`, `SearchParameters`, `SearchResult` and the four indexing progress types), `PersonClusterOverrideData`, `DocumentClassificationOverrideData`, `AnnotationReviewData`, `WordCloudDocumentKey` and `CandidateRecord`. The kit goes from 10,183 lines in 18 files to 29,219 in 40.
- **The seams** (`FRUSCoreKit/Search/IndexingSeams.swift`). `IndexingResources`: the four data files that change what an index holds (person authority, document subjects, decimal-class labels, broken references) and the collection authority's alias fallback, as providers asked on first use; `.none`; and `loading(fromDirectory:)`, which refuses a folder lacking one of the four. `IndexingStampStore`, whose requirements are `UserDefaults`' own methods, and `InMemoryIndexingStampStore`. `IndexedDocumentDonor` and `DonatedDocument`. `runPostIndexPasses(overrides:afterRollupRebuild:)`: the rollup, the broken-reference flags and the subjects, in the order the app's launch runs them, each a call of its own into the actor (`nonisolated`), so work queued on the pipeline runs between passes, as it did between the launch's three calls.
- **The pipeline** takes `resources:`, `defaults:` (now a stamp store) and `donor:`. The FTS-schema and broken-refs stamps go to `defaults`, as the date-index and rollup stamps did; the app passes `.standard`, so no stamp moves. The memory-warning observer names UIApplication's notification by its string, which a test pins. The internal `donatedDocuments(afterRowId:limit:)` holds the Spotlight rebuild's keyset SQL. The app's half is in `FRUSExplorer/Search/IndexingPipeline+App.swift`: the initialiser every call site uses, with the old signature, passing `IndexingResources.bundled` (the existing lazy stores, so each decode keeps its first-use timing), `UserDefaults` and `SpotlightDonor`; `extension UserDefaults: IndexingStampStore {}`; the Spotlight section, verbatim but for the page reader; and `updateSummary(_:)`.
- **Elsewhere.** `IndexingStateTracker` keeps its sentinel in a stamp store (`init(store:)`; `init(userDefaults:)` stays in the app). `SearchService` reads the subject index through `pipeline.resources`; its collocation measure moved to the app's `SearchService+Collocation.swift`, so `pipeline` and `positiveTerms(from:)` are internal. The four bundle loaders moved to app files of their names. `DecimalFileSegment.isDecimalFileNumber(_:)` is the kit's, and `NARACatalogClient`'s forwards to it. The pipeline names `FRUSURLScheme.resolveCrossRefTarget`. `DateRange` has a public initialiser, so a search's date filter can be built outside the kit. The app's three launch branches call `runPostIndexPasses`, publishing a rebuilt rollup from its callback, between the rollup and the next pass as before.
- **Linux.** Imports behind `canImport`: CryptoKit (else swift-crypto's `Crypto`), OSLog, SQLite3 (else `CSQLite`), FTS5Store and SourceNoteKit. `Linux/LinuxOSLogShims.swift`, a copy of FTS5Store's `LinuxLogger.swift`, whose declarations are internal to that module.
- **`Package.swift`.** `FRUSCoreKit` depends on FTS5Store and links sqlite3; `FRUSCoreKitTests` depends on FTS5Store and SourceNoteKit. Still 39 library targets, 31 executables and 38 test targets. `project.yml`'s build settings are unchanged; its comments on the kit say what it now holds.

## Session 2026-10-05 — FRUS Explorer Light can open the exported index read-only, name its own figure addresses, and serve the reader's page, which is kit code the app forwards to with the same bytes

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`) serves the Mac's exported index read-only and immutable. Its search, browse and reader endpoints need three things the kit did not have. Every kit opener wrote to the file it opened: it switched the file to WAL and ran the schema set-up's clean-up writes. A browser cannot load `frusexplorer://figure/` images. And the reader's page, `HTMLTemplate`, imported SwiftUI for one colour-scheme parameter. This pull request adds the first two to the kit and moves the third. Nothing the app shows changes.

**Changed**
- **Read-only opens.** `FTS5Store(readingDatabaseAt:schema:)` and `IndexingPipeline(readingIndexAt:fts5Store:resources:volumesDirectory:)` open with `?mode=ro&immutable=1` (`FTS5Store.immutableURI(for:)`).
  - They set only the pragmas that shape reading: busy timeout, temporary tables in memory, page cache and memory map. They never set the journal mode.
  - They skip the schema set-up, its migrations and clean-up writes, the cached `document_cache` upsert and the iOS memory observer. `frus_exact_word` is still registered.
  - The store refuses another schema generation or a missing table with `FTS5Error.openFailed`. SQLite refuses every write.
  - `isReadOnly` says which open a pipeline had.
  - The public initialiser every caller uses now delegates to a private one with `readOnly: false`, which runs its statements as before and in the same order.
- **A host's figure addresses.**
  - `FigureImages.linked(url:)` writes the reader's figure markup with the host's address for each image; `FRUSRenderNodeHTMLSerializer.reader(figureURL:)` is the reader's serializer with it, and `.reader` is unchanged.
  - `FRUSURLScheme.figureHost`, `figureURL(for:)` and `isSafeComponent(_:)` are public.
- **The reader's page is kit code.** `FRUSCoreKit/TEI/ReaderPage.swift` holds the page around the fragment, `documentCSS` and `figureCSS` (moved verbatim), and `cssVariables(appearance:textSize:)`, moved from `FRUSTheme`.
  - `ReaderAppearance` (light, dark) replaces `ColorScheme` there. `TextSizePreference` moves into the kit under its name.
  - `ReaderPage.build` takes the serializer (`.reader` by default) and a host's head markup, which by default adds nothing.
  - `HTMLTemplate.build(model:colorScheme:textSize:)`, `documentCSS`, `figureCSS` and `FRUSTheme.cssVariables(colorScheme:textSize:)` forward to it, so every caller compiles unchanged.
- **Tests**, under both compilers:
  - **IndexReadOnlyOpenTests:**
    - an index built read-write and copied out of WAL mode, opened read-only, answers nine queries exactly as before (results with score bits, counts, expressions, `=exact`, two refusals) and browses;
    - it refuses a write, and its folder keeps the same bytes and nothing beside them;
    - unreadable files are refused.
  - **ReaderPageTests:**
    - the page before its fragment has, for both palettes at all four sizes, the SHA-256 that `HTMLTemplate.build` wrote on `v2` before the move;
    - a host's head and serializer reach the page;
    - in Xcode, the app's names equal the kit's.
  - **Existing suites:** the figure test's page check now runs under `swift test` too.
  - **Count:** FRUSCoreKitTests goes from 878 tests in 116 suites to 884 in 118.
- **Docs.** `CLAUDE.md` (the TEI row, and what was made public for the web edition), version-history lines, and a note where `TextSizePreference` was. No editable-content block moves. The kit goes from 31,887 lines in 47 files to 32,684 in 49.

**Apple platforms: nothing changes, and how that was checked**
- **`FRUSExplorerMac`**, clean, unsigned Debug, beside `v2` @ `f69b4a0a` built the same way: "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **" both, with the same five warning lines. The debug dylibs define 233,941 and 233,858 unique symbols.
- **The symbol diff** (normalized as for #1573 and #1574): 14 removed, 92 added.
  - **Removed:** `HTMLTemplate.documentCSS` and `figureCSS` as stored constants (now forwarders); `IndexingPipeline.init`'s initialising entry, its closures and its allocating method descriptor, now the private initialiser's; `FRUSTheme.cssVariables`' inner `px`; and the `FigureImages` payload metadata the new case reshapes.
  - **Added:**
    - the read-only initialisers of `FTS5Connection`, `FTS5Store` and `IndexingPipeline`, and the private one;
    - `isReadOnly`, `immutableURI(for:)` and `reader(figureURL:)`;
    - `ReaderPage` and `ReaderAppearance`, with `ReaderAppearance(_:)`;
    - their metadata and witnesses.
- **iOS 27.0**, an iPhone 17 simulator, unsigned:
  - a clean `build-for-testing` of `FRUSExplorer`, "** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **" in 271 s, with the 7 known warning lines;
  - the full unit target, the app removed first, with `TEST_RUNNER_FRUS_TEI_MIRROR`: "✘ Test run with 6505 tests in 767 suites failed after 431.863 seconds with 8 issues." `v2` (#1574's head) ran 6498 tests in 765 suites the same way, with the same 8 issues;
  - the 7 more tests are the two new suites', one of them Xcode only. The 8 are the Keychain tests an unsigned build fails (-34018). Both runs skip the same 17 tests and 2 suites.
- **`swift test`, whole, on the macOS host:** exit 0; 38 runs, 2,547 tests, all passed, none skipped (`FRUSCoreKitTests` 884).
- **The reader's HTML and the search expressions.** FRUS Explorer Light's `tools/mac-golden`, which compiles the whole app module, built against this branch. It wrote all 392 fixture rows' HTML and all 482 queries' expressions byte-identical to its golden files; only their provenance changed.

## Session 2026-10-06 — The reader's page meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and marks its links by more than colour

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`) serves the page `ReaderPage` writes, and its axe check found two failures in it, `color-contrast` in the light reader and `link-in-text-block` in the dark one, which it keeps on a known list until this lands. Three of the page's text colours were under 4.5:1, WCAG's minimum for small text, which is all the reader's text: the light accent (4.02:1 on the page, 3.52:1 in an editorial note) and the dark accent in an editorial note (3.97); the teal of person links, one colour in both palettes (3.67 and 3.22 light, 4.63 and 3.94 dark); and the light secondary (3.98 and 3.87). And person and cross-reference links differed from the text around them by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1, axe's `link-in-text-block`).

**Changed**
- **The palette** (`ReaderPage.cssVariables`). Light: accent `rgb(0,122,255)` → `rgb(0,102,204)`, person names `rgb(0,150,136)` → `rgb(0,121,107)`, secondary 50% → 60% black. Dark: accent `rgb(10,132,255)` → `rgb(64,156,255)`, person names `rgb(0,150,136)` → `rgb(0,179,161)`. Every text colour is now at least 4.5:1 against the page and against the editorial note's tint laid over it, in both palettes: the lowest is the light person-name teal in an editorial note, 4.66. The dark secondary, the body and footnote text, the backgrounds, the editorial tint and border and the table border are unchanged. The comment above each changed colour gives its ratios before and after, and the doc comment states the rule.
- **The links** (`ReaderPage.documentCSS`). `a.pers-name` and `a.cross-ref` are underlined, at the font's own thickness and 0.15em below the baseline, and the underline thickens to 0.125em on hover, where it used to appear. A gloss keeps its dotted rule, and a broken reference its dotted rule and mark. Against the body text, the dark links were already under 3:1 (the cross-reference blue 2.86, the person-name teal 2.88), which is why axe flagged the dark reader and not the light one (blue 3.76, teal 4.11). Darkening the light links for 4.5:1 brought them under 3:1 as well (blue 2.71, teal 2.84), so colour alone could no longer mark them in either palette.
- **Where it shows:** the reader on every platform; printing from the Mac reader (File ▸ Print, M-14), which prints the reader's own web view under a stylesheet with no print rules, so the underlines and the darker colours reach the paper (iOS has no print command); the collection HTML export and its preview, which embed the same variables (light) and stylesheet; and FRUS Explorer Light. The PDF and Word exports draw their own text and do not change. No other CSS or HTML in the app or the kits names these colours: outside completed planning mock-ups the old values occur nowhere else, and the variables are read only by this stylesheet and the two embeds.
- **Tests** (`ReaderPageTests`, under both compilers):
  - the eight head pins are re-taken, and their comment says why. Each head grew by 519 bytes, the link rules and their comment, since each new colour is as long as the old. With the five colours and the link rules put back, all eight heads hash to #1575's pins, so nothing else in the head moved;
  - the contrast arithmetic, WCAG 2.2's relative luminance and ratio written in the suite, gives WCAG's figures (21:1, 1:1, #767676 passing and #777777 failing on white) and fails the light palette this replaces;
  - every text colour is at least 4.5:1 against the page and the editorial tint in both palettes, each alpha colour composited over the ground it is drawn on; and the stylesheet draws text in those five variables and no others;
  - `a.pers-name` and `a.cross-ref` are underlined with the quiet underline and thicken on hover; a gloss and a broken reference keep their dotted rules;
  - FRUSCoreKitTests goes from 884 tests in 118 suites to 887 in 118. No other test pins the page's bytes or these strings; the collection HTML test compares against `embeddedCSS` itself.
- FRUS Explorer Light's golden files are the reader's fragments, the body alone, so they do not change.

**How it was checked**
- **`FRUSExplorerMac`**, clean, unsigned Debug: "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **", with the five known warning lines.
- **iOS 27.0**, an iPhone 17e simulator (a parallel session had the iPhone 17), unsigned:

Run five times each on the same simulator, `FigureReaderTests` recorded that same failure once on `v2` (identical figures) and one failure of its sibling, "A late image does not bring the reader back…", on this branch: the two are timing-sensitive, and an underline moves no layout.

## Session 2026-10-06 — FRUS Explorer Light can read the reader's links with the app's own parse and open the page-range and person stores immutable, and the app's link handler dispatches what the kit reads with the same calls

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`) serves the Mac's exported index read-only. Its reader (its S9b) follows the links inside a document: `doc/` navigates, `person/` and `gloss/` open cards, and `brokenref/` opens the Unresolved Reference sheet. Two things it needs were not in the kit. The parse that reads a `frusexplorer://` href back into a ref or target lived only in the app's `FRUSURLSchemeHandler.dispatch(url:)`, a WebKit file, with a decoding rule of its own. And `PageRangeStore` and `PersonMentionStore`, which answer a page link and the cards, opened the file by its path, where #1575's other opens read it with `?mode=ro&immutable=1`. Nothing the app shows changes.

**Changed**
- **The link parse is kit code.** `FRUSURLScheme.readerLink(from:)` returns a `ReaderLink` (`person(ref:)`, `gloss(ref:)`, `crossReference(target:volumeId:citing:)`, `brokenReference(target:)`). It is `dispatch`'s parse, moved verbatim:
  - a `person`, `gloss` or `doc` path component is percent-decoded twice (Foundation's `pathComponents`, then `removingPercentEncoding`) and a `brokenref` component once, as before, and the doc comment says why;
  - it returns `nil` for another scheme, another host (a `figure` URL included) or a `doc` or `brokenref` link with no path. A `person` or `gloss` link with no path names the empty ref, which `dispatch` looked up and the app answers as not found;
  - `citing` is `nil` when the query names no hint, as `PageCitationHint(queryItems:)` returned it to `dispatch`.
- **The handler forwards.** `dispatch(url:)` switches on what the kit reads and keeps its lookups and callbacks. The navigation delegate passes only `frusexplorer` URLs, and for those every call is the one it made.
- **Immutable opens.** `PageRangeStore(readingDatabaseAt:)` and `PersonMentionStore(readingDatabaseAt:)` open `FTS5Store.immutableURI(for:)` with `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_URI` and each store's own mutex flag (`NOMUTEX`, `FULLMUTEX`).
  - They set only the busy timeout, create nothing, and refuse a missing file with each store's `databaseOpenFailed`. `isImmutable` says which open a store had.
  - The existing initialisers delegate to a private shared body and open as before. `PageRangeStore`'s failed open now closes the handle SQLite allocates, and its unused private `openDatabase()` is gone.
  - `resultCode(executing:)`, internal, lets a test show that a connection refuses a write: neither store has a method that writes.
- **Tests**, under both compilers unless marked:
  - **ReaderLinkTests** (new): 31 hrefs as the serializer writes them, each to the `ReaderLink` it names or to `nil`; every link the reader's serializer writes for 14 nodes reads back to its ref or target; a ref's own `%` escape is decoded twice and a dead target's once. In Xcode only, the app's handler makes, for every `frusexplorer` href in the table, the call `v2`'s `dispatch` made, with six lookups found.
  - **IndexReadOnlyOpenTests:** over an index of a volume with persons, terms, mentions, a rollup and two documents beginning on one page, the immutable stores:
    - answer 17 page questions and 19 person and term questions exactly as the app's opens do;
    - refuse three writes with `SQLITE_READONLY`, and leave the folder holding the same bytes and nothing beside them;
    - read while another connection holds the file's exclusive lock, which keeps the app's open out (the control waits out its 5 s busy timeout);
    - refuse a missing file, and make none.
  - **Existing suites:** `ExternalRefTargetRoundTripTests` parses with `readerLink(from:)`, where it kept a copy of `dispatch`'s parse; the figure video test checks its link under `swift test` too; `DeepLinkRouteTests` (Xcode) reads the renderer's host switch where it moved and checks that each in-app host names a link.
  - **Mutated:** seven mutants, each run against the four suites: either immutable open made plain, `brokenref` decoded twice, `person` decoded once, an empty `person` path read as `nil`, the query ignored, the scheme unchecked. Each failed at least one of the new tests.
  - **Count:** FRUSCoreKitTests goes from 884 tests in 118 suites to 891 in 119.
- **Docs.** `CLAUDE.md` (the FRUSCoreKit entry's public names for the web edition) and version-history lines. No editable-content block moves. The kit goes from 32,684 lines in 49 files to 32,826 in 49.

**Apple platforms: nothing changes, and how that was checked**
- **`FRUSExplorerMac`**, clean, unsigned Debug, beside `v2` @ `101e17d7` built the same way: "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **" both, with the same five warning lines. The debug dylibs define 233,982 and 233,941 unique symbols.
- **The symbol diff** (normalized as for #1573–#1575): 10 removed, 51 added.
  - **Removed:** the two stores' `init(databaseURL:)` initialising entries and allocating method descriptors (and `PersonMentionStore`'s error-message closure), now the private initialisers'; `PageRangeStore.openDatabase()` and its descriptor; and `dispatch(url:)`'s three path closures.
  - **Added:** each store's private `init(databaseURL:immutable:)` with its entries and descriptor, `init(readingDatabaseAt:)`, `isImmutable` and `resultCode(executing:)`; `FRUSURLScheme.readerLink(from:)` with the two path closures; and `ReaderLink`, with its metadata, value witnesses and `Equatable` conformance.
- **iOS 27.0**, an iPhone 17 simulator, unsigned:
  - a clean `build-for-testing` of `FRUSExplorer`, "** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **", with the 7 known warning lines, as on `v2`;
  - the full unit target, the app removed first, with `TEST_RUNNER_FRUS_TEI_MIRROR`: "✘ Test run with 6513 tests in 768 suites failed after 463.814 seconds with 8 issues." `v2` @ `101e17d7`, run the same way on the same simulator: "6505 tests in 767 suites … with 9 issues";
  - the 8 more tests are the new suite's 4 (one Xcode only) and `IndexReadOnlyOpenTests`' 4. The 8 issues on both are the Keychain tests an unsigned build fails (-34018). `v2`'s ninth is the late-image reader test, which flakes on a cold simulator (#1568) and passed alone. Both runs skip the same 17 tests and 2 suites.
- **`swift test`, whole, on the macOS host:** exit 0; 38 runs, 2,554 tests, all passed, none skipped (`FRUSCoreKitTests` 891).

**Linux** (Docker Desktop, `swift:6.4-noble` on arm64)
- FRUS Explorer Light's package at its `main` (`a506099`), with this branch copied over its submodule: "✔ Test run with 891 tests in 119 suites passed", none skipped.

**Owed by the owner:** Mac check 3 for this pull request (FRUS Explorer Light's plan), from a clone at a real path; then the merge. FRUS Explorer Light's pin move follows.

**Not done:**
- A `.volume` `CrossRefDestination` case. `resolveCrossRefTarget` reads a target that names a whole volume (`frus1961-63v05`) as a document of that name in the volume being read. FRUS Explorer Light's golden HTML holds 41 such links, 39 of them in `frus1961-63v06` and 2 in `frus1969-76ve09p1`'s preface. A `.volume` case changes what a tap does in the app, so it is left for a pull request of its own.

## Session 2026-10-08 — On paper, person and cross-reference links print without their underline, and the open questions of #1578 and #1579 are settled

#1578 underlined person and cross-reference links in the reader and left four questions for the owner, and #1579 three. The owner answered them on 2026-10-08. One answer changes the app.

**Decided by the owner**
- **The colours stand.**
- **Underlines do not belong on paper.** A printed document underlines what its writer underlined, so an underlined name on paper reads as the source's emphasis.
- **An empty person or term reference still reads as "not found"** (`frusexplorer://person/`), the reader's link scheme check stays exact, and the `resultCode(executing:)` test hook on the two read-only stores stays.

The links keep their colour, and the screen is unchanged. The rule reaches the Mac's File ▸ Print, which prints the reader's own web view, and a collection's HTML export when a browser prints it, since the export embeds the same stylesheet. A gloss's dotted rule and a broken reference's are not underlines and print as before.

- **A mutant:** with the rule moved out of `@media print`, the screen's underline test fails (2 issues), and so do the print test and the pins.
- **In WebKit itself.** A page with one person link and one cross-reference was printed to PDF through `WKWebView.printOperation(with:)`, the call `MacDocumentView.printCurrentDocument` makes, with and without the block, and each PDF's first page was rasterised at 4× and scanned for the longest horizontal run of link-coloured pixels. Both pages were also looked at.
- `swift test`: exit 0, 38 "Test run with" lines, 2,558 tests (one more than `f384d2d5`'s 2,557), no ✘ line.
