## Session 2026-10-10 — A search result's menu adds its document to a collection, and the bulk add a selection will use is in place (#1576 lane 2)

Lane 2 of the implementation plan on #1576 (bulk actions on search results), after lane 1 merged as #1627. No index version, no CloudKit deploy, no re-index, no shared kit file, and no `@Model` or stored property added.

**What a reader gets**
- **Add to Collection… on a result row**, without opening the document: touch and hold a result on iPhone or iPad, right-click it on the Mac. It opens the collection picker the document view already uses.
- **A document the collection already holds is not added again** (the owner's decision 3). The picker shows its checkmark and closes, and the collection's count stays as it was. An excerpt of the same document does not count as the document.
- On iPhone and iPad VoiceOver has the same command among a row's actions. On the Mac it reaches the command through the row's menu, as it does every other.
- **Three changes to the picker in every mode**, a document's own Add to Collection and Add Excerpt included. A row takes a tap anywhere on it, where it took one only on its name and caption. The list keeps the order it opened in while it is open. And one presentation adds once: a second tap before the sheet closes does nothing.

**How** (`CollectionDocumentAppend.swift`, `BulkResultRequest.swift`, `CollectionPickerSheet.swift`, both search views)
- `CollectionDocumentDiscovery.appendDocuments(_:to:modelContext:)` refuses a smart collection and a list over 1,000 documents (`bulkDocumentLimit`, decision 5) before writing anything; treats a document named twice as one; skips a document that already has a `.document` entry among the collection's live entries; adds the rest in the order given through the editor's own `appendEntries`, so they take one `nextSortOrder` and are linked by the inverse; sets `lastModified`; and saves once, itself. With nothing to add it writes nothing. A save that fails adds nothing: the entries are unlinked and deleted and the stamp is put back before the error is thrown. It answers with the ids of the entries it inserted, which lane 3's Undo will re-fetch, and how many documents were already there.
- `BulkResultRequest` is the command and its documents, frozen in the order on screen when the command is chosen, and whether a Meaning search listed them. It holds each document once and cannot be empty. `bulkResultSheets(_:)` presents the sheet with `.sheet(item:)` on that value, so each host holds a request and mounts one modifier, and neither builds the picker from whatever is on screen when the sheet opens (#862).
- `CollectionPickerSheet` gains a documents mode, `init(documents:fromMeaningSearch:)`. The two older modes keep their initialiser's shape, so the four call sites in three files are unchanged. Its title carries the count past one document ("Add 37 Documents to Collection"); a list a Meaning search made shows "This app's model" beside "FRUS text" (decision 6); a refused add, or a save that fails, is said in an alert and the sheet stays. One row is one document, so the counted title is first seen in lane 3.
- `CollectionPickerOrder.held` is the list's order while the sheet is open: the order it opened with, and a collection made since ahead of it. The picker's query sorts by `lastModified`, and a documents-mode add stamps the collection it adds to, so without it the tapped row left for the top of the list at the tap.
- Each host adds a state value, one mount and a menu item, and the iPhone's row a VoiceOver action.

**One review pass** (one agent, on the diff). It found no defect in the write, and these, all acted on.
1. The picker's list is sorted by `lastModified`, and documents mode stamps and saves at the tap, so the tapped row jumped to the top: its checkmark out of sight on a long list, and another collection under the reader's finger for the 0.6 s before the sheet closes. The list now holds its opening order, and a presentation adds once.
2. After a failed save the entries stayed in the context under an alert titled "Not Added": counted by the row behind it, read as held by a second attempt, and written by whatever saved next. A failed save now takes them back, and the message says nothing was added.
3. The sheet's title counted the request's documents raw while the add took each once, and an empty request could present and confirm an add of nothing. The request now holds each document once and cannot be empty. Handing the outcome to the host is lane 3's.
4. On the Mac the row is a stack of texts under a tap gesture, not one accessibility element, so a named action had nothing certain to land on and could not be checked here. It is removed from the Mac; the menu is the route there.
5. Test gaps closed: the initialiser's Meaning flag, which every scan missed; the limit when most of the list is already held; the UI test's oracle, which now adds two different documents; the menu item's place outside any condition; the action's place on the row; and the mount's own body.
6. Three comments and one figure in the Amendment Log corrected.

**Tests**
- `CollectionAttachmentTests`, eleven added, each driving `appendDocuments` on a real store: a never-saved collection links each entry both ways and a second context reads the rows; five documents with two present adds three, in order, at positions 8, 9 and 10 after 3 and 7; an excerpt does not count as present; the same document id in another volume is another document; a document named twice is added once; with every document present nothing is written; an add stamps the collection and the stamp is saved; a document whose entry was just deleted is not counted as present; a smart collection is refused; 1,001 documents are refused, 1,000 are taken, and the 1,001 are still refused once the 1,000 are held; and a save that fails takes the entries back out, after which the next attempt adds them.
- `BulkResultRequestTests` (6): the order, the engine, identity, no request for no results, each document once, and the reference's key.
- `CollectionPickerDocumentsModeTests` (12): the title and the failure messages; the initialiser's stored values; the held order as a rule; and source scans matched on the call for what nothing hosts: the picker adds through `appendDocuments` after the smart-collection guard and the one-add guard; both bodies badge a Meaning list; the row's content shape; the held order's wiring; the modifier presents `CollectionPickerSheet(documents:` from the request and the mount applies it; each host builds the request from the row, places the item directly after Archival Neighbors… at the menu's own level, and constructs no picker itself; the iPhone's row carries the action directly after its menu and the Mac's carries none.
- `SearchResultAddToCollectionTests` (UI, 2): see the runbook. On iPhone 17 and iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), both iOS 27.0: 2 tests, 2 passed on each.
- **Eighteen mutations, in nine builds, each failing the tests written for it**; the ninth build ran one of them against the UI test, which failed on it too. Before the review: a held document is added again; a smart collection is not refused; the limit is not held; `lastModified` is not set; an excerpt counts as the document; a document named twice is added twice; an entry just deleted counts as present; presence is the document id alone; the add does not save; the request reverses the rows. After it: a failed save leaves the entries in; the limit counts what is missing; the request keeps a repeat; the documents initialiser drops the Meaning flag; the list follows the live order; the rollback deletes without unlinking; a request is made for no results; a failed save leaves `lastModified` moved.

**In the app**
- The clone of the full-corpus iPhone 17e simulator (iOS 27.0), a Debug build of this branch before the review's changes: a keyword search for `Olney`, a long press on the first result, and the menu reads **Archival Neighbors…**, a divider, **Add to Collection…**. Choosing it opens a sheet titled **Add to Collection** with the "FRUS text" chip; that store has no collections, so it shows "No Collections".
- The add itself was driven by the UI test on the final code, on an iPhone and an iPad.
- **The picker's row took no tap on its blank part.** Found by the UI test's first iPad run, which taps a row's centre: on iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 27.0, the picker did not close; with the content shape it did; with the shape taken out again on the same warmed simulator it failed again at the same step.

**Checked**
- A clean `build-for-testing` of the `FRUSExplorer` scheme (iPhone 17, iOS 27.0) on the final code: `** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, and no warning line but the two known residues (`GeneratedSummary`'s conformance and the AppIntents note).
- The iOS unit target, from a shut-down iPhone 17 (iOS 27.0), on the final code: "Test run with 6745 tests in 792 suites passed after 545.825 seconds with 6 known issues", `** TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED **`, no relaunch of the host. That is 29 tests and 2 suites more than `v2`'s 6,716 in 790. The six known issues are `systemLogReachesTheRowAndTheRun`'s (#1606).
- `FRUSExplorerMac` (the DirectDistribution configuration, unsigned), a clean build of the final code: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, with the same two residues.
- `SearchResultAddToCollectionTests` on the final code: iPhone 17, iOS 27.0, 2 tests, 2 passed; iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 27.0, 2 tests, 2 passed.
- `CodingStandardsAuditTests` and `EditableContentKeyTests` run again after this entry was written: both pass.
- `swift test` is not owed and was not run: the diff names no package input.

**Not done**
- Nothing was run on the Mac.
- VoiceOver was not listened to. The iPhone and iPad row's action is there by code and by scan.
- "This app's model" on the picker was not seen: the simulator has no search model, so no row there comes from a Meaning search. The initialiser's test and the bodies' scan hold it.
- The counted title was not seen: one row is one document.
- The held order and the one-add guard were not seen with several collections on screen. The order is tested as a rule; its wiring and the guard are read from source.

## Session 2026-10-10 — Search results can be selected on iPhone and iPad, and a selection added to a collection or marked reviewed (#1576 lane 3)

Lane 3 of the implementation plan on #1576 (bulk actions on search results), after lane 2 merged as #1628. No index version, no CloudKit deploy, no re-index, no shared kit file, and no `@Model` or stored property added. The Mac is lane 4's and is not changed here.

**What a reader gets** (iPhone and iPad)
- **Two ways into selection**: **Select Results** in the ••• menu, after the two save items, and **Select** on a result's long-press menu, which starts with that result picked.
- **A selection bar in the actions bar's place**: Done, the count ("12 selected"), a Select menu with This Page, All N Shown and None, and at the end, where the ••• menu was and drawn with its glyph, an Actions menu. A tap on a result picks or un-picks it, and a picked result shows a filled circle and tells VoiceOver it is selected. Its long-press menu opens it.
- **The commands are in the Actions menu**: Add to Collection…, and in Checklist Mode Mark Reviewed.
- **What a command did stays on screen**, as a line above the results, with Undo where something changed: "Added 31 documents to “Chile”. 6 were already in it." Each outcome is announced to VoiceOver.
- **The picks last as long as the search.** A page turn keeps them; a re-run of the same search keeps those it still shows and says how many it does not; a new query, a switch of engine, a search that fails or finds nothing, and Done end the selection. A result Checklist Mode hides leaves the selection and comes back unpicked.
- **Add to Collection takes a thousand documents at a time** (the owner's decision 5): with more picked it is dimmed and a line says why. Mark Reviewed has no limit.
- **At the largest text sizes the lines above the results scroll** where they would take more than half the room the results have.

**The plan's rule on the bottom bar, applied.** The plan put the commands in a bar at the foot of the results and said: "If the bottom bar cannot clear banner and keyboard at 375 pt and accessibility sizes, the commands go in one Actions menu in the top selection bar." The bar was built and `ResultSelectionBarFitTests` measured it, Checklist Mode on and the banner showing. iPhone 17: clear at all five sizes, with 331, 195, 141, 102 and 7 pt between the first result's top and the bar at L, XXXL, AX1, AX3 and AX5. iPhone SE (3rd generation): 122, 82 and 58 pt at L, XXXL and AX1; at AX3 the first result's top (y 283) under the bar's top edge (y 280); at AX5 Mark Reviewed at y 334 to 382 under a banner whose top was at y 344. So the commands are a menu, and with it the suite passes 5 of 5 on both phones: 381, 303, 251, 162 and 67 pt from the first result's top to the banner on the iPhone 17, and 215, 138, 118, 58 and 10 pt on the iPhone SE. The bar as built is on a local branch, `l3-bottom-bar-with-column-fix`.

**A fault lane 1 left, found and fixed here.** The count header, the checklist's strip and the list were three siblings in the navigation root's own stack, and the first two take the height their text needs. Since lane 1 the strip is always there in Checklist Mode with two buttons, which at the accessibility sizes on an iPhone sit one above the other. Seen on an iPhone 17e at AX3 with the banner showing, on this branch with the two changes below taken out, which lays out as `v2` does: the mode picker about 35 pt up, behind the search field, the strip's Undo cut off by the banner, and no result showing. SwiftUI centres a view taller than its room, so it runs out at both ends and takes what is attached to it along.
- `SearchView.resultsColumn`: the results branch is one view. Its fixed rows are in `ViewThatFits(in: .vertical)`, the plain rows first and the same rows in a scroll view second, so they take their height where that is no more than an equal share of the column and scroll within it where it is more. At the standard size the screen below the search field is pixel-identical to before with Checklist Mode on, and the header-to-list gap is unchanged with it off.
- `TopAnchoredOverflow`: a layout at the navigation root that never reports more height than it is offered and lays its content from the top. With the rows scrolling, the list, the Timeline and All Results Reviewed give way by themselves; the Collocates reading, which has two controls of its own above its list, does not, and without this layout at AX5 with the banner showing it put the mode picker behind the search field (seen on the iPhone 17e).
- Not measured: the stack attached above the results (the mode picker, the bar and the Query Inspector) cannot scroll. At AX5 on the iPhone SE with the banner showing it ends 20 pt above the banner in the state the fit suite measures; a project's Working On banner, a working-corpus banner or a narrowed-by row would add to it.

**How** (`ResultSelection.swift`, `ResultSelectionViews.swift`, `TopAnchoredOverflow.swift`, `SearchViewModel.swift`, `SearchView.swift`)
- `ResultSelection` is a value type: whether the list is in selection, and the picked results' ids. It holds keys and never rows; the rows are resolved from the list, in its order, when a command is chosen, and frozen into lane 2's `BulkResultRequest`.
- `SearchViewModel` owns it. The picks are pruned in the observers of everything that can hide a row (`results`, the checklist's marks, the documents opened since, the mode itself), so no pick is of a row the list does not show. A completed search is settled by lane 1's `ChecklistAnchor`: the same search keeps the picks, another ends selection. Selection also ends when `searchError` is set, since an error is drawn where the rows were and some refusals leave `results` as it was, and when `searchMode` changes, whoever changes it.
- `BulkOutcome` is the line and what its Undo takes back: the collection entries an add inserted, by id, or the last bulk mark. `CollectionDocumentDiscovery.removeEntries(withIds:)` is the Undo of an add: it re-fetches by id, in batches of 200, and an id that finds nothing is already undone. The picker tells its host what an add did through `onAdded`.
- A completed search ends the last command's line; the same search's dropped picks take its place. An outcome is counted when it is set, and the bar announces on that count: two full pages marked in a row leave the same words.
- Marking a selection does not send the list to its top, as Mark Page Reviewed does: the picked rows are scattered and the reader is among them.
- `ResultSelectionBar` is one row and takes the actions bar's slot at exactly its height, so nothing moves when selection begins or ends. Its Actions menu is the actions bar's own glyph at its size, named "Actions" for VoiceOver and the Large Content Viewer.
- `ResultSelectionStatus` is the command's line and the over-limit line, the first of the rows above the results. Not under the bar: they wrap and grow with the reader's text, and under the bar, at AX5 with the banner showing, a three-line outcome made the stack attached above the results taller than its room (seen on the iPhone 17e). The bar still makes the announcement, because the line's view is replaced when the rows start or stop scrolling.
- `FRUS_UI_TEST_SEED_BULK_VOLUME` writes a side-loaded volume of thirty documents that share one word, and any launch without it removes the file and its index rows. The browse fixture is left alone.
- The ••• menu's help lists its contents, so it is re-keyed to `search.moreActions.help.v3`.

**Two review passes** (one agent each, on two diffs: the lane as first built, and the redesign).
- First pass, acted on: the row's VoiceOver hint said "Double tap" in a string the Mac compiles (`macTextNeverSaysTap` would have failed); a refused search left a selection of rows nobody could see, so an error now ends selection; the announcement is posted for each outcome counted, late and at high priority; a failed Undo says it did not finish and offers no second try; a completed search ends the last line; `searchMode` ends selection itself; marking picked rows no longer sends the list to its top; test gaps closed (the strip's Undo withdrawing the line, the picks' order under a date sort, the add's enablement in the view model, the count of outcomes, the Meaning path, a save that throws in `removeEntries`, the UI test's page turn).
- Second pass, acted on: the count was cut short at the accessibility sizes once the row had four controls ("100 selected" at 375 pt, "1,000 selected" at 402 pt), and the fit suite, measuring "0 selected", could not see it, so the gaps are 8 pt, the count shrinks to six tenths and has the Large Content Viewer, and the suite holds the count's room to "8,888 selected"; no test reached `TopAnchoredOverflow` on the Search screen, so a sixth fit test turns the Collocates reading on at AX5 (the Timeline, which the reviewer named, and All Results Reviewed give way without the layout; Collocates, with two controls of its own, does not); the fit suite waits for the checklist's strip; the rows above the results are built once and not twice a pass; an outcome is announced once, where it was spoken again each time the bar came back on screen; five comments corrected; the outcome's Undo has a VoiceOver hint, since the strip's Undo is in the same rows; the layout's unit tests measure from the host's safe area.
- Second pass, not acted on: the over-limit line is above the results and not beside the dimmed menu item; where the rows scroll there are two vertical scroll views, and the status-bar tap to the top was not checked. Checked and not so: the row's text-size limit does not shrink the menus it presents (seen at AX5).

**Tests**
- `ResultSelectionTests` (7), one fixture per rule of the value type.
- `ResultSelectionCopyTests` (8): the counts, the add's sentences, the undone add, the dropped picks, the limit, the failed Undo, the row's hint and the Undo's two hints naming no gesture, the two menus' words, and an outcome owed its announcement once.
- `SearchSelectionModelTests` (29), driving `SearchViewModel`: both ways in; This Page, a page turn, All Shown, None; a hidden row and an opened row leaving the selection, and coming back unpicked; a replaced and an emptied list; a re-run of the same search on a real index keeping the picks still shown and saying how many it dropped; a completed search ending the last line; a new query, a refused search, an error, an engine change by the picker and by any other writer ending selection; the Meaning path through a stand-in engine; Mark Reviewed and its Undo; the list not moved by a selection's mark; the strip's own mark and Undo withdrawing the line; each outcome counted; an add's outcome, its Undo by id, an add of nothing, a failed Undo; nothing recorded outside selection; Done forgetting the line; the limit, and when the add can run; and the picks' order under a date sort.
- `CollectionEntryRemovalTests` (5), on a real store: exactly the inserted entries removed and saved; a missing entry not an error; a thousand removed across batches; a save that throws; another collection's entry left alone.
- `UITestBulkVolumeSeederTests` (3): written when asked and removed when not; thirty documents with the word and none of the browse fixture's titles; and, against a real pipeline, indexed when asked, thirty rows for the word, and un-indexed when not.
- `ResultSelectionWiringTests` (9): source scans matched on the call for the slot, the menu item, the rows, the Actions menu and its request, nothing attached at the foot, the status lines' place among the rows, the outcome and its Undo, the announcement and the count it keeps, the row's two figures the fit suite measures with, the two properties that end selection, and boot's two calls.
- `TopAnchoredOverflowTests` (5), in a real hosting controller: content taller than its room leaves the bar above it and the bar below it at their edges; the control, where the same content without the layout moves both; content that fits is where it is without the layout; content that fills is given the room; and the height reported.
- `SearchResultsColumnWiringTests` (3): the root's content is inside the layout with every inset outside it; the results branch is the one column; the fixed rows are the plain rows first and the scrolling rows second.
- `BulkResultRequestTests`, `CollectionPickerDocumentsModeTests` and `SearchTipsWiringTests.moreMenuOpensTips` updated for the shapes this lane changed.
- `SearchBulkActionsTests` (UI, 4) and `ResultSelectionBarFitTests` (UI, 6, iPhone only): see the runbook.
- **Thirty-three mutations, each failing a test written for it**: thirty in seven unit builds, and three by the fit suite on a simulator (the rows not scrolling, at AX5 on the iPhone 17; no layout at the navigation root, in the Collocates reading; the Actions glyph at three times its size, at AX1 on the iPhone SE). Two of the three were first aimed at tests that passed: the rows not scrolling at AX3 on the iPhone 17, where they fit plain, and no layout in the Timeline reading, which gives way by itself.

**In the app**
- By hand on a cloned iPhone 17e simulator (iOS 27.0, the full corpus, its "iCloud Account Issue" banner showing), a search for "Olney". At the standard size: ••• ▸ Select Results turned the actions bar into Done · 0 selected · Select · ••• with the Query Inspector's row where it was; two results tapped read "2 selected" with filled circles; the Actions menu held Add to Collection… alone with Checklist Mode off and both commands with it on, both dimmed with nothing picked; Add to Collection… presented the picker titled for two documents (the clone holds no collection, so the add was the UI suite's); with Checklist Mode on, Mark Reviewed on two picked results left "2 results marked reviewed" with Undo above the count header, "0 selected" and the strip at "2 reviewed hidden"; with the keyboard up the bar and its menu stayed.
- At AX3 and AX5 with that outcome showing: the mode picker under the search field, the bar in its slot, the lines above the results scrolling, the top of a result showing. All 1,000 Shown at AX5 read "1,000 selected", whole and smaller. The Select menu's items drew at the reader's size.
- The fault, on this branch with the layout and the scrolling rows taken out, at AX3 with Checklist Mode on: the mode picker behind the search field, the strip's Undo cut off by the banner, no result showing.

## Session 2026-10-10 — Search results can be selected in the Mac's Search window, and the selection's rules are one value both view models hold (#1576 lane 4)

Lane 4 of the implementation plan on #1576, after lane 3 merged as #1629. No index version, no CloudKit deploy, no re-index, no shared kit file, and no `@Model` or stored property added. **The Mac half was run**, in the isolated check copy (`tools/mac-check-copy/`): the lane's list was walked there, what it and the review found was fixed, and the fixes were looked at again in a rebuilt copy.

**What a reader gets** (Mac)
- A titled **Select** button in the Search window's titlebar, beside Checklist. On, every result has a checkbox at its leading edge and a strip appears above the list. It turns on for the list reading, with rows to check and no error; once on it can always be turned off.
- A click on a checkbox checks the result; a click anywhere else on the row still opens the document (the owner's decision 2). **Space** checks or clears the highlighted row, once for each press.
- The strip: the count, a Select menu (This Page, All N Shown, None), Add to Collection…, in Checklist Mode Mark Reviewed, and Done; under them what the last command did, with Undo.
- A checked row's menu, with others checked too, adds the selection ("Add 12 Selected to Collection…"). Its other items, Mark Reviewed among them, are still the row's own, and an unchecked row's menu is that row's throughout.
- The window loads up to 7,500 results and one add takes 1,000 (decision 5): over it Add to Collection is dimmed, in the strip and the menu, and a line says why.
- The checks last as long as the search, by the rules of lane 3; another reading also ends the selection.

**How** (`ResultSelection.swift`, `ReviewedMarks.swift`, `ResultSelectionViews.swift`, `SearchViewModel.swift`, `MacSearchViewModel.swift`, `SearchSheet.swift`)
- `ResultSelectionSession` is the selection's rules as one value: the picks, the search they were made in, what the last command did, and the picks a re-run dropped. Lane 3 wrote these into `SearchViewModel`; they are moved, and `SearchViewModel` keeps the same properties and functions, each now a call into the session. `SearchSelectionModelTests`' 29 tests of lane 3 pass as they were.
- `MacSearchViewModel` holds the same session. Seventeen of its members are the iPhone's line for line, and `MacResultSelectionWiringTests.viewModelIsItsTwins` reads the two files against each other. Three are the Mac's own: it marks through its own bulk mark; it settles its checklist before a search runs, so its selection records the search with the rows; and it asks, before it marks a selection, whether the checklist is on the search whose rows are on screen.
- `results`, `searchError`, `searchMode` and the three checklist properties of the Mac's view model gained the observers the iPhone's have. Both search paths settle the selection as the rows arrive and before the next suspension; the Meaning path takes its anchor before the run.
- `ResultSelectionStrip` is the strip, with the commands as buttons. The checkbox is beside `SearchResultRow` and not in it: the row is private, other tests read it, and the click that opens a document is the row's own.
- The reading picker's setter ends selection when the reading is not the list. Lane 2's sheet presenter is given `onAdded` on the Mac.

**In the Mac check copy** (27 volumes of 1961–63, 10,543 documents, no iCloud; three builds of this lane and one of `v2`)
- The titlebar, read through accessibility at every 10 pt of width from the 640 pt minimum. It folds its items into its » menu from the right. This lane: the reading picker shows from 720 pt, Save as Working Corpus… from 940, Checklist from 1,050, **Select from 1,140** and Facets from 1,170. `v2`: 720, 940, 1,050, and Facets from 1,090. So at the 820 pt the window opens to, all the trailing buttons are in the menu on both, and what the lane costs is that Facets needs 80 pt more to show as a button. In the menu a toggle shows no mark for on or off, Checklist no more than Select.
- Select on: a checkbox on every row, on the row's first line; the strip above the list and above the checklist's strip; "0 selected". At the 640 pt minimum, with Checklist Mode on and all 1,852 results of a search checked, the strip's row fits on one line.
- A click on a checkbox checked it and opened nothing; a click on a row's title opened the document and left the checkbox as it was. With Checklist Mode on, a checked row that was opened left the list and the count ("19 selected" from 20).
- Space checked the highlighted row, and after ↓ cleared the next. Held down for two and a half seconds, with the count sampled through accessibility about every 0.15 s, it changed the count once.
- The menu on a checked row with another checked read "Add 2 Selected to Collection…", and on an unchecked row "Add to Collection…". With 5,079 checked the item and the strip's button were dimmed and the strip said "Select 1,000 documents or fewer to add them to a collection."
- Add to Collection… with twenty checked: the picker titled "Add 20 Documents to Collection", a new collection made from it, the strip "Added 20 documents to “Lane 4 check”." with Undo, and Undo "Removed 20 documents from “Lane 4 check”."
- Mark Reviewed on nineteen: the rows went, "0 selected", "19 results marked reviewed" with Undo, and the checklist's strip "20 reviewed hidden" with its own. On all 1,852: All Results Reviewed, selection still on, and Undo "1,852 results are back in the list".

## Session 2026-10-11 — Search results can be tagged, one from its menu or a selection at one stroke, and the tags are added to what a document has (#1576 lane 5)

Lane 5 of the implementation plan on #1576, after lane 4 (#1630). No index version, no CloudKit deploy, no re-index, no shared kit file, and no `@Model` or stored property added. **The plan gave this lane a guarded clear in the launch tag sync, and with it #1591. That was already on `v2`**: #1591 was fixed on its own on 2026-10-09 (#1614, `DocumentTagAssignment.reconcileTagColumn`), so the lane adds no clear and uses that fix's `reindexTagColumn` for its own writes. **The Mac half was run after the merge**, and is the comment on #1631: between 11:50 and 11:53 UTC, in the isolated check copy built from #1577 lane 2's tree (this lane's code with that lane over it; 27 volumes), every check passed. (Corrected on 2026-10-20 in A12, #1694, which found the walk while settling #1577 lane 2's record: this said the Mac half had not been run because the screen locked before the walk, which was so when the pull request merged, at 11:38 UTC.) The Mac target compiles clean, its wiring is held by scans, and its picker, writer and session are the code the iPhone ran.

**What a reader gets**
- **Add Tags…** on a result's menu on iPhone, iPad and Mac, and among a row's VoiceOver actions on iPhone and iPad.
- **Add Tags…** for a selection: in the Actions menu on iPhone and iPad, a button in the Mac's strip, and "Add Tags to 12 Selected…" on a checked row's menu on the Mac.
- The tag picker in an adding mode, titled "Tag 37 Documents": every tag off, beside each how many of the documents carry it already, and a line saying that a document keeps the tags it has. Done adds the tags switched on and takes none off.
- The tagged rows show the tag at once. In selection a line says what was added, with Undo, which takes off the tags that command added and no others.
- The 1,000 limit is the collection's, and one line speaks for both commands it dims.

**How** (`UserTagAssign.swift`, `UserTagPickerSheet.swift`, `BulkResultRequest.swift`, `ResultSelection.swift`, `ResultSelectionViews.swift`, both view models, `SearchView.swift`, `SearchSheet.swift`)
- `UserTagAdmin.assign` makes one fetch of every assignment, inserts only the pairs the store does not hold, and saves once. A fetch that fails stops it; a save that fails takes the rows back out; a list over the limit is refused first. Its answer carries each document's whole tag set as the store has it.
- `UserTagAdmin.removeAssignments` deletes the rows the command inserted, by id. A row gone already is not an error, and no other row is touched.
- `assignAndIndex` and `removeAssignmentsAndIndex` follow each store write with `DocumentTagAssignment.reindexTagColumn` for the documents touched. The rewrites are chained, each waiting for the one before, so that a tagging's rewrite cannot finish after its Undo's.
- The picker has a `Mode`. The writer that replaces a document's tag set takes the document as its argument, and the adding mode has none to give it; its Done calls `assignAndIndex`. The sheet closes once to a presentation, in both modes.
- `BulkResultRequest.Command.addTags`, presented by lane 2's modifier, which is now given the index and `onTagged`.
- `BulkOutcome.Undo.tagAssignments`; `ResultSelectionSession.recordTagging`; a third closure on the session's `undo`.
- `SearchResult.replacingUserTagIds` copies a row with other tags, and both view models' `refreshUserTags` swaps the named rows in memory. `recordTagAssign` and the wider `undoBulkOutcome` are the same text in both.

**On an iPhone simulator, by eye** (a clone of the full-corpus simulator, iOS 27.0, a search for "Olney")
- One result: its menu lists Add Tags… after Add to Collection…; the picker was titled "Tag 1 Document"; a tag made there was on the row when the sheet closed, with no line about it, since nothing was selected.
- Three rows picked, one of them that row: Actions ▸ Add Tags… gave "Tag 3 Documents", the tag off, "1 of 3 has it" beside it, and the line under the list. Done: "Added “Venezuela boundary” to 2 documents. 1 already had it.", with Undo, the tag on all three rows, and the three still selected.
- Undo: "Removed “Venezuela boundary” from 2 documents." The two rows lost the tag and the first kept it.
- Filters ▸ My Tags then counted 1 document under the tag, and with the filter on the search found 1 result, the document that kept it: the index was as the store is after a tagging and its Undo.
- All 1,000 loaded results selected (Select ▸ All 1,000 Shown), which is the limit and not over it, so both commands were live. The picker was titled "Tag 1,000 Documents" and said "1 of 1,000 has it". Done: "Added “Venezuela boundary” to 999 documents. 1 already had it." The simulator's index was read beside the run, a read-only count every 50 ms of the rows that carry a tag: it went from 1 to 1,000 in under 0.2 s, and after Undo ("Removed “Venezuela boundary” from 999 documents.") back to 1 in about 0.1 s. That is a simulator on this Mac and not a phone.

**What the review and the full run changed** (one agent, one pass over the diff)
- *Done and Cancel could each run after the other on a sheet that was closing.* A Cancel after a Done would have deleted a tag made in that sheet, which the Done had just given to the documents; a second Done would have replaced the line and its Undo with "Nothing added". Read, not seen. The sheet now closes once to a presentation.
- *The test of the order of rewrites did not guard the order.* It ran a tagging and its Undo back to back on a real index and passed with the chain cut, since the two rewrites are quick. The writer gained a seam for the rewrite, and a test holds the first rewrite open and sees that the second has not started.
- *A removal's failed save had no test, and the writer filtered rows the context's fetch never returns.* A test holds what a failed removal leaves; another holds that a row deleted and not yet saved is not in a fetch, and the two filters are gone.
- *The picker a document opens had lost its plain section title* in the reshaping, and the failure alert said "saved" where a read can fail too. Both put right.
- *The line under the tag list would have been cut to one line on the Mac.* The full unit run failed #1475's tree-wide census: a `List` section's footer that the Mac draws must be a `WrappingFooterSection`'s. The adding mode's section is one now. The lane's scoped runs had not named that suite.

## Session 2026-10-11 — The manuals say what a bulk add does to a project's History, and when a bulk tag reaches another device (#1576 lane 6)

Lane 6 of the implementation plan on #1576, the notes, after lane 5. Manuals and planning files only: no Swift file and no string the app shows, so no `Docs/EditableContent` block.

**What the manuals gained** (`Docs/iOS-User-Manual.md`, `Docs/macOS-User-Manual.md`, section 7.7a in each; the AI Generated notice stays)
- Under **Add to Collection…**: a collection filed under a project carries its documents into that project's History. The scope takes them in the next time the filter panel is opened; from then a search scoped to History finds them, and a Focus search with Only new to this project on leaves them out.
- Under **Add Tags…**: the tags reach the reader's other devices through iCloud, and a search there narrowed by My Tags finds the documents once that device has them, a few seconds after the sync when the app is open and shortly after it is next opened when it is not.
- From reading the bulk-actions part as a whole: **Select** in the iPhone manual's list of what a row's menu holds (7.1), which named every other item; and **Space** in the Mac manual's table of the Search window's keys (19), which lane 4 gave to a selection.

**Checked by reading, before either sentence was written**
- *History.* `ProjectEngagedDocuments`: a project's engaged set is every document in the collections whose `projectIds` holds it, with its anchored notes and its visits. The History scope gates on that set, and `SearchViewModel` passes it as `excludeDocumentIds` under Focus with Only new to this project on; the Mac's view model does the same. The set is read again when the active project changes and each time the filter panel opens, on both platforms (`SearchView.refreshEngagedKeys`, `SearchSheet.refreshProjectScope`), and at no other time: a search run again with the panel shut uses the set it had, which is why the manuals name the panel.
- *Another device.* **The plan's sentence was out of date.** It says another device's tag filter picks up a bulk tag at its next launch. Since #1614 (2026-10-09) the app reconciles the index's tag column when an iCloud import settles, eight seconds after imports go quiet, on both platforms (`FRUSExplorerApp.swift`, beside the note reconcile), so with the app open the tag reaches Search there within seconds. The manuals say that.

It ran on lane 5's build, since no Swift file and no project file differs from that build's; tests read the manuals and the planning files as they run, which is why the whole target was run for a change to documents.

- On the Mac the facet panel, an inspector with its own button, describes the rows that are on screen. It took its count, its wording and the documents it counts over from the picker. **How** (`ResultSetScope.swift`, both view models, `SearchView.swift`, `SearchSheet.swift`)

Each host also empties the rows itself in one place, where it cannot write the route, so the rows' own observer resets it for an emptied list. `resultsAreSemantic`, which the bulk commands read, is a read of the route.

## Session 2026-10-11 — A UI test can reach a Meaning result: a stand-in encoder and a match-file store of the seam's own for the seeded fixture volume (#1577 lane 3)

Lane 3 of the implementation plan on #1577. No index version, no CloudKit deploy, no re-index, no shared kit file, and no `@Model` or stored property added. The seam is compiled into DEBUG builds only, and it changes no Mac behaviour.

**Why.** No UI test reached a Meaning result: a Meaning search needs the 229 MB query encoder, which no simulator has and no test may download, and a match file for each volume it ranks. Lane 4's tests need a Meaning list on screen.

**What it is** (`UITestMeaningSeeder.swift`, new; `FRUSExplorerApp.swift`)
- `FRUS_UI_TEST_SEED_MEANING=1`, beside `FRUS_UI_TEST_SEED_VOLUME`, replaces three inputs of the searcher and leaves its code, the backend, the bundled index and the bundled sign bits as the app's own.
- *The question's embedding*: the ±1 vector of the bundled sign bits of one document, through the searcher's `embedOverride`, so the encoder is never loaded.
- *The match-file store*: one of the seam's own, in a folder of the temporary directory made afresh at each launch that asks, holding one file made for the fixture volume: a row for each of its 120 bundled rows, each the ±1 vector of that row's own bits as int8 codes, written with `SemanticVectorsArtifacts.volumeShard` under the bundled provenance digest and row count. A row then scores `1 − 2h/512`. The app's own store is not read, written or cleared.
- *The request for missing match files* always declines.
- The launch takes the seam's searcher when there is one (`UITestMeaningSeeder.makeSearcher`, which the unit suites call too) and builds its own otherwise, and in every build that is not DEBUG.

**The two questions, measured on the bundled artifacts through the kit's own readers before the design** (`frus1961-63v06`, whose fixture holds d1, d2 and d3, which have bundled rows, and n1, n2 and t1, which have none)
- Near, the default: the fixture's d2. Its three documents with rows are the first three of 314,616 by Hamming distance (d2, d1 at 90 bits, d3 at 100), so a plain Meaning search lists all three at 100, 65 and 61 percent. They are three of 78 hits, since 78 of the real volume's 120 rows are among the 800 candidates: the strip counts 75 close matches as not listed and 722 possible matches in 179 volumes as unscored.
- Far, for a question that holds "afield": `frus1861` d1. None of the fixture volume's 120 rows is among its 800 candidates, which lie in 134 volumes, so a plain search lists no fixture document, and a search inside a working corpus of them ranks all three (24, 24 and 16 percent). The second question is the plan's control: with the near one alone, the tree before lane 1 lists the same three rows.

**The control.** `MeaningResultsSeamTests` on `477ee9b6`, the tree before lane 1, with the seeder, the launch's hook, the row's value and the suite added, on the same iPhone 17: the first two tests passed, and `testAFarQuestionInsideAWorkingCorpusRanksEveryMemberWithAVector` failed with 0 rows listed and the corpus applied. On this branch it lists the three. Run twice, with the seam's first form and again after the review's rework, with the same result.

**One thing a reader gets.** On iPhone and iPad VoiceOver reads a ranked result's score after its heading ("Semantic match 65 percent"). The row is one accessibility element whose label is its heading, so the chip was silent; `SemanticScoreCopy` holds the figure and the words, and the chip draws the same figure.

**Review** (one pass by one agent over the diff, ten findings, all acted on)
- *The seam shared the app's match-file store.* A far question's 800 candidates lie in 134 volumes, so a real match file left on a simulator for any of them could list rows where the suite expects none; the planted file replaced a published one for the fixture volume; and the clean-up deleted by name. The seam has a store of its own, and the marker file, the clean-up and the launch-order constraint the first form needed are gone.
- *The far-question test passed on an empty list alone*, which a Meaning search run before the launch has indexed the fixture also gives. It asks the near question first, reads three rows, then asks the far one and reads "800 possible matches" in the strip (the near question leaves 722).
- *Nothing said that a near search has 78 hits.* The seeder's comment, the suite's header, the runbook and the plan note say it, and a unit test holds the figures.
- *The unit suite built a searcher of its own that mirrored the launch's.* The launch and the suites call one function.
- Smaller: the key's spelling is pinned, since a UI suite cannot name the app's constant; the counts that only documents quote are in tests of their own; a comment in `ProvenanceChip.swift` that said the score went unannounced; `SearchView`'s version line; the manual's sentence moved from 7.12, whose rows are the zero-result fallback's, to 7.12a; a re-pack note in `Planning/Generators-Runbook.md`; the suite launches with Download With Volumes off.

**Tests**
- `UITestMeaningSeederTests` (7), on the artifacts the app ships, read from the test host's bundle with the kit's readers: the key's spelling; the sign vector is the row's bits, most significant first, and packs back to the row; the encoder's two documents; the near question's first three candidates and the far question's none; the counts documents quote; the synthetic match file opens under the bundled pin and row count and scores a row by its Hamming distance. A regenerated bundle that moves a figure fails here and says which.
- `UITestMeaningSeamSearchTests` (6) run the app's own searcher, built by the launch's function, through the seam: a plain search; the figures documents quote of it; a search inside a set; the seam's store holds the planted file alone, in the folder it was given, and is made afresh; a launch that does not ask makes no seam and no folder; a volume the bundle has no rows for gets no seam and leaves the folder as it was.
- `SemanticScoreCopyTests` (3) and `UITestMeaningSeamWiringTests` (3): the percentage and the words; and, read from source, that the launch takes the seam's searcher in DEBUG alone, that the seam's searcher is made in one place of the seam's store, its encoder and a fetch request that declines, and that the seeder is compiled in DEBUG alone.
- UI: `MeaningResultsSeamTests` (3), the first suite to reach a Meaning result and the first to save and apply a working corpus.
- Mutations: 29, one to a build, 29 caught. 28 failed a test on the first run. One survived, a seam returned though its file could not be planted; it has a test now and fails it.

## Session 2026-10-11 — The taxonomy generator has a second source: the Office of the Historian's own taxonomy file, read before the page, and writing the bundled taxonomy byte for byte (#1622)

The pull request after #1635, on the owner's word, and the third of the five issues filed during the week of the plan of record's §0c. Tooling alone: no file the app compiles is changed, and no bundled resource. No index version, no CloudKit deploy, no re-index, no shared kit file.

**Why.** `TaxonomyGenerator` had one source, the page `history.state.gov/tags/all`, and a parse that turns on the page's markup. The site is being rebuilt. Since #1600 a page with other markup stops the run where it used to empty the bundled file, and then the tool cannot regenerate `volume-tag-taxonomy.json` at all.

**The file** (`taxonomy/taxonomy.xml` of the public HistoryAtState/tags repository, read 2026-10-11 at commit `0e701226`: blob `6fd68631`, 101,303 bytes, last changed upstream on 2025-01-24. The repository's licence puts it in the public domain in the United States and under CC0 elsewhere, and its README calls it the source data of the site's taxonomy.)
- 11 `<category>` and 500 `<tag>` elements, each with an `<id>` and a `<label>`: three roots, eight categories and eight tags below them, 292 tags at the third level and 200 at the fourth. The 508 ids below the roots are the bundled taxonomy's slugs, none more and none fewer.
- One comment, which holds a whole tag: `lgbtq-rights`. A count of `<id>` in the text gives 512.
- 28 definitions, two of them on roots, and ten usage hints, which are the Office's notes to its own taggers.
- Six `<ptr target="…"/>` pointers: three in the definitions of two entries (`detainees`, `military-intervention-presence-and-withdrawal`) and three in usage hints. One `<a href>`, in the definition of the root `places`.
- No ampersand and no CDATA section.

**What it took to write the same bytes**, each found by comparing a prototype's entries with the bundled file's, field by field, until all 508 were equal:
- *Where an entry sits* is the page parser's rule stated on depth: under a root an entry is its own subcategory and has no parent; under `sovereign-territories` or `dependencies-and-areas-of-special-sovereignty` it is its own subcategory and keeps that parent; anywhere else its subcategory and its parent are the entry it sits in. The two parsers now read one list of those two slugs (`TaxonomyParser.structuralSlugs`).
- *A definition is kept as the file writes it*, line breaks and indentation included, with only its ends trimmed. Nineteen of the 26 bundled descriptions hold a line break followed by sixteen to twenty-four spaces: the page prints the file's text unchanged, and the page's parse trims no more than the ends.
- *A pointer in a definition is the page's link markup.* The bundled description of `detainees` ends `<a href="/tags/asylum">Asylum</a> or <a href="/tags/refugees">Refugees</a>`, and `military-intervention-presence-and-withdrawal`'s ends with a link to Warfare. The file's `<ptr target="asylum"/>` is written as that link, under the target's label.

**What was built** (`TaxonomySource.swift` and `TaxonomyXMLParser.swift`, new; `TaxonomyGeneratorRunner.swift`, `TaxonomyGate.swift`, `TaxonomyFetcher.swift`, `TaxonomyParser.swift`, `TaxonomyModels.swift`, `main.swift`)
- `TaxonomySource`: the repository's file and the page, with each one's address and the order a run reads them in. The file is fetched from the head of the repository's default branch (`…/HistoryAtState/tags/HEAD/taxonomy/taxonomy.xml`), so a renamed branch does not move it.
- `TaxonomyXMLParser`: Foundation's `XMLParser` over the file. An id, a label or a definition counts only as the child of a category or a tag. A comment's content and a usage hint are not read. Four things it will not guess at are errors: text that is not XML, an entry with no id, an entry with no label, and two entries with one id.
- `TaxonomyGeneratorRunner.generate(from:outputPath:read:)`: reads the sources in order and writes the first that `TaxonomyGate` accepts. A source that cannot be read, cannot be parsed or is refused is passed over with its reason; a write that fails is thrown as it is. `generate(fromTaxonomyXML:outputPath:)` is the file's half, beside `generate(fromHTML:outputPath:)`, and the gate and the write are one function under both.
- `TaxonomyRefusal.explanation(for:)`: the three refusals worded for the source the list came from. `description` is the page's wording, as before.
- `TAXONOMY_SOURCE=repository` or `page` reads that one source and no other. Any other value stops the run before it reads anything.

**The file first, and why.** The issue allowed the file in place of the page or the file when the page gives no tags. This reads the file first and keeps the page as the second source, because the file is the data and the page a drawing of it, because `manifest.json`, whose volumes carry these tags by slug, is read from the Office's repositories too, and because the test below holds the bundled file to what the file writes. The cost is that a run no longer reads what the public site shows unless it is told to, and the repository's head can be ahead of the site. The other order is one constant, `TaxonomySource.automaticOrder`.

**Measured with the tool itself** (2026-10-11, `swift run -c release TaxonomyGenerator`, each over a copy of the bundled file with `OUTPUT_PATH`)
- `TAXONOMY_SOURCE=repository`: 508 tags (people 121, places 274, topics 113), none dropped or added, the copy byte-identical afterwards.
- `TAXONOMY_SOURCE=page`: the same, from the live page.
- No source named: the file was read, with the same result.
- `TAXONOMY_SOURCE=repository` over no file at all: the bundled file byte for byte.
- `TAXONOMY_SOURCE=xml`: exit 1, the copy untouched, and a line naming the two values.

**Tests** (`TaxonomyXMLParserTests.swift`, new: four suites, 25 tests; `TaxonomyGeneratorTests/Fixtures/taxonomy.xml`, new)
- `TaxonomyXMLParserTests`: one small file with a case for each thing the parser decides, and a file for each of the four errors.
- `TaxonomySourceParityTests`: the same taxonomy as a file and as a page in the site's markup gives the same entries in the same order and the same bytes, through the two real parsers.
- `TaxonomyRepositoryFileTests`: the committed copy of the Office's file writes the bundled taxonomy byte for byte, over nothing and over itself; and its entries are the ids a second reading finds in its text outside comments, less the three roots. **The copy and the bundled file are committed together from here on**: a run that changes the bundled file fails this until the copy is replaced with the file the run read.
- `TaxonomySourceOrderTests`: the file is read first and the page is not asked for when the file is written; an unreachable file, a file that is not XML and a file the gate refuses are each passed over with their own reason; with neither source the output file keeps its bytes; and a run told one source asks for no other.
- **Seventeen mutations, one at a time, each caught by the test written for it**: a root taken for a parent, the structural rule dropped, a definition's whitespace collapsed, a pointer written as its label alone, an unknown pointer left blank, a definition untrimmed, a link written as its text, an id read anywhere, each of the three checks removed, the page read first, an unreadable source made fatal, an XML error made fatal, the page's wording used for the file, an unknown `TAXONOMY_SOURCE` read as either, and a run that reads on after it has written.

**Found on the way**
- **The bundled descriptions are not clean text**, as above: hard line breaks with their indentation in nineteen, and anchor markup in two. **No screen shows a tag's description**: `VolumeLevelTagStore` copies it into `VolumeLevelTag.description`, and no view reads that property. So nothing a reader sees is wrong, and the byte-for-byte match keeps the text as it is. If a screen is ever to show one, the generator is where it would be cleaned.
- **`lgbtq-rights`.** Four volumes of `manifest.json` carry it: `frus1952-54v01p2`, `frus1958-60v03mSupp`, `frus1977-80v28` and `frus1981-88v41`. Neither source gives it a name, since the file holds it inside a comment and the page is drawn from the file. `VolumeLevelTagStore.resolve(slugs:)` skips a slug the taxonomy does not name (read, not seen in the app). Whether the tag joins the bundled taxonomy is the owner's decision, as the issue said.

**Checked**
- `swift test`, owed because the diff is package input: exit 0, 38 `Test run with` lines, 2,599 tests, of which 25 are new, and no failed line. `swift test --filter TaxonomyGeneratorTests`: 42 tests in 6 suites.
- A clean `build-for-testing` of the `FRUSExplorer` scheme (iPhone 17, iOS 27.0): `** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, and no warning line but the two known residues.
- The iOS unit target on iPhone 17 (iOS 27.0): "Test run with 6961 tests in 817 suites passed after 413.741 seconds with 6 known issues", exit 0, no failed line. The same counts as #1635's run: this pull request adds no app test. It was run because two of its suites read what this pull request changes, the license-header scan and the scan of each generator's inputs. This entry was written after it.
- `FRUSExplorerMac` (the DirectDistribution configuration, unsigned), a clean build: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, with the same two residues.
- The package build printed no warning for the generator's files or for the fixture's folder, which the test target excludes.

**Not done**
- **`lgbtq-rights` is not added**, and the descriptions are not cleaned: either would end the byte-for-byte match, and the first is the owner's.
- **A run does not compare its two sources.** It reads the second only when the first gives nothing, so a page and a file that disagree are not noticed by a run. The committed copy's test notices when the bundled file stops matching the file.
- **The page's parser is kept as it was**, and will stop giving tags when the site's markup changes; the run then says so and writes from the file alone.
- **The fetch has no test**, as before: the tests hand each source its text.
- **A CDATA section and an ampersand in the file were not tried**: the file has neither. The parser's doc comment says what an ampersand would do.
- No manual, README, editable-content or TestFlight change: nothing a reader meets has changed.

**Docs**
- `Planning/Generators-Runbook.md`: the tool's entry, with the two sources, the new variable, the measurements above, and the rule that the copy is committed with the bundled file. `CLAUDE.md`: the index row's inputs. `Package.swift`: the tool's line in the header comment, and the test target excludes `Fixtures`.
- `Planning/Plan-Of-Record-2026-09-28.md`: §0c's paragraph for this pull request, and *Where the queue stands* brought to the present.

## Session 2026-10-11 — The index bump's brief, and Browse opens a chapter, subchapter or compilation that holds prose and no documents (#1535)

The owner asked for the index-bumping sessions of the plan of record's §0c to begin. This is the first: the brief the plan dated 2026-10-16, written five days early, and the one issue of the four that turned out to need no index change. One pull request. No index version, no CloudKit deploy, no re-index. One shared kit file.

**The brief** is `Planning/Index-Bump-Brief-2026-10-11.md`. It measures each item, says what each fix stores and touches, gives the order, and lists six decisions for the owner with a recommendation each. What it found that the plan did not have:
- **#1535 is not an indexing defect.** `TEIParserDelegate` already promotes a prose-only compilation, chapter or subchapter, and each is a row Search finds. Only Browse's rule refused them.
- **#1536 is larger than filed and is not mostly lists of papers.** 1,332 document-holding sections in 137 volumes print text of their own at corpus `99d851c79`, 1,210 of them of the three kinds the issue counted (it gave 1,237 at an earlier corpus). 485 are the table of those present at a meeting, in five wartime conference volumes. The text carries 1,609 cross-references that no table holds.
- **#1599: history.state.gov lists a document's people and terms in its sidebar** from the `ana` pointers, with no link in the text (document 368: 7 persons and 5 terms, its 12 pointers). The app has no list of a document's people, so the fix needs one or the reader shows nothing.
- **#1613's rows are drawn**, as a placeholder node in a document's graph named after the volume, and counted by the collection inspector and `edgeCount`. The rankings already refuse them.
- **The same shape for footnotes: 17,087 rows** store a reference to a note as an edge to a document named after the note. `inboundEdges` matches the id exactly and the rankings refuse `*fn*`, so a document cited through one of its notes gains nothing from it. 80 web addresses and 46 mail addresses are stored as cross-references too.
- **The film sections' leaked player text is 2 rows**, where §0a estimated 12 from the code.
- **The bump is three pull requests**, each with its own version (66, 67, 68), as build 49 took 63 to 65. A reader re-indexes once, at the build that carries all three.

**How it was measured**
- *The index:* the full index on the `iPhone 17e` simulator (553 volumes, 316,768 rows of `document_cache`, built 2026-10-08 at version 65), opened read-only with `sqlite3` and from Python. Cross-reference targets were classed by `GLOB` on `target_document_id`; sections by walking each volume's stored outline and looking each section up in `document_cache`.
- *The corpus:* Python's `xml.etree` over the 553 files `manifest.json` names, at `99d851c79`. A section "holds documents" when a `<div type="document">` is anywhere inside it, and its own text is what its children other than `<head>`, `<pb>` and `<div>` hold.
- *history.state.gov:* documents 1 and 368 of 1981–88 vol. XVI and document 1 of vol. XI, opened in a browser; the sidebar's two panels were read from the page after its script ran.
- The scripts were scratch files and are not committed. The brief's §6 says what was not measured.

**#1535, what was built**
- `FRUSCoreKit/Browser/VolumeStructure.swift`: `compilation`, `chapter` and `subchapter` join `VolumeSection.proseReadableKinds`. `canReadDirectly` is unchanged: it still refuses a section that holds a document or a section, or has no `xml:id` of its own.
- On iPhone and iPad such a section shows **Read** and its title where it said "No documents in this section."; on the Mac its row in the volume's contents opens in the reader. Both paths already existed for front matter.
- Comments in `CompilationView.swift` and `MacCorpusBrowserWindow.swift`, edited in place so no line moved and no `Docs/EditableContent` range needed re-pointing.

**Tests** (`ProseOnlySectionReadingTests`, a new suite in `FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/TEIParserTests.swift`, run by Xcode and by `swift test`)
- The kit's own structure parser reads a small volume, and a prose-only chapter, subchapter and compilation each answer `canReadDirectly`.
- One section breaks each rule and none breaks two: one holds a document, one holds a section, one has no `xml:id`. Each stays a list.
- `parseDocument(documentId:volumeURL:)` gives each prose-only section its own text and neither of the others'.
- **Against the unfixed code** (the three kinds taken out again, the suite alone through `swift test --filter`): 3 issues, one for each kind, and exit 1. With the fix: 4 tests passed.

**Seen in the app** (1919 Paris Peace Conference, vol. XIII, whose Introduction holds four chapters of prose)

The chapter shows **Read The Paris Peace Conference, 1919** over the line "This section contains prose content rather than individual numbered documents.", where it said "No documents in this section." The button opens the chapter in the reader, beginning "The treaty of peace with Germany brought to an end the principal phase of a war which lasted 51 months".

It shows the Prose Section page with **Read The Paris Peace Conference, 1919**, and the button opens `frus1919Parisv13/ch1` in the reader with the same text.

**Checked**

Its warnings are the two known residues and the condition's own "code after 'return' will never be executed". No other Mac build was made.

**Not done**

## Session 2026-10-11 — Index version 66: a cross-reference to a footnote is an edge to its document and one to a whole volume a link between volumes, and three stored values lose their noise (#1613); the owner's answers to the brief

Pull request A of the index bump (`Planning/Index-Bump-Brief-2026-10-11.md`), begun in the session that wrote the brief, on the owner's word, after #1637 merged. Index version 66, so every library re-indexes once at the build that carries it. No CloudKit deploy, no `@Model` or stored property, no table or column, no bundled file. Kit code.

**The owner's answers** (2026-10-11): "take first five recommendations. build 50 will carry the bump.", and, after asking why the Subject-Numeric files were declined and being given the reasons with fresh counts, "add subject-numeric to the brief as pull request D." The brief's §4 records the six, its §3.7 is now pull request D with the counts read from the version 65 index (9,443 citations: 6,830 with a class key, 2,419 with a series and none, 194 with neither), and its §2 and §5 say four pull requests and build 50 after the last.

**What was built**
- **Cross-references** (`FRUSCoreKit/Search/IndexingPipeline.swift`).
  - `crossReferenceRow(…)` builds the row for both walks, `collectDocumentRefs` and `extractCrossReferences`. It returns none for a web or mail address, and gives a row that names a footnote or a whole volume what it settles as (`SettledCrossReferenceTarget`), by `FRUSURLScheme.resolveCrossRefTarget`, the rule the reader's link follows.
  - The rows are inserted as written, as before. `settleCrossReferenceTargets` rewrites them in the store pass after `markBrokenCrossReferences`, which matches a row by its raw target, and beside page resolution. A footnote's row takes the document that holds the note; a volume's row takes the volume as `target_volume_id` and an empty `target_document_id`. A row the broken-reference pass marked is left raw, so the library-wide re-marking still finds it.
  - `auxInsertCrossReferences` hands back both maps the later passes need (`InsertedCrossReferences`).
- **The app's queries** (`FRUSExplorer/CrossReference/CrossReferenceStore.swift`): `outboundEdges`, `edgeCount` and `documentTargetPredicate` refuse the empty id (`namesADocumentPredicate`). The volume-to-volume queries are untouched and count the new rows as they stand. `inboundEdges` and the rankings take a footnote's reference with no change, since it now names a document.
- **Terms** (`TermsParserDelegate`): a term and its definition are folded with `normalizedWhitespace`. The lookup's fold from #1582 stays.
- **Video figures** (`FRUSASTNode.printedFigureChildren`, `FRUSASTNode.videoPlayerElements`): the text the index stores leaves out a video player's elements and the loose text beside them, as the reader's converter already did. The converter now reads the same list. `body_hash` is the reader's text and does not move.
- **Persons** (`PersonsParserDelegate.monthDayPattern`): a month may carry a comma before its year with no day between.

**Measured through the kit's own parser and extraction**, over the 553 catalogue volumes at corpus `99d851c79` (a throwaway package test, 76 seconds, not committed), against the version 65 index of 2026-10-08:
- 316,814 documents and sections. Version 65 collected 185,655 references; 66 collects 185,529. The 126 between are the addresses: the index held 80 beginning `http` and 46 that were `mailto:history@state.gov`.
- 17,088 rows settle as a note's document, in 232 volumes, 273 of them in another volume. The index held 17,087, every one naming a note of a document that exists, and none marked broken.
- 6,944 rows settle as a volume, in 406 volumes: 5,688 name a catalogue volume, 1,256 one of 57 volumes outside it, and 249 the citing volume itself, which the volume queries leave out as a self-reference.
- **Why 6,944 and not the corpus's 8,266:** the index collects a reference only inside a document or a section it holds. The other 1,322 are in text it does not hold, a section's own text (#1536) among them. They were not broken down.
- 66,203 terms and definitions, none holding a line break, where the index held 198 terms and 49,517 definitions that did.
- No document's text holds `298x530` or `brightcove`, where two rows did.
- 63,033 persons-list entries. Ten, in six volumes, differ in their years from the index, and each prints "until Month, year": six go from a start to an end (Keyserling in `frus1952-54v02p1` and `p2`, Robertson and Dillon in `frus1958-60v17`, Davies in `frus1964-68v21`, Mestiri in `frus1969-76ve05p2`), and four gain the end beside a start the same entry gives ("until April, 1972; … from May 1972"). Lane PAGE had estimated about twenty years, seven of them an entry's only one.
- The bundled broken-reference index names no footnote, whole volume or address (0 of 142 records), so the raw-row rule leaves no row today.

**Tests**
- `SettledCrossReferenceTests` (`FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/BrokenRefsPipelineTests.swift`, 4 tests): a volume indexed through the pipeline's own store pass leaves the five rows expected and none for the addresses; a footnote and a whole volume that a broken-reference index names keep their raw targets and marks, and the library-wide pass finds the row again; both walks collect the same rows.
- `StoredNoiseTests` (`TEIParserTests.swift`, 3 tests): the terms, a video figure beside a figure with no player, and four persons entries, through the kit's parser.
- `WholeVolumeReferenceRowTests` (`FRUSExplorerTests/CrossReferenceStoreTests.swift`, 4 tests, the app's alone): a document's outbound edges, its edge count and the ranking leave a volume's row out, and the volume queries count it.
- **Each fix removed in turn**, one at a time, with the test that failed named: eleven in the kit (an address collected again, a footnote and a volume not settled, each of the two statements settling a broken row, the pass not called, a term and a definition unfolded, a video figure printing everything and keeping its loose text, the comma refused) and three in the store (the edge list, the edge count, the ranking). The first run found none failing for the volume statement's broken-row condition; `aBrokenWholeVolumeReferenceStaysRaw` was written for it and fails without it. The kit's were run in a second worktree, since the first attempt ran them in the tree an Xcode build was reading, and both were stopped and restarted.

**Seen in the app** (1969–76 vol. XXXVIII Part 1, `frus1969-76v38p1`: 231 references, 23 to a whole volume and 58 to a footnote)
- *iPhone 17, iOS 27.0* (the simulator, the volume copied in and indexed by the app): Document 24 cites Document 8 and, as a whole, `frus1969-76ve15p2`. Its Cross-References sheet lists **Cited By This Document: 8. Address by the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Kissinger)** and nothing else. Document 7 lists **Cites This Document: 12. Remarks by President Nixon** and **13. Memorandum for the President's File…**, each "See footnote 4, Document 7."; the version 65 index held no reference to Document 7 from either.
- *The Mac* (the check copy, built from this branch): its index was at version 65 with one volume, and on launch the app re-indexed it and stamped 66. Read by SQL, the same volume holds 231 rows, 23 with an empty document id and none in footnote or volume form; Document 24's two rows are `d8` and the volume; Document 7 is cited by `d12` and `d13`; and none of 175 terms holds a line break. **The Mac's screen locked before the graph could be clicked**, so nothing of this was seen drawn on the Mac.

- `swift build --target FRUSCoreKit`: complete. `swift test`: exit 0, 38 `Test run with` lines, 2,610 tests, of which 7 are new, and no failed line.

## Session 2026-10-11 — Index version 67: 1981–88 vol. XVI's people are mentions, and the reader lists the persons and terms a document names on its `@ana` (#1599)

Pull request B of the index bump (`Planning/Index-Bump-Brief-2026-10-11.md`, §3.3), begun on the owner's word after #1638 merged, in the session that wrote the brief and pull request A. Index version 67, so every library re-indexes once at the build that carries the bump. No CloudKit deploy, no `@Model` or stored property, no table or column, no bundled file. Kit code, and one app file.

**The volume.** Since the Office of the Historian's corrections of 2026-09-14, `frus1981-88v16` names the people and terms each document mentions on the document div's `ana` attribute and marks none of them in the text. history.state.gov lists them beside the document. The app read only inline `persName corresp` and `gloss`, so the volume's documents had no person link and no term link, and its people gained no mention from it.

**What was built**
- **The parse** (`FRUSDocumentAST.annotatedReferences`, `FRUSDocumentParser.swift`): a document carries its `@ana` pointers as written. `annotatedId(_:)` reads the id a pointer names in its own volume and refuses one into another file; the two copies of a document (`carrying`, `applyingClassificationOverride`) keep the pointers.
- **The index** (`IndexingPipeline.annotatedPersonRefs(_:persons:)`): a pointer whose id the volume's own persons list holds is a `person_mentions` row, beside any the text marks. What a pointer names is known only from the list that holds its target, so the pipeline asks the list and does not read the id's prefix: 163 persons-list ids in 22 volumes and 370 term ids in 4 do not begin `p_` or `t_`. `currentDateIndexVersion` 66 → 67.
- **The reader** (`ListedReferences`, `ASTToRenderNodeConverter.convert`, `FRUSRenderNodeHTMLSerializer`, `ReaderRendering.swift`, `ReaderPage.swift`): the converter resolves the pointers through the reader's person and glossary lookups, each once and in the document's order, and the reader's two serializers write them after the footnotes section as two lists under one rule, headed **Persons** and **Abbreviations & Terms** as history.state.gov heads them. Each entry is the link an inline name or term would be, with the same class and the same `frusexplorer://person/` or `frusexplorer://gloss/` address. The section is outside `.frus-document`, as the footnotes section is, so the offset engine does not walk it. An export's serializer writes no lists. The stylesheet gains `.named-references` and `.named-list`, with no new colour.
- **The app's link handler** (`FRUSURLSchemeHandler.register(model:)`): it also registers the listed persons and terms. See *Found on the screen*.

**Found on the screen, and fixed.** The first build wrote the lists, and on the iPhone a tap on a name opened "Person Information Unavailable — This volume was indexed before the app recorded details about people." The app answers a link from the entries of the page it registered, which it gathers from the link nodes of the body and the footnotes, and the lists are in neither. `ListedReferences` had carried an id and a name; it now carries the volume's own `PersonEntry` and `GlossEntry`, as a link node carries its entry, and the handler registers them. The kit's tests had passed: they held the markup and that each address is one the reader reads, and nothing drove the handler. `theAppAnswersATapOnAListedEntry` does now.

**Measured through the kit's own parser**, over the 553 catalogue volumes at corpus `99d851c79` (a throwaway package test, 61 seconds, not committed):
- 316,814 documents and sections. **88 carry `@ana`, all in `frus1981-88v16`**: 1,041 pointers, of which 622 name an entry of its persons list and 419 an entry of its terms, none names neither, and none points into another file.
- **622 new mentions**, of 117 of the 120 people the volume's list holds, in all 88 documents. None was already marked inline.
- Every other mention is as it was: 611,482 inline mentions. The index of 2026-10-08 holds 611,307, and the 175 between are two volumes upstream changed after it was built (`frus1952-54v09p1`, 3,632 to 3,812, its restored documents; `frus1945v01`, 2,777 to 2,772, its list of persons moved). No other volume differs.

**Tests**
- `NamedReferencesTests` (`FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/ReaderRenderingTests.swift`, 10 tests in the package and 11 in Xcode): one fixture volume followed from the file to the parse, to the index's mentions through the pipeline's own store pass, and to the reader's page. Its first document names two people and three terms its lists hold and, each once, a person twice, an id no list holds, and a person through another file. The others are marked inline only, both ways, and terms only. The page is compared whole; an export and a converter with no lookups write none; and the rendering version of the document with and without the attribute is the same, with the page of one a prefix of the other's.
- The Xcode-only test drives `FRUSURLSchemeHandler` with the reader's model and expects the volume's own entry for a listed person and a listed term, and none for a person the document does not name.
- `ReaderPageTests`: the eight pinned heads are re-taken, each 537 bytes longer, all of them the two rules and their comment; the comment above the pins says so.
- **Each fix removed in turn**, with the test that failed named: seventeen in the kit (the parser not reading the attribute; indexing not adding the mentions; every pointer a person; a pointer into another file read as this volume's; a repeated pointer listed twice; no terms listed; the person lookup not asked; every serializer writing the lists; the reader's and a host's writing none; each copy dropping the pointers; an empty list headed; an empty section written; a name unescaped; a person's link written as a term's; a term listed by its definition) and two in the handler (the persons not registered, the terms not registered). One pattern of the first run did not apply and was re-run. The kit's ran in a second worktree.

**Seen in the app** (1981–88 vol. XVI, Document 368, whose `@ana` holds 7 people and 5 terms)
- *iPhone 17, iOS 27.0* (the simulator, the volume copied in and indexed by the app; 622 mentions, 117 people, 88 documents in its index): the document ends, under its footnotes and a rule, with **PERSONS** (Allen, Belaúnde Terry, Bushnell, Fontaine, Haig, Reagan, Valverde) and **ABBREVIATIONS & TERMS** (Exdis, OAS, S/S, S/S-O, USG), the names in the person-link colour and underlined, the terms with a term's dotted rule. With the fix, **Haig, Alexander Meigs, Jr.** opens List of Persons: "Secretary of State, from January 22, 1981, until July 5, 1982", "Mentioned in 20 indexed documents". **Find all mentions** opens Search narrowed by him with 20 results, Documents 368 and 369 first.
- *The Mac* (the check copy, built from this branch with the fix; its index re-made at version 67, the same 622, 117 and 88): the same two lists under Document 368. Haig opens the card with the same role, "Mentioned in 25 indexed documents", which is the 20 and 5 more in `frus1969-76v38p1`, where the same person is listed, through the reconciled identity. **OAS** opens "Organization of American States". Document 7 of `frus1969-76v38p1`, which marks its names inline and has no `@ana`, ends with its footnotes and no list.
- **Pull request A's Mac walk, made in the same sitting** since the screen was unlocked (`frus1969-76v38p1`):

- `build-for-testing` of the `FRUSExplorer` scheme (iPhone 17, iOS 27.0), over the build folder the session's earlier pull requests filled: `** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, and no warning line but the two known residues.

**Not done**
