## Session 2026-10-12 — A Live Activity that nothing is driving is ended at launch, and an activity the app has stopped updating says so (#1642)

Pull request #1655, the fifth of the plan of record's queue, worked ahead of pull request 4 (build 50) on the owner's word of 2026-10-12: the number had not been bumped when the session began, the session stopped and asked, and the owner said to go ahead. Nothing in it depends on the bump. No index version and no CloudKit schema change.

**The defect, seen on a simulator for the first time.** The issue was read in the code. On an iPhone 17 simulator made for the session (iOS 27.0), with the build of `fa80a894`:
- The app was terminated 1.5 seconds after `liveactivitiesd` logged "Created activity", while it indexed one volume. The Dynamic Island went on showing the download mark and "…", and the Lock Screen the volume's title over "Parsing…".
- 2 minutes 43 seconds later, after a background launch and a foreground launch of the same build, the Lock Screen still read "Parsing…". `liveactivitiesd` logged no end.
- With no stale date the system scheduled no "Marking activities stale" task for it.

**What the system does, measured from `liveactivitiesd`'s log on that simulator**
- **It marks no activity stale sooner than two minutes after an update.** A stale date 30 or 60 seconds after the update was scheduled at 120 seconds; 180 and 600 were scheduled as asked. Each update moves the mark. So the app asks for 120 seconds (`LiveActivityLifecycle.staleAfter`), and every sentence that describes this says two minutes. The first version asked for 60 and would have said "a minute".
- **It ends an activity itself after eight hours** ("Ending activities" was scheduled 28,800 seconds after creation), as Apple documents.
- **Ending an activity it already lists as ended dismisses it.** One with 71 seconds of its dismissal still to run was removed by the launch's sweep.
- **It refuses an activity asked for in a background launch.** After a reinstall stopped a leftover ("Stopping uninstalled activity"), the system opened the app in the background (`BG-Active`). That process ran the launch's pass over a waiting volume and indexed it; the app asked for an activity six times and none was created. Measured on the unfixed build; the fixed build adds no request, and a background launch of it ended a leftover and asked for none.
- **Tapping Allow on the Lock Screen's "Allow Live Activities from FRUS Explorer?" opens the app in the background** ("Launching process to deliver push token"), twice of two (Allow, and later Always Allow). The launch asked for 11 seconds after the first was handed that process and showed the onboarding wizard: a second route to what `LiveActivityPolicy` records. `CLAUDE.md`'s fifth rule for UI runs and the runbook say so now.
- **It suspends the app about two seconds after the device is locked** (9 seconds once), which is the common way an index stops: the reader leaves the app.

**The owner's decision of 2026-10-11, as built**
- **A leftover is ended at launch.** `AppState.endLeftoverLiveActivities()` is called once on the boot path, after the launch has decided which index passes it will run, and again as each of those passes ends. `LiveActivityLifecycle.isLeftover(_:driver:)` is the rule, a type with no system state in it: an activity the system still shows, which this process neither started nor took over, and which no run here is about to take over.
- **The activity of a pass the launch resumes is kept.** Each of the launch's three passes (the whole-library pass, the rebuild from the cache, the pass over volumes left unindexed) says it will begin before its task is made (`launchIndexPassWillBegin()`), and while one is in flight a live indexing activity is spared: the pass takes it over at its first update, as it did before. Spared only while live, only for its own kind's run, and only in a process that may show an activity, so a leftover does not sit through a whole pass when the reader's switch is off.
- **A leftover is dismissed at once**, not after the three seconds a finished run's activity lingers: a dismissal that comes due after the app has gone opens the app again in the background.
- **It runs in every process**, a test's and a background launch included. It starts nothing and can only remove. A test's process may show none (`LiveActivityPolicy`, unchanged, and its three tests pass unchanged), so it spares none.
- **Every update carries a stale date**, two minutes out, built in one place (`AppState.liveActivityContent(_:)`).
- **A keep-alive, which the decision did not name and the measurement asked for.** A run reports when it has something to report. The merge that ends a whole-library pass is silent for 30 to 60 seconds on a full corpus, and a summarization run while it lists a large scope's documents, for minutes. A stale date counted from the run's last report would pass there with the app at work. So while the process holds an activity it sends the last state again every 30 seconds. Measured with a scratch build whose pass reported once and then nothing, over 75 volumes: without the loop the system marked the activity stale at 120 seconds, with the pass still indexing; with it the pass ran 3 minutes 51 seconds and was never marked, the loop sending seven times.
- **The widget draws a stale activity as stopped** in each presentation: the icon is a grey pause mark, the bar is held grey at its last fraction (a state with no fraction has no bar), the count and the seconds left give way to "Indexing has stopped. Open FRUS Explorer to continue." (or "Summarizing has stopped. …"), and the small Dynamic Island shows a pause mark where the percentage was, with that sentence as its VoiceOver label. `ContentState.detail(isStale:)`, in the file both targets compile, decides it, stale first.

**Seen on the simulator** (iPhone 17, iOS 27.0; a device made for the session and deleted since). Every look below was made on the build that had the two-minute stale date and came before the review. What the review changed is below it in the code too: the sweep records what it ends and the two take-overs ask, the pause mark has a VoiceOver label, and the minimal presentation is two branches that draw what one line drew. So the two launch cases were run again on the final build, on a second simulator, and read from the system's log alone; they are the last item of this list. The widget was not looked at again.
- *Killed while it indexed, nothing else to index.* Terminated 17:23:24. Lock Screen at 17:23:47: the title over "Parsing…". The system marked it stale at 17:25:23. Lock Screen at 17:25:31, dimmed and lit: a grey pause mark, the title, "Indexing has stopped. Open FRUS Explorer to continue." on one line. Home Screen: the Dynamic Island with a grey download mark and a pause mark. Opened at 17:26:18 in the foreground: ended and discarded at 17:26:20.3, no activity asked for. Dynamic Island empty, Lock Screen clear.
- *The same in a background launch.* An earlier leftover was ended 1.75 seconds after the system opened the app in the background.
- *Killed with another volume still to index.* The relaunch did not end the leftover. Its pass took it over 3.2 seconds after launch (the system's stale mark moving with each update, no new activity created) and ended it when the volume finished, and the system dismissed it three seconds later: the sweep at the pass's end did not cut that short.
- *Suspended, not killed.* Locked during a whole-library pass; the system suspended the app. 35 seconds later the Lock Screen still showed a blue bar, "1,900/1,960 docs" and "~0s". 120.0 seconds after the last update the system marked it: grey pause mark, the bar grey at the same place, "Indexing has stopped. Open FRUS Explorer to continue." Brought back to the front: an update reached the system 0.39 seconds later and the activity was current again, on a later volume.
- *The summarization sentence*, on a scratch build that labelled an index run as a summarization run, since no summarization runs on a simulator: it wraps to two lines on the Lock Screen and fits; the expanded Dynamic Island holds it on one, under the title and the grey bar.
- *The final build, from the log.* Killed while it indexed with nothing else to index, and opened again: ended 6.5 seconds after the launch ("state: active; should be discarded now"), no activity asked for. Killed with another volume waiting, and opened again: no end at the launch; the pass's first update moved the system's stale mark 7.6 seconds after the launch, with no activity asked for or created; ended when the volume finished, and dismissed three seconds after that. Both launches were slower than the earlier ones because the Mac was building for the Mac and booting that simulator for the first time (load above 300).
- **Not seen:** a real summarization run's activity; the minimal presentation (it needs another app's activity beside it); a device; an iPad's Lock Screen; a stale mark heard with VoiceOver.

**Found, and left as found**
- **In a queue indexed volume by volume, every other volume can have no activity.** The activity is ended at each volume's end and lingers three seconds; a volume that starts within them takes over that ended activity, and no update reaches it. Measured on the unfixed build: of three volumes in one launch pass, the first and third had an activity and the second none. The doc comment that said the Dynamic Island "does not flicker between volumes" was removed, and a comment where the activity is taken over says what happens. Ending the activity with the queue and not with each volume would fix it and would let a queue indexed in the background keep its activity; it is a change to what the Lock Screen shows through a queue, and the owner's to ask for. In §5b of the plan.
- **A volume the background task re-indexes after a kill has no activity.** Before, the leftover was still there, hours stale, for that run to take over. Now the launch has ended it, and none can be started from the background.
- **Between two background runs of a batch with Continue in the background on, the activity reads "Summarizing has stopped"**, though the app will summarize again by itself at the next wake. Each state is true when it is shown; the sentence is the owner's to change, in its block.
- **The app asks for an activity at every progress update while it is in the background**, up to ten times a second, and is refused each time. Six in the launch measured.
- **A volume whose pass throws keeps its banner and its activity** for as long as the app runs, or until a later volume finishes: no `.complete` arrives, and the queue's watchdog waits for one. The keep-alive goes on calling that activity current meanwhile. Once the app stops it goes stale like any other, and the next launch ends it.
- **The activity's title is empty through the finishing merge** of a whole-library pass: the update names no volume.
- **"~0s" is printed for most of a volume**: the seconds left are a whole number, and a volume takes a few seconds.

**The review, one pass at medium on the diff, and what it changed.** Seven findings.
- *The keep-alive calls an activity current for as long as the app runs when its run ends without a `.complete`* (a volume whose pass throws). **Left, after a fix that did nothing was taken out.** The first answer ended a held activity when the queue is torn down. Read again, the teardown cannot run with one held: the queue's watchdog waits for `currentIndexingProgress` to be cleared, only a `.complete` clears it, and the same turn ends the activity. So the line was removed with its pin, the keep-alive's doc comment says what it cannot tell, and the cause, which pins the queue's banner the same way, is in the list above.
- *The sweep's end is not instant, and a run that is not a launch pass could take the same activity over before it landed.* Fixed: the sweep records what it has ended, and neither take-over accepts one of those.
- *The pause mark in the small Dynamic Island had no words for VoiceOver.* Fixed: the stopped sentence is its label.
- *A wiring pin matched an exact indent.* Loosened.
- *The block table, the amendment log and this entry were not yet written.* Written.
- *Also left:* the background re-index above, which follows from the decision; and a brace-matching helper the new suite repeats from `LiveActivityPolicyTests`, which is not to change.

**Tests.** `LiveActivityLifecycleTests`, a suite of its own in `IndexingSummaryCardTests.swift`, 16 tests. `LiveActivityPolicyTests`' three pass as they were: two requests, both in `AppState`, each behind the policy.
- The leftover rule with one fixture for each condition alone: dismissed, driven, and each of the three conditions of being spared (live, its own kind's run, a process that may show one).
- The system's five states; the stale date and the keep-alive's four turns; what a stale activity shows over each of the three states it can cover, and that a current one shows what it did.
- On an `AppState`: a launch pass is a run from `launchIndexPassWillBegin()` until its end, two passes do not end each other, a summarization run counts while it runs, and a test's process spares none.
- In the source, for the calls a test's process cannot make: one place builds content and it carries the rule's date; the sweep dismisses at once and records what it ends; the boot sweeps once, after its three passes have spoken, and each pass's end follows its call; the widget switches on the rule in both places.; and the small island's pause mark carries the sentence for VoiceOver.
- **Mutation, on committed trees, the failing test named for each.** Twenty-two mutations in ten runs, each set between a passing run of the unmutated tree before it and after it. The fifteen that change what the app does were run on the tree before the teardown line above was taken out, and the rule's code did not change after; the seven source pins were run on the final tree. Each condition of the rule dropped alone failed its own fixture: *dismissed* ("One already dismissed is no leftover"), *driven* ("One this process drove is its own"), and of being spared, *live*, *a process that may show one* and *its own kind's run* (each "It is spared only while live, only for its own kind's run, and only where a run may show one", in a run of its own or with a mutation no fixture of that test reads). A stale activity read as ended, and an ended one as live, each failed the states test. A launch pass that never counts, one whose end does not count, a summarization run that does not count and a driver that may always show each failed its `AppState` test. Stale not first, the finishing phase after the fraction, and a stale date of 60 seconds each failed theirs. Of the source pins: the sweep dismissing after three seconds, not recording what it ends, a pass that does not say it will begin, and content with no stale date failed six expectations in one run, each its own; and a take-over that ignores what the sweep ended, a pause mark with no label and a view that never reads stale each failed one, in a run of its own. The pins read the source when they run, so they were run against the final build with no rebuild.

**Docs**
- `Docs/iOS-User-Manual.md`: §4.7's Live Activity paragraph says what the activity does when the app stops and when it is opened again, and §13.4's says the same of a summarization run. The Mac manual has no Live Activity and is unchanged. The AI Generated notice stands.

**Checked**

## Session 2026-10-13 — FRUS Explorer Light can call the concordance, the facets, the facet panel's narrowing and selection, the Query Inspector's model and the result list's date order, which the app now calls in the kit too

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`) serves the Mac's exported index read-only. Its phase-1 search features are the facets with include, exclude and Apply, the Query Inspector, the list's date order and the concordance, and the shared code for them was internal or lived in app files. Nothing the app shows changes.

**Changed**
- **The concordance is public:** `KWICLine`, `KWICSort`, `ConcordanceResult` and `SearchService.concordance(for:parameters:radius:)`. `KWICBuilder` stays internal.
- **The facets are public, and the panel computes a section through the search service.**
  - The types in `ResultSetFacets.swift` are public, and `FacetDisplayState` and `FacetRequest` have public initialisers with the memberwise ones' labels and defaults.
  - `SearchService.resultSetFacets(parameters:request:documentKeys:)` is `FacetPanelController.load`'s route, moved: the search's match expressions and filters, or a meaning search's keys with neither.
  - `load` calls it and no longer takes the pipeline; both hosts drop the argument.
  - One difference, in a Debug UI test only: with `UITestBrowseSeams.holdsPipeline` set, the app publishes `appState.indexingPipeline` late, and `load` computed nothing until then. The service has its own pipeline, so the panel now computes. Nothing else sets `searchService` without `indexingPipeline`.
- **The narrowing and the staged selection are kit code.**
  - `FacetNarrowing` moved to `FRUSCoreKit/Search/FacetNarrowing.swift`. Its subject case read `DocumentSubjectStore.shared`, so `apply(to:resources:)` reads the vocabulary from the `IndexingResources` a host gives its pipeline. The app keeps `apply(to:)`, which passes `.bundled`, whose subject provider is `DocumentSubjectStore.shared`.
  - `FacetSelection.swift` moved whole. `FacetPanelController.stagedSections` moved beside the applier as `FacetSelectionApplier.stagedSections`, and the controller's name forwards.
- **The Query Inspector's model is kit code.** `QueryInspection.swift` moved whole, its reads public, and `QueryInspector`'s three passes are public. The parse-taking entries, the refusal probe and `Inputs` stay internal.
- **The date order is kit code.** `SearchSortOrder` moved to `FRUSCoreKit/Search/SearchSortOrder.swift` with `sorted(_:)`, the comparator both view models kept a copy of. Both return it now. The order is unchanged, and the enum gains `String` raw values.
- **Tests**, under both compilers unless marked:
  - **Moved into the kit's suites:** `FacetSelectionTests.swift` (19 of its 25 tests in the package) and `QueryInspectionTests.swift` (41 of its 54). What needs the app is inside `#if !SWIFT_PACKAGE`: the staged-selection lifetime suite, the two scope-signature tests, and the inspector's 13 tests of its controller, the iOS view model, the strip and its hosts, whose source scans climb one folder more. `QueryInspectionTests` imports FTS5Store `@testable` for the parser's nesting limit.
  - **The narrowing map's five tests** moved from `FacetPanelControllerTests` to `FacetNarrowingTests` (new).
  - **New:** `ResultSetFacetsTests` holds the service's facets to the pipeline's by both routes and to the search's count (3). `FacetNarrowingTests` reads a subject bucket's key from the host's resources, and none without them (1). `FacetSelectionTests` holds the staged sections to the applier (1). `SearchSortOrderTests` (new) holds the three orders (3).
  - **Changed:** `FacetPanelControllerTests` loads without a pipeline. `FacetMeaningModeTests`' route check reads the service. `SubjectResultsFacetTests`' filter-only gate scan reads `QueryInspection.swift` where it moved.
  - **Count:** FRUSCoreKitTests goes from 950 tests in 126 suites to 1,022 in 132.
- **Docs.**
  - `CLAUDE.md`: the folder table's `Search/` row, and the FRUSCoreKit entry's public names.
  - Version-history lines.
  - In `Docs/EditableContent/07-Search-and-Browse.md`, 60 ranged blocks are re-pointed by the distance their keys moved, with an amendment-log entry. No block's text changes.
- **Size:** the kit goes from 34,043 lines in 49 files to 35,258 in 53.

**Apple platforms: nothing changes, and how that was checked**
- **`FRUSExplorerMac`**, clean, unsigned Debug, beside `v2` @ `13e093ba` built the same way: "** BUILD SUCCEEDED **" both, with the same five warning lines. The debug dylibs define 238,930 and 238,920 unique symbols.
- **The symbol diff** (normalized as for #1573–#1579): 27 removed, 37 added.
  - **Removed:**
    - `FacetPanelController.load` with its pipeline parameter, and its async parts;
    - the two view models' sort closures and their copies of `dateOrder`;
    - `SearchSortOrder`'s derived `hash(into:)`, `hashValue` and `==`, which its raw values replace;

## Session 2026-10-13 — FRUS Explorer Light can call the BibTeX, RIS and Zotero exporters, the TEI's publication year, the display title, the header display and the reader's footnote landing, which the app now calls in the kit too

FRUS Explorer Light (`joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App`) serves the Mac's exported index read-only. Its phase-1 Cite offers BibTeX and RIS, its lists name a document as the app's lists do, and its reader lands on a footnote a reference names. The code for those was in app files, two copies of the TEI year scan among them. This is the second of its two phase-1 pull requests. The first, #1664, merged as `9feff971`, and this branch is rebased on it. Nothing the app shows changes.

**Changed**
- **The exporters are kit code.**
  - `BibtexExporter`, `RISExporter` and `ZoteroJSONExporter` moved into `FRUSCoreKit/Citation/`, the last with the Zotero items the other two render.
  - `fetchTagsAndNotes`, which reads SwiftData, stays in the app, unchanged, in `ZoteroJSONExporter+App.swift`.
  - The two exporters that imported nothing import Foundation.
- **The TEI's publication year is kit code.** `TEIPublicationYear` (`read(from:)`, `year(inHeader:)`) is the scan iOS's `DocumentViewModel` and the Mac's `DocumentExportSupport` each kept a copy of, verbatim. Both call it, off the main actor as before, and each keeps its own fallback for a header that states no year.
- **The display title is kit code.** `DocumentDisplayTitle` moved to `FRUSCoreKit/DocumentView/`, with `Facts`, which was `CrossReferenceStore.DocumentTitleFacts`; that name is its typealias now. `DocumentHeaderDisplay` moved to `FRUSCoreKit/Search/` whole.
- **The footnote landing is kit code.** `FootnoteLanding.script(anchor:)` builds the script `_FRUSWebViewCoordinator.revealFootnote(on:)` built, byte for byte, and the coordinator runs it.
  - `script(keyExpression:)` takes the key as JavaScript, for a host that has the key only when the script runs.
  - `FRUSURLSchemeHandler.revealedFootnoteGlobal` forwards to `FootnoteLanding.revealedGlobal`, which the script sets and the figure retry reads.
- **`FRUSCanonicalURL.volumeURL(volumeId:)` is public:** the page a reference to a volume outside the catalogue opens.
- **Tests**, under both compilers unless marked:
  - **Moved into the kit's suites:** `DocumentHeaderDisplayTests`, `DocumentDisplayTitleTests`, `RISExporterTests` and `ZoteroJSONExporterTests`. What needs the app is inside `#if !SWIFT_PACKAGE`: the header display's scan of the four rows that draw it, the Cross-Reference Analytics labels, and the tests that read tags and notes from SwiftData. The header display's source scan climbs one folder more.
  - **New:** `TEIPublicationYearTests` (5): the bare year, `@when` first, 1751–2099 only, no statement, and the file's first 8 KB. `FootnoteLandingTests` (4): the key, encoded, the global and the wash, and the script's text pinned by SHA-256 and length. `FRUSCanonicalURLTests` (2).
  - **Count:** FRUSCoreKitTests goes from 1,022 tests in 132 suites at `9feff971` to 1,061 in 139.
- **Docs.**
  - `CLAUDE.md`: the folder table's `Search/`, `TEI/`, `DocumentView/` and `Citation/` rows, the kit's folder list, and the FRUSCoreKit entry's public names.

## Session 2026-10-14 — The Gemma licence re-read, the EmbeddingGemma 2 spike in the plan of record, and a ballpark for the re-embed on the Air

**What was asked.** The licence situation of the embedding model behind the semantic features and what it means for shipping a Meaning search with no gate for the reader, in the app and in FRUS Explorer Light; a ballpark for re-embedding the corpus with EmbeddingGemma 2 on the M5 MacBook Air; and a pull request that puts the spike in the plan of record. No code changed.

**What was found.** The memo `Planning/semantic-vectors/EmbeddingGemma-2-Spike-2026-10-14.md` has the whole reading with its sources; the headlines:
- **EmbeddingGemma 300m is unchanged** under the Gemma Terms (page last modified 2026-04-01, the Prohibited Use Policy 2024-02-21, the Appendix naming it; `license: gemma`, gated). Every obligation is built except the custom App Store EULA, which is drafted, not entered, and owed before the first App Store submission; the app is TestFlight-only.
- **Under the Terms the app's gates can move and cannot go.** Weights in the binary are still Distribution; without a download moment the custom EULA is the only enforceable provision for App Store copies and the Mac DMG has none; bundled weights cannot be recalled under §4.5. The vectors, shards and map are Outputs and already ship gate-free.
- **EmbeddingGemma 2 is Apache 2.0** by Google's announcement, its documentation, the Hugging Face record and the card's licence link, which goes to the Gemma 4 licence page, the plain Apache text. Under it the consent sheet, the EULA clause, the Terms screen, the policy re-reads and the termination exposure all go, in the app and in the web edition. Two things only secondary coverage reports, for the owner to read on the card: a kept "Deployments must adhere to the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy" sentence, and no LICENSE file in the repository.
- **The web edition under the Terms:** a hosted Meaning search in a multi-user instance is Distribution to its readers (§1.1(b)), so the operator owes the §3.1 flow-down in its own terms with them. FRUS Explorer Light's phase 4 design has the admin's acceptance and no reader-facing terms; its single-user localhost mode has no third party. Recorded for the owner; nothing changed there, per `CLAUDE.md`'s rules.
- **The runtime:** llama.cpp gained the `gemma-embedding2` architecture on 2026-10-06 (PR 30054); the vendored `llama.xcframework` was last rebuilt 2026-10-05 at commit `8663224`, so a move rebuilds it with a new dSYM release. Upstream llama.cpp drives the M5's neural accelerators through the Metal tensor API (PR 27461); LM Studio's runtime 2.21 is reported to fail that self-test on M5 Macs and fall back, 2 to 3× slower on prompt processing.
- **The ballpark for the Air,** chained from the Studio's measured 5.96 h for 605,643 chunks and about 353.7 M tokens: 6 to 9 hours if the accelerators engage, 10 to 18 if they do not; the harvester's ETA settles inside the first hour. Nothing about the model was measured.

**What changed.**
- `Planning/Plan-Of-Record-2026-10-11.md`: decision 10 (the owner's, 2026-10-14: the spike is queued), queue row and bullet 10, the order line, the §3 bullet marked decided, and the EULA line of §3's App Store Connect bullet.

- `Planning/semantic-vectors/EmbeddingGemma-2-Spike-2026-10-14.md`: new. The licence reading for both editions, the spike in two stages (the runtime, the file and the Air's throughput in an afternoon; the full re-embed with the corpus gates and the 25 judged queries as stage 2, which is the move's largest cost paid in advance), what a move would touch, the ballpark, and what is not verified.

The new model keeps more of its own neighbourhood under truncation (recall@10 0.921 at 512 against 0.878). The 300m through the new runtime reproduces the shipped store chunk for chunk (cosine ≥ 0.999982) and Gate A exactly.
- **Latency and memory**, the step-4 method: 2.14 ms a query warm and 688 ms cold, against 1.66 ms and 390 ms for the 300m on the same runtime.

- **The pack:** a control repack of the shipped store into scratch is byte-identical to the bundle; EmbeddingGemma 2 packs under digest `89481b18…` at 512 and `cafefae8…` at 256, with sign bits equal to the numpy pool's for every document.

## Session 2026-10-15 — Filters keeps its volume-scoped groups when the app opens on Search, and the Meaning seam's suite reads the rows of the question it asked

**What was asked.** A session B4's second pull request started: find out why `MeaningResultsSeamTests.testAFarQuestionInsideAWorkingCorpusRanksEveryMemberWithAVector` failed on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27.0, `80CF0F18…`) at Filters, "Filters has no My Working Corpora group after 8 swipes", before its Meaning search, on B4's branch and at `v2` `28dd78a0` alike, while it passed on the iPad Pro 13-inch and had passed on both on 2026-10-11; and fix it, in the test or the app.

**What was found.**
- **The app's.** Search loaded Filters' volume list (`SearchViewModel.availableVolumes`) once, in the tab's `.task`, from `appState.indexedVolumeIds` as it stood then, and Filters draws My Working Corpora, My Volume Scopes, By Subject and Limit to Volumes only while that list holds a volume (`showVolumeScopeSections`). Boot publishes the search service and reads the indexed set afterwards, in a task of its own (`AppState.seedIndexedVolumeIds`), so a Search tab the app opens on can read the set first. Logged in the app on the iPhone: the tab's `.task` read an empty set at 14:54:11.07, boot's read began at 14:54:12.04 and landed with the fixture 43 ms later, and Filters then saw the saved corpus (`workingCorpora=1`) and no volume (`availableVolumes=0`). The recording shows Filters going from Date Range straight to Person.
- **Why only that iPhone.** The window's saved scene decides the tab a run opens on (`frus.selectedTab` in the app's `Library/Saved Application State`; `-frus.activeTab` seeds only a window with none). The iPhone's held Search; the iPad's held Collections, so Search appeared when the test tapped it, six seconds after the read had landed (logged); an iPhone 17 under iOS 26.5 held Browse and got past Filters. The tree at #1634 (`9d247985`), built and run on the same iPhone with the same `-only-testing`, failed the same way, so nothing since 2026-10-11 caused it and there was nothing to bisect.
- **The test's.** On the 26.5 iPhone the test then read Three, Two, One where the list settled on Two, Three, One (build 50's model): `ask` waits for a third fixture row, and the list already held three, from the Meaning search that choosing Meaning runs on the field's text, so it read them while they were replaced. The delete keys also left `content"` after the question, since a tap on a focused field puts the cursor where it lands.

**What changed.**
- `SearchView` (1.29): `reloadAvailableVolumes()` reads the list when the tab appears, when the panel opens (as the Mac's `syncToFilterVM` does) and whenever `appState.indexedVolumeIds` changes, which also keeps a selected subseries' scope (`effectiveVolumeIds`) current.
- `MeaningResultsSeamTests` (1.2): `submit` empties the field with its Clear text button and waits for the list to empty.
- `FilterVolumeListTests` (new, in the same file): the fixture cold at launch, its download finished on the test's signal from Search, and Filters ▸ Limit to Volumes ▸ Volumes read before and after.
- `Docs/EditableContent/07-Search-and-Browse.md`: eight ranges into `SearchView.swift` re-pointed, each 30 lines on. `CLAUDE.md`'s suite table and the UI-test runbook: the finding, the guard's row and entry. This entry.

**Checked.** The guard on the code before the fix: failed at its last assertion on the iPhone 17 and the iPad Pro 13-inch (iOS 27.0), with the volume indexed. On the merged tree (after B4's two pull requests), each device, iOS 27.0: `FilterVolumeListTests` 1 of 1 and `MeaningResultsSeamTests` 3 of 3. A clean `build-for-testing` printed only the `GeneratedSummary` residue.

**Not done.** The issue for the defect is drafted for the owner, not filed. The other readers of `indexedVolumeIds` found by a search read it when they use it, but for the Mac's `CrossReferenceGraphWindowView`, which keeps a copy of its own and was not examined. Not run: the macOS app, which builds this file but uses its own Search window.

## Session 2026-10-15 — A2: on the Mac a hand-off or a recalled search runs inside the applied working corpus, a search a later one replaced writes nothing, and #1647's two checks are tests (#1646, #1647, #1648)

**What was asked.** The plan of record's A2, started by the session that ran A1 once #1678 had merged: fix #1646, #1647 and #1648 in one pull request, with one review pass; check #1647's two open questions before it closes; and bring the plan's status lines up to date (A1 merged as #1678, #1659 closed on the owner's word).

**#1646 (Mac).** `MacSearchViewModel.applyParameters` dropped the snapshot's document gates and with them the applied working corpus, while the banner (`filterVM.appliedWorkingCorpusName`) went on reading *Inside “name”*. Reproduced in the Mac check copy at `678dec75` (36 volumes of 1961–63): with a corpus "Berlin" of 1,829 documents applied, the saved search "Khrushchev" came back with 1,610 rows (inside the corpus it has 724) and the filter row read *no filters … everything indexed*. Three changes:
- `SearchParameters.runningInside(workingCorpus:)` (new, `Search/SearchModels.swift`): a hand-off's only document gate is the applied corpus; the snapshot's own gates go. `applyParameters` builds the window's parameters by it. iPhone and iPad already composed the gate so, and a test holds both to the rule.
- `mirrorParameters(into:)`, split out of `syncToFilterVM`: `applyParameters` brings the filter view model to the new parameters, which it kept at the search before the hand-off.
- `leaveWorkingCorpus()`: the banner's ✕ derives the document gate alone. It called `applyAdvancedFilters()`, which copies back every field from the filter view model: seen in the copy, after Find all mentions it dropped the person and emptied the list; found in review, it undid any facet's narrowing, which writes the window's parameters alone.

**A recall's stamp.** Both recall sites stamped a saved search with the total on screen, which inside a corpus is the corpus's; the badge counts the saved search's own parameters, so the next time the list appeared it counted every match outside the corpus as new. That was already so on iPhone and iPad, and the Mac fix would have made it so there. `SavedSearchFreshnessEvaluator.recordRun(of:service:indexedVolumeCount:context:)` counts the saved search itself; in the copy the recall inside "Berlin" showed 724 and stamped 1,610.

**#1648 (both).** Nothing under a search checks for cancellation (`SearchService`, `FTS5Store`, the Meaning engine), so a replaced run ran to its end and wrote over the newer one. `SearchRunLedger` (new, `Search/ResultSetScope.swift`) numbers each run; `search()` and `performSearch(service:)` and their Meaning branches wait for all a run fetches, ask once whether a later run has replaced it, and write it all together only if none has, leaving `isSearching` to the latest; both return `true` when theirs was not replaced. A refusal, a switch of engine, `clearAll()` (only tests call it) and `replaceSearchesUnderWay()` (the emptied field on iPhone and iPad, the rebuilt index on the Mac) replace the run under way. The hosts record a run, and the Mac starts its facets over, only when it was not replaced, and the Mac's search task is its only search: the recall and the rollup rebind no longer run a second one beside it. No kit change, so nothing for the web edition: the replaced query still runs to its end. #1577 lane 2's `aMeaningRunThatLandsLateShutsTheDoor` asserted the defect as its precondition and is now `aMeaningRunThatLandsLateIsDropped`.

**#1647.** Both checks pass on the code #1676 left, and are tests now (`FilterVolumeListReloadTests`): a read keeps the reader's choices, and a subseries takes in a volume indexed since; a hand-off applied before boot's read searches the same volumes as one applied after, with each volume a single choice in Filters rather than their subseries, so a volume of that subseries indexed later joins only the later one. Nothing was changed for it; closing it is the owner's, and a comment is drafted.

**The review** (one pass, a single reviewer over the diff) found three defects and some wording, all taken:
- A hand-off or a recalled search with no words empties the field itself, and its search can be under way before the field's handler runs; the handler's new replacement would have dropped it and left the empty prompt. The handler asks `SearchViewModel.isSearchingWithNoWords` first and leaves such a search alone.

## Session 2026-10-15 — #1648's second step assessed: how long a newer search waits behind one it replaced, and how the kit could stop the replaced one's statements

**What was asked.** Started by the A2 session after #1679 merged: assess, and build only on the owner's word, the step #1648 left for the kit, stopping the SQL of a search a later one has replaced. First deliverable a memo: measure the wait on a large index, read how the pipeline runs a statement, and weigh three designs with their risk for other statements on the connection and for FRUS Explorer Light. No code changed.

**What was found.** `Planning/Issue-1648-Stopping-A-Replaced-Search-2026-10-15.md` has the figures and the reading; the headlines:
- **A newer search waits for the whole remainder of the one it replaced**, at two actors: on the pipeline behind its ranking statement and its count, and on `SearchService` behind its snippet pass. Measured over build 49's library on the pinned iPhone 17e simulator (553 volumes, 316,768 documents), driven through the kit's read-only open in a throwaway release-mode package test on the M5: 0.5 to 0.9 s late at iPhone and iPad's 1,000 rows and 1.0 to 4.1 s at the Mac's 7,500, warm; 8.1 s and 10.1 s in all behind a cold filtered common word; 134 s behind `=government`. With the heavy run's task cancelled, as the Mac's `.task(id:)` cancels it, nothing changed: 48 of 48 cancelled runs returned their rows.
- **The search statements run on the pipeline's own connection** (`auxDb`), not FTS5Store's, and the first `sqlite3_step` is most of each one: the ranking pass scores and sorts every match before a row comes back, so a check between steps cannot stop it.
- **All three ways of stopping a statement worked as fast**: a flag read by `sqlite3_progress_handler`, `sqlite3_interrupt` from another thread, and the task's cancellation read by the handler each stopped every shape tried within 0.3 to 1.5 ms (2 to 13 ms for an exact-word statement); the handler at 1,000 instructions cost nothing measurable. They differ in what else they can stop: only a handler armed per statement by a task-local leaves the connection's other statements alone (shown: unarmed in a cancelled task, and outside any task, the statement ran to its end), where `sqlite3_interrupt` on the shared connection could stop an indexing write and roll back its transaction.
- **Recommended**: design (b), the armed progress handler, with cancellation checks at the statement boundaries and in the snippet loop, and iPhone and iPad cancelling the run they replace; the Mac needs nothing new. Its own pull request: no index bump, no CloudKit change, no public signature; compiles on Linux with no new import. Before A5 or after build 51, the owner's call.
- **Found on the way**, now in the plan's §6g (a section of its own: #1697 filed §6e's groups meanwhile): an exact-word search for a common word holds the pipeline for about two minutes; on the Mac most of every search is the snippet pass; and the default scope's user-content union costs a common word's count about 0.3 s where the corpus alone costs milliseconds.

**What changed.**
- `Planning/Issue-1648-Stopping-A-Replaced-Search-2026-10-15.md`: new.
- `Planning/Plan-Of-Record-2026-10-14.md`: a §4 bullet for the owner's decision (removed again once the owner decided, below), and a bullet with the three findings, in §6g since #1697 filed §6e's groups. A2's own lines are left for the next lane's session, as A2's hand-over arranged.
- This entry.

**Not run.** No test reads the new memo; `CodingStandardsAuditTests.planOfRecordMatchesTheVisualMarketingPlan` reads the plan's §7 line, unchanged. The throwaway harness (`ZZSupersededSearchWaitTests.swift`) was deleted before the commit, and the cloned index removed. Nothing measured on a phone or on Linux.

**Not done.** The issue is drafted in the memo's §8 and not filed; nothing is built or pushed. Waiting on the owner's word.

## Session 2026-10-15 — A2b: a search a later one replaced stops its statements, so the newer search no longer waits behind it (#1680)

**What was asked.** The owner's word on the assessment above (decision 43): file #1648's second step as drafted in the memo's §8, place it in Track A before A5, and build it in this session as its own pull request. Filed as #1680 and placed as A2b, next in the queue, ahead of A3, since it was built at once and nothing else was open; the owner can move it anywhere before A5. #1681 merged meanwhile and numbered the owner's other answers 20 to 42, so this decision is 43.

**What changed.**
- **The kit** (`FRUSCoreKit/Search/IndexingPipeline.swift`, `SearchService.swift`; nothing in `FTS5Store/`): `SearchStatementStop` registers one `sqlite3_progress_handler` on `auxDb` in the shared initialiser, which stops a statement only when the task-local `isArmed` is set and the running task is cancelled; `searchDocuments` and `searchDocumentsCount` run their statement through `stoppingWhenCancelled(_:)` (no statement prepared for a task already cancelled, the statement armed, `SQLITE_INTERRUPT` in a cancelled task thrown as `CancellationError`, and a check after the statement, so a task cancelled at any point before they return gets no answer), with a test hook that reports a statement prepared and run to its end; `SearchService.search`'s snippet pass is `results(from:parameters:)`, which checks cancellation at every row and after the last, with a row hook.
- **iPhone and iPad** (`SearchViewModel`): the keyword fetch is a task of its own (`keywordFetchUnderWay`), cancelled by `startRun()` and `replaceRunsUnderWay()`, the only two ways the screen replaces a run. The ledger stays.
- **The Mac**: one line, from the review: `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return false }` after `performSearch`'s last wait. Its `.task(id:)` already cancels and its catch already returns on `CancellationError`, but a run cancelled by the window closing after its rows came back lost only its count, read as nil through `try?`, and as the latest run it wrote its rows with no total and the window recorded a history entry without one.
- **Docs**: `CLAUDE.md`'s Search data flow (and: register no other progress handler on `auxDb`), both manuals' *While a search runs*, the plan of record (decision 43, A2b, the TestFlight notes' line, and §6g for the assessment's three findings, since #1697 filed §6e's groups meanwhile); three EditableContent ranges re-pointed, with the Amendment-Log bullet, the memo's status, and the doc comments of the two pipeline methods, `SearchService`, the ledger and both view models.
- **Tests**: `SearchCancellationTests` (new, five, under both compilers): a search in a task already cancelled throws for the rows and the count and prepares nothing; a statement whose task is cancelled after the check at its start is stopped by the handler before its end; one over no match, too short to reach the handler, still gives a cancelled task no answer; the snippet pass stops at the row after its cancellation, and gives no answer after its last; and a keyed read and a whole volume's indexing, unarmed, run to their end in a cancelled task. `ReplacedSearchStopTests` (new, Xcode): on iPhone and iPad a second search cancels the first run's fetch while its statement is held, the held statement is stopped (three statements prepared, two run to their end) and the second lands with no error. A2's `everyWriteAfterAWaitAsksFirst` reads iPhone's opening line as `let run = startRun()`, with the reason beside it.
- **The review** (one pass, an independent reviewer over the code diff) found no defect in the stop or in the iPhone wiring, and three smaller points, all taken: the iPhone test claimed more than it pinned (now it counts the hook's moments); the Mac's cancelled run above; and the docs promised a stop "within about a millisecond" that a statement ending before the handler's next call does not get (now the checks after the statement and the loop drop a cancelled task's answer, and the docs say "usually"). The sweep that followed showed the per-row snippet check unpinned once the check after the loop existed, so the loop has a row hook and the test counts the rows reached.

**Checked.**
- `swift build --target FRUSCoreKit` and `swift test` on the merged tree: exit 0, 38 test runs, 2,905 tests in 347 suites (A2's 2,900 and this lane's five).
- The unit target on an iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27.0) of this lane's own, since another session was testing on the shared one: at `0926ae64`, the merged tree as pushed, 7,198 tests in 851 suites passed with the 6 known issues of #1606. Before the review's round a full run of 7,198 tests in 851 suites had three failures beside #1606's six known issues: the EditableContent range gate (three ranges this lane moved, now re-pointed) and two `RichTextRestingCapTests` presentation checks, which ran while the Mac check copy was building beside them and passed when run again, 21 of 21 on this simulator and on the shared iPhone 17.

## Session 2026-10-16 — A3c: the semantic map keeps redrawing after its Mac window is closed and reopened, and the research question's bar heads the Corpus Browser's detail column (#1700, #1701)

**What was asked.** Plan of record A3c (decision 51), started by the plan-of-record session once #1703 had merged: the owner's two Mac defects from a demo of build 50 that day, one pull request with each its own commit. #1700: the semantic map stopped redrawing (pans and zooms moved the labels and not the points; a lens changed the legend and not the map) after the same actions had worked earlier that day. #1701, a title alone: the research question's overlay obstructs the Mac Corpus Browser. Each was to be reproduced in the Mac check copy before anything changed, #1700 on a fresh launch and after the Mac had been idle and locked; if #1700 could not be reproduced, #1701 was to land alone.

**#1700, reproduced and found.**
- The owner's demo ran in a second macOS account, where build 50 had been running since 08:48 and the lid had closed at 08:52, 10:21 and 15:02 (`pmset` and WindowServer's logs). That process's own log, read without touching the account, names nothing about the map.
- In the check copy at `0b511628` (release, the shipped configuration): on a fresh launch zoom, pan and the Era lens all redrew; after the owner locked the screen with the map open (display off 20:22 to 20:26) they still did. **Closing the Semantic Analytics window and opening it again from the Analytics menu reproduced it exactly**: a pan moved the labels over still points, Zoom In spread the labels over an unchanged map, and Era changed the legend while the map kept Provenance's colours, stretched to the new height. The reopened window had the same window id: SwiftUI's `Window` scene hides a closed window and shows the same one, with the same view, again.
- With lldb on the copy (ad-hoc signed, `get-task-allow`): on a fresh map a zoom went `-[MTKView displayLayer:]` → `dispatch_source_merge_data` → `-[MTKView draw]`, called from the handler `__initCommon` installs on MetalKit's private `_displaySource` → `SemanticMapRenderer.draw(in:)`. Closing the window ran `-[MTKView _windowWillClose:]`, which calls `dispatch_source_cancel` as its last act; libdispatch then described the view's source as "cancelled, deleted" (a `data-add` source on the main queue). After the reopen, 71 `displayLayer:` merges produced no `draw`. `draw()` called on that same view from lldb drew the current camera and lens at once. iOS's `MTKView` has no such source or close handler (its methods and ivars dumped inside the iOS 27.0 simulator).
- The Debug Mac build the plan named was not made: the release copy reproduced it, and lldb read each call where the DEBUG probe prints one draw in 120.

**What changed.**
- **#1700.** The map uses MetalKit's explicit-drawing mode: `SemanticMapSurface.configure(_:)` (split out of `makeMap()` so the suite can configure a view of its own) sets `enableSetNeedsDisplay = false`, still paused. `SemanticMapRenderer.setNeedsRedraw()` schedules one frame on the next main-queue turn, and `drawPendingFrame()` draws it by calling each attached view's `draw()`; requests in one turn share it, as the source's merges did. `drawnViewCount` replaces `markedViewCount`, and `presentedFrameCount` counts frames committed with a drawable. The house rule holds: the map is still paused and draws only when something changes.
- **#1701.** Seen first in the copy, with a project whose question was set against Global Context: the bar, a top `.safeAreaInset` on the whole `NavigationSplitView`, was drawn over both columns' first rows (the sidebar's Browse header, a pushed volume's header line), which sat at the same height as with no bar. It now heads each view inside the detail column's `NavigationStack`, the root and what `navigationDestination` pushes, through `WorkingOnBarAbove`, which stacks it above content filling the column. The walk found why both halves matter: stacked above the whole stack (the first build), the bar was covered by every pushed view, which on the Mac takes the column's full height; and above a root that does not fill, the empty column's placeholder, it sat halfway down. `WorkingOnBanner`'s placement rule now says the Mac's split view is not exempt.
- **Docs.** Three EditableContent ranges re-pointed with an Amendment-Log bullet; the plan of record's A3c status. Neither manual changes: the Mac manual says only that the Corpus Browser and Search windows show the question in a "Working on:" banner.

**Tests.**
- `SemanticMapSurfaceTests` (48): the configuration case pins explicit drawing; the mutator and realization cases draw through `drawPendingFrame()`, after the registration's own frame so the first mutator cannot ride on it; a request is drawn on the next main-queue turn and three requests in one turn are one frame; and #1700's regression test hosts a view whose `displayLayer:` does nothing (`NotificationlessMTKView`, the Mac's condition made by hand), configured as the map's, in a real window, and requires the first frame and a pan's to reach a drawable within two seconds.
- The A/B, in a second worktree: with the old dirty-mark path put back (notifications on), the regression test failed on both expectations; the same old path with an ordinary `MTKView` passed it, so it is the dead path the test fails on, not the window. A first version waited one main-queue turn, and the control showed why that was wrong: MetalKit's own path draws at the next Core Animation commit, which can come after the turn.
- `ProjectHomeSummaryTests.corpusBrowserBarSitsInTheDetailColumn` (in `ProjectAdminServiceTests.swift`) pins #1701's placement by source (the Mac has no runtime test).
- Single mutations, each run alone in the second worktree, each failing the case named: dropping `camera`'s `didSet` fails the mutator case (pan, zoom, frame) and the regression test; drawing on the spot instead of on the next turn fails the scheduling case; dropping the `draw()` call (the counter still counts) fails only the regression test; the old inset on the split view, the bar on the root only, and the bar above content that does not fill each fail the placement scan.

**The Mac check copy** (`tools/mac-check-copy`, 36 volumes of 1961–63, access granted to the copy alone), walked at `710a360e`, whose app code is the final code: the map draws its first frame on opening; after closing and reopening its window, twice, Zoom In, a pan, Era and Provenance all reach the map; resizing the window to 1100 × 760 redraws it at the new size. The Corpus Browser with *A3c walk*'s question set: the bar heads the empty column with the placeholder centred below it; a subseries list, a pushed volume (its header line whole) and a pushed compilation each start below it; the sidebar's Browse header shows; Global Context removes it with no gap, the project brings it back on the open view, and Back keeps it.

## Session 2026-10-17 — §6g's identifier findings assessed: how many of the person authority's Wikidata and VIAF ids name someone else, and what a rule, corrections or withholding them would do to the bundle

**What was asked.** Started by the A4c session to begin on the owner's word once #1709 had merged (the owner's word came the same morning), based on `v2` at `b3272d86`: assess, and put options to the owner for, the two findings A4c sized and left (its review's §6.1 and §6.2). The first is the Wikidata ids that name someone else, with VIAF sized the same way. The second is the overlay entries that carry several people-ids and stamp one person's role text and ids on all of them. Measure each option's effect on the bundle after a byte-for-byte control. A memo; no build, and no rollup or index version.

**What was found.** `Planning/Person-Authority-Identifier-Assessment-2026-10-17.md` has the figures and every way of fixing them. The headlines:
- **About 1,600 of the bundle's 3,769 Wikidata links name someone else (42%)**, not A4c's 450. 190 links read from three strata of a finer test: 37 of 40 hard failures, 40 of 50 soft-only failures and 18 of 100 passing links are someone else. Among them are 176 items that are not people (NARA holdings, obituaries, a ship), namesakes (Senator Paul M. Simon as the singer-songwriter) and relatives (Herbert Hoover Jr. as his father).
- **VIAF**: about 580 of the 2,186 overlay ids that could be sized name someone else; 824 could not be sized, since no Wikidata item holds them and viaf.org allows 1,003 requests a day. A VIAF id's Wikidata holder and viaf.org's own cluster agree on 362 of 375.
- **The multi-id entries**: 15 of the 31 are different people (A4c named 12; also Einaudi, Truman and LeBreton), 18 records wear another person's role text, and the entries' own identifiers are mostly name-only matches to a third person.
- **The options**, each a real bundle through a mirror of the enrichment that reproduces the shipped file byte for byte:

  | Option | Wikidata links kept | Share right |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Withhold a hard failure | 2,968 | ~71% |
  | Withhold any failure | 2,430 | ~82% |
  | Keep only what the overlay's VIAF id or the registry's years corroborate | 1,355 | ~98% |
  | The recommended (b4): that, or a word of the record's registry remarks, with a VIAF id kept when its own holder passes | 1,857 | ~96% |
  | Withhold every overlay id | 0 | — |

  Under (b4), 1,609 VIAF ids stay at ~97% right. For the roles, giving a multi-id entry's role text only to the ids whose registry remarks hold it removes all 18 wrong ones and costs 10 duplicates their copy.
- **Option (a)**, identifier-only corrections, was run through the generator itself: 896 corrections for the hard failures alone. It matched the per-record rule on every record but four, and those four are the item-2 limitation: Raúl Castro and both Einaudis lose their right ids with the wrong ones.

**What changed.**
- `Planning/Person-Authority-Identifier-Assessment-2026-10-17.md`: new.
- `Planning/Plan-Of-Record-2026-10-14.md`: a §4 bullet for the owner's decision, and §6g's two A4c bullets given the measured figures.
- This entry.

**Checked.**
- **The control**: `PersonAuthorityIndexGenerator` at `b3272d86` with `GENERATED_DATE=2026-10-16` reproduced `person-authority-index.json` byte for byte (SHA-256 `a53e0c9a…`).
- **The mirror**: it matched the shipped Wikidata, VIAF and role values on all 12,836 records, and the file it writes is the shipped file's bytes.
- **Option (a)** through the generator in a scratch worktree, removed afterwards.

**Not run.** No test reads the new memo. `CodingStandardsAuditTests.planOfRecordMatchesTheVisualMarketingPlan` reads the plan's §7 line, unchanged. Nothing built, so no unit target or `swift test` was owed.

## Session 2026-10-17 — The collection editor's two UI suites wait 30 s, so the five tests that failed on `v2` in a 5 s wait pass again (plan of record §6g)

**What was asked.** From the plan-of-record session, once A4b (#1711) had merged: make the five collection-editor UI tests that fail on `v2` itself pass again by fixing the tests, not the app. They are `CollectionEditorTitleTests`' three Section defaults tests (#1413) and `CollectionProseRowRestTests`' `testALongIntroductionRestsOnItsOpeningWords` and `testTextColorKeepsALongNoteBlockOpenWhileItsPickerIsUp`, found in A4b and put in §6g. Raise the waits where a measurement shows they need it, say in each suite's doc, the runbook and `CLAUDE.md` what allowance the suites need, and run each suite whole on every device its runbook entry names. Test code and docs only: no app code, no index version, no CloudKit change. Based on `v2` at `35db74c0`.

**The cause, read from A4b's logs** (the `t =` lines of its runs of the two suites, 2026-10-17). Since Xcode 27.1 (installed 2026-10-16), a query for a control by its identifier (`app.descendants(matching: .any)[identifier]`) took 4 to 13 s at a run's median, and up to 28 s, on iPhone 17 and iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) (iOS 27.0) and iPad Air 11-inch (M4) (iOS 26.5); a query by label took about a second. XCTest first checks a wait's condition about 1.05 s after the wait begins. So a 5 s wait ran out while its first check was still running, whatever the screen showed. The suites' own `waitForAbsence` (an `XCTWaiter`) has no second check, and that is every failure: "The Section defaults sheet did not close" (`closeSectionDefaults()`), "Done did not put the keyboard away" (its first check of the settings sheet's Done took 4.3 s) and "The colour picker did not close". `waitForExistence(timeout:)` checks once more after it runs out, which is all that kept the other 5 s waits passing: all 61 waits for a control by identifier in A4b's runs of `CollectionEditorTitleTests` ran past their 5 s. Where a screen changed after both checks had begun, that failed too: once "Text Color opened no colour picker with a Sliders tab".

**What changed.**
- `CollectionEditorTitleTests`, `CollectionProseRowRestTests` and `CollectionEditorAddMenu` (one file): a `patience` of 30 s each, used by every wait, where most were 5 s and some 10: each `waitForExistence`, both `waitForAbsence` helpers, both `waitUntil` helpers, and the Add menu's lookup. A wait that is met returns at once. The precedent is `SearchBulkActionsTests.patience` and `MeaningResultsSeamTests.patience`. `TabBarNavigator`'s `resolveTimeout` is left alone: it falls back to its other routes, and no run measured it short.
- Each suite's doc says its waits and its allowance, with a version-history line; the runbook's two entries carry the cause and this lane's runs, and their commands pin each device's OS and pass 600 s; `CLAUDE.md`'s two index rows say "allow 600 s a test" and lose A4b's "fail on `v2`" notes.

**Checked.** Built for testing once (`TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED`, no warning from the changed file), then each suite run whole, one simulator at a time, with `-test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 600 -maximum-test-execution-time-allowance 600`:
- `CollectionProseRowRestTests`, iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5 (`4973970C`): 5 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failed, in 583 s; the introduction test 111 s and the Text Color test 137 s, the slowest. 2 of the run's 37 waits took longer than 5 s, the wait for the settings sheet's keyboard to go among them (about 5.3 s).
- `CollectionProseRowRestTests`, iPhone Air, iOS 26.5 (`2D758D07`): 5 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failed, in 590 s; slowest 129 s. 1 of 35 waits took longer than 5 s: the keyboard's going in `testALongNoteBlockRestsOnItsOpeningWords` (about 5.5 s), a test that passed in A4b's runs.
- `CollectionEditorTitleTests`, iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5: 9 tests, 3 skipped (the tab-tap tests, on the sheet route), 0 failed, in 1,081 s; the four heading tests opened the Add menu from the toolbar's overflow.
- `CollectionEditorTitleTests`, iPhone 17, iOS 27.0 (`80CF0F18`): 9 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failed, in 1,514 s.
- `CollectionEditorTitleTests`, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 27.0 (`9AB3A0C9`, booted for the run and warmed with one test, which skipped as it should): 9 tests, 3 skipped, 0 failed, in 1,222 s.
- The Section defaults tests took 139 to 348 s on the iPhone, 166 to 266 s on the Air and 191 to 342 s on the iPad Pro, so two of the three devices went past 300 s. In each run all five waits for their sheet to go took longer than 5 s (up to 11.6 s on the iPhone, 7.6 s on the Air, 8.1 s on the iPad Pro), and 22 to 29 of a run's 102 to 124 waits did.
- No run printed "Restarting after unexpected exit", "exceeded execution time allowance" or a launch failure. The file's edits after the build are comments only: undoing the three gives back the SHA-256 the run script recorded before building.
- `CodingStandardsAuditTests` (which scans the UI test files): 63 tests in 1 suite passed. No unit test reads the runbook or `CLAUDE.md`.

**Not done.** The queries themselves: an identifier lookup goes through `.any`, the slowest kind measured, and typed lookups might bring each test back under 300 s; not measured here. The plan of record's §6g bullet is left to the plan-of-record session.

## Session 2026-10-17 — A5, #1577 lane 4: Search Within These Results on iPhone and iPad, and a keyword search inside a set of documents tests the set as rowids (decision 53)

**What was asked.** From the plan-of-record session: build #1577's lane 4 as A5's first pull request, against `v2` at `632dc509`, with decision 53's faster SQL shape for a small gate in the same lane; lanes 5 to 7 each get a fresh session after it merges. Measure the gated statement before and after on a full index and quote both; pin the same rows in the same order with kit tests; A/B every new test; ask before pushing.

**Decision 53, the kit** (`FRUSCoreKit/Search/IndexingPipeline.swift`; its own commit)
- A document gate (`documentIds`: an applied working corpus, a project's History scope) was `(dc.volume_id || '/' || dc.document_id) IN (…)`, a test of each candidate row's key, so a statement driven by the match joined `document_cache` for every row the words match before the gate could discard it: one rowid seek into the index's largest table for each of a common word's matches across the corpus, whatever the size of the set. The assessment's §9 named it.
- The gate is now the rowids of its members, found through `document_cache`'s primary key (a `VALUES` list of the keys, one bind a member as before, split at the first `/`), tested against `m.docrowid` where the match drives the statement and `dc.rowid` where `document_cache` does. `filterConditions` returns a `FilterClause` that says whether a condition reads the row's own columns; with the gate alone, the ranking phase, the count and the facet match set drop their joins. With other filters SQLite tests the gate at the match's loop, before the joins.
- **Measured** on the A4 clone of the pinned 17e's library (553 volumes, index v69, `frus.db` 3.55 GB), copied with `cp -c` and opened read-only through the kit's own `SearchService` in a throwaway package test, cold on a fresh clone of the file and then warm, `government` (195,778 matches), the rows and the count sent together as the view model sends them:

  | Gate | rows, before → after | with the count, before → after | warm, after |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 327 documents (the top of a `Suez` search, 52 volumes) | 6,829 → 590 ms | 7,237 → 839 ms | 349 / 614 ms |
  | 1,000 documents | 7,107 → 791 ms | 7,390 → 919 ms | 512 / 650 ms |
  | 7,500 documents (the top of `Soviet`) | 7,469 → 859 ms | 8,237 → 1,020 ms | 462 / 611 ms |
  | none (the floor) | 852 → 855 ms | 1,016 → 1,018 ms | 476 / 639 ms |
  | 327, `petroleum` (19 rows) | 501 → 117 ms | 504 → 117 ms | 21 / 21 ms |

  Every case returned the same rows in the same order with the same scores and snippets (a digest of id, score and snippet length per row). The owner's iPhone logged 7,515 and 8,304 ms for its 327-document case on build 50, about the Mac's cold figure; the phone's figure after the change is the owner's to read from the same `gated-keyword` line, now that a gated keyword search costs what an unfiltered one does. In the `sqlite3` shell the statement alone read 145,859 pages before and 2,768 after (the count 145,350 and 2,182); a gate plus a date range 145,707 and 2,858; a browse with no words inside the gate was no slower (2,652 and 2,752 pages). Driving the match from the gate's rows (`rowid IN …` on the FTS table) was measured and not built: 0.41–0.46 s of processor for 327 members, since FTS5 recomputes bm25's statistics at each row, so it grows with the gate.
- `DocumentGateParityTests` (7, `FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/`, compiled by Xcode and by the package): the rowid gate against the key test it replaced, kept reachable for tests alone (`searchDocumentsGateByKeyForTesting`, `searchDocumentsCountGateByKeyForTesting`, and the facet path's joined parity shape, which now renders the gate by key too), over every filter shape, both match scopes, pages, tied scores, the gate's edge cases (empty, absent, repeated and malformed members, one member, 520 members), a browse with no words, the filter key set and facets; and the plans of the real statements, split out for that (`searchDocumentsStatement`, `searchDocumentsCountStatement`). **Seven mutations, each caught by its own test**, in a second worktree at the commit: the volume half keeping its slash (six tests), the joins kept in the ranking phase (the plan test alone, as it should be: the rows are the same), the gate-only count counting the whole match, the facet match set losing its gate, the gate's binds out of order beside a volume scope, a row-reading filter not counted as one, and the gate dropped beside another filter.

**Search Within These Results on iPhone and iPad** (the app; its own commit)
- `SearchLayering.swift` (new): `SearchLayerDirection` (words in a Meaning list, or a keyword list or browse ranked by a question; the other engine only, never stacked), `PinnedResultBase` (the held rows, the members the layer runs inside, everything a return puts back, the trail anchor set aside, and the base's sentences and record part), and `LayeredResultComposer` (a words layer in the base's order with its scores; a ranking with its unranked tail in the base's order; the gate composer the Mac's lane will call). `SearchLayerViews.swift` (new): the base row, the empty layer, and the copy.
- `SemanticSearchBackend.rerank(query:base:parameters:)`: the in-set search with the whole list as its limit, the list's own rows reordered with their keyword snippets, the unranked last, the other filters after. `DocumentScopeGate.combine(corpus:projectGate:pin:)`, the three-way gate.
- `SearchViewModel`: `holdBase(meaningAvailable:)`, `leaveBase()` (rows and every figure back from memory with no search, the version bumped), `leaveBaseKeepingTheWords()`, the field emptied inside a base (`fieldEmptiedInsideBase()`, asked by the field's handler before it clears anything), words found in a Meaning list inside `search()`'s keyword path and a ranking in a function of its own, `rankHeldList(run:base:backend:)`, which `searchMeaning(run:)` hands a held list to, so that the plain Meaning run reads as it did and only its rows are a Meaning list, the base joined to the gate in `searchParameters` alone, `isShowingBase` read from the search version, every hand-off leaving the base, Clear Filters not, the checklist kept through layers, the trail anchor set aside and given back, and a layer's row recorded whole with `base=` in its signature.
- `SearchView`: More ▸ Find Words in These Matches / Rank These Results by a Question after Select Results (before it, the item pushed Select Results out of an iPhone SE's menu at AX5, and `ResultSelectionBarFitTests` failed); Sort ▸ Closest to a Question… on a keyword list; the base row in `searchModePicker`'s slot; the field's prompt, focus and handler; the empty layer before both zero-states; the unranked rows' line; Save this search off with its second line; the More menu's help re-keyed to `.v4` (#1576 took `.v3`, so "the next suffix after #1576's" is `.v4`); VoiceOver announcements.
- `ResultSetScope`: `layerFiltersNarrowed` ("…and pass your filters"), `listIsInRankOrder` (no "closest first" under a date sort) and `layerBaseLabel` (a capture names both layers), the three notes lane 2 left owed answered. `FacetPanelView.preambleHeadline`: the layers' wording. `SearchScopeSignature.layered` and `describe`'s base phrase.
- **From #1683, in the files this lane edits**: "Describing all 1 matches", "Describing the 1 closest matches", a Meaning capture of one ("These documents…"), and the three "1 reviewed documents" sentences have their singulars; and Select Results is off while a search runs, which closes the iPhone and iPad half of "a selection begun while a switch's search runs lasts into the other engine's list". The checklist strip's and Collocates' ungrouped counts (`ChecklistStrip`, `CollocationView`), the Mac's lines and All N Shown past the add limit are not in this lane's files and stay on #1683.

**The review** (one agent, read only, over the app diff) found two medium defects, four low ones and three tests that could not fail as they claimed. Each is fixed, with a test that fails without the fix:
- A ranking with fewer rows than its list, for the rows the checklist hid when the list was held or a filter chosen since, read as a fetch cut short: a working corpus saved from it said "the highest-scoring 9 of 10" and was stored as partial. The scope now reads the list's own cut (`ResultSetScope.layerBaseWasCut`, from `PinnedResultBase.wasCut`), and the capture counts the reviewed rows the list left out (`layerBaseHiddenByChecklist`).
- Emptying the field after a layer put the list's rows back with the layer's words as the query a capture records: `restoreRows` gives the list its words back.
- Tags given to rows while a list was held were lost to the next layer and on leaving, since #1576 lane 5's refresh writes the rows on screen alone (and is pinned as the Mac's twin): the held list takes the tags of the rows on screen before they are replaced (`PinnedResultBase.takeUserTags(from:)`).
- Facets over a held list's own rows aggregated under the emptied field and the list's gate, a keyword list as an empty query and a browse as its loaded rows alone: `facetParameters` gives them the match that found them.
- "…and pass your filters" was said for a filter taken away and not said for one set in the sheet and never run: the list's filter signature is the run's, not the fields', and only a filter that is set can narrow.
- A hand-off that runs nothing (Search this volume) dropped the list and left the layer's rows and engine on screen, and every hand-off lost the sort a ranking had set aside: a hand-off now leaves the list as ✕ does. A list restored with a phrase alone was held as "your browse": it is a keyword list named by its phrase.
- The trail test reads which row the re-run refreshed; the refusal case holds an error over rows that are kept; the UI test's unranked-row check no longer passes over a row that is not drawn.

**Found by the fit suite.** `SearchLayerBaseRowFitTests` failed on the iPhone 17 at AX3 and AX5 once its own two flaws were fixed (it measured with the keyboard up, when the tab shell's banner gives way, and it opened the More menu before the Meaning engine had booted, so the menu was rebuilt under the tap). The top inset was taller than the screen: the base row's sentence took three lines (156 pt at AX5) where the Keywords | Meaning control takes one, and over a held keyword list the field's Meaning engine drew the strip's long opening under the actions bar. SwiftUI centred the inset, which put the row above the screen (y −143 to 13 at AX5) and the list's first row below it (y 952 of 874). The strip now waits until a question has ranked the list, and at the accessibility sizes the row draws its text at XXXL in two lines at most, its second line moved to VoiceOver and the Large Content Viewer: capped at AX1, as the selection bar is, it still took three lines on the iPhone SE and left a result no room above the banner at AX5 (9 pt short).

Brought to the new wiring, each saying why where it stands: the field's prompt, the scope's route, the route written beside every assignment of rows (iPhone and iPad assign rows in 11 statements now), the #1648 rule read over `rankHeldList` too, the trail's count, Select Results' dimming and the More menu's help key, a ranking's capture provenance, and the Meaning signature's wrapper.

## Session 2026-10-18 — The Save Search sheet opens with its Save on, on iPhone, iPad and the Mac, and #1577 lane 4's suite saves the name it offers

**What was asked.** From #1577 lane 4's session, once its pull request (#1715) had merged: Search ▸ ••• ▸ Save this search opened the Save Search sheet with the search's words as the name and its Save dimmed, doing nothing until the name was edited (seen in lane 4's UI run on the iPhone 17 and iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.1). Find the cause by measuring, fix it structurally, guard it with a UI test that fails on `v2` and passes after, on both devices at `OS=27.0`, check the Mac's twin sheet, and remove the space `SearchWithinResultsTests.testARecalledSavedSearchLeavesTheBase` typed to get past it. Based on `v2` at `f83acb37`. No index version, no CloudKit change, no kit code.

**The cause, measured.** A temporary probe (`Logger` lines in the More menu's action, `SearchView.body`, the sheet's content, its Save item and its `onAppear`; never committed) on the iPhone 17 (`2CD5886D`, iOS 27.0): the action set `saveSearchName` to the search's words and `showSaveSearchSheet` to true; no `SearchView.body` ran after it; the sheet's content read the name as empty and its own Bool as false, and built Save disabled; `onAppear` read both as set; and no body ran again for 44 s, while the test's wait found Save off at each of its six checks, until its teardown tapped Cancel. `SearchView`'s body reads neither `@State`, only the sheet's closure does, so setting them did not re-run the body, and the sheet was built from the closure made before the tap. The name field showed the words because a binding reads the stored value; `.disabled(…)` was worked out once from the old one. It was not the toolbar: the whole sheet was built stale, and the toolbar's Save is the one part of it that shows. #1590 (`NewPromptRequest`), #1051 B-7 (`SemanticMapSheetItem`) and #862 measured the same shape. **The Mac** (`MacSearchWindowView`, the same name-beside-a-Bool sheet), in the Mac check copy at `f83acb37` on a fresh launch: "test ban" in the name field, Save drawn dimmed at 1 s and 6 s, and a click on it did nothing. (A first look the same night read the window with `axread` before clicking, saw `AXEnabled=1`, and the click saved: the accessibility read had refreshed the sheet.)

**What changed.**
- `FRUSExplorer/Search/SaveSearchSheet.swift` (new): `SaveSearchRequest`, the item, carrying the search's words and the `SearchParameters` to save, with the offered name and `savedName(from:)` (trimmed, `nil` when empty, which is when Save is off); and `SaveSearchSheet`, one view for both Search screens, which keeps the name as its own `@State` set from the request, with iPhone and iPad's form under a navigation bar and the Mac's dialog as each was.
- `SearchView` (iPhone and iPad) and `MacSearchWindowView` (the Mac) each hold a `SaveSearchRequest?` in place of the name and the Bool, make one in the command's action (the parameters are taken then, where they were read at Save; a sheet is modal over its window, so it is the same search), present `.sheet(item:)`, and insert the `SavedSearch` in the closure they hand the sheet. Their own sheets and the Mac's `performSave()` are gone; the Mac keeps its merge of the submitted words into the parameters as `parametersToSave`.
- `SearchWithinResultsTests.testARecalledSavedSearchLeavesTheBase` saves the name as offered: the tap at the field's end and the space are gone, and its comment.

**Tests.** `SaveSearchSheetTests` (UI, in `SearchWithinResultsTests.swift`): the fixture's phrase listed, More ▸ Save this search, the name field holding the phrase, Save on within 30 s with nothing typed, Save closing the sheet, and Saved searches listing the name. `SaveSearchRequestTests` (unit): the request's name and identity, `savedName(from:)`, both screens presenting from the request with no `showSaveSearchSheet` or `saveSearchName` left (the Mac's half has no runtime test), and both of the sheet's bodies working Save out from the sheet's own name.

**Checked.** Each UI run alone on its simulator, `-test-timeouts-enabled YES` with 600 s allowances, iOS 27.0, from one build for the iPhone destination:
- **The control**, `v2` at `f83acb37` with only `SaveSearchSheetTests` added (`1236d269`; the probe was gone from the product, `strings` finding none of its lines): iPhone 17 (`2CD5886D`), 1 test, 1 failed in 92 s; iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) (`B2FF6BBE`, booted for the run), 1 test, 1 failed in 221 s; both at "Save is off though the sheet offers the name". (The probed build failed the same way on the iPhone, in 103 s.)

Two earlier iPad runs at the fix are not counted: in the first, the app the run launched stayed at about 100% of a core and never went idle while another session's `build-for-testing` drove the load average to about 900 and the Mac paged (13 GB of swap); the second passed `SaveSearchSheetTests` (194 s, Save on at the first check) and then lost its accessibility channel in the next test's `setUp` (`kAXErrorIPCTimeout` setting the orientation), so the iPad was rebooted for the third.
- `SaveSearchRequestTests` (5 cases), `EditableContentKeyTests`, `UnconstructedViewAuditTests` and `MacSheetToolbarPlacementAuditTests`: 39 tests in 4 suites passed.
