## Session 2026-10-20 — Browse's Index Now leaves `AppState` the indexing pipeline's one reader, so `AppState` no longer stops hearing indexing for the rest of a launch (found in A11, #1695)

**What was asked.** Started by the session that built A11, for a defect it found by reading and kept out of that lane, since it predates A11 and is none of #1695's lines: Browse's **Index Now** could stop `AppState` hearing the indexing pipeline until the app was relaunched. Prove it in the app first, with a unit test that fails on the code before every run and not by chance; then give the app one reader of the stream; run the Browse suites that tap Index Now, the unit target on iPhone 17 under iOS 27.0 and the Mac build; and this entry. Branch `claude/funny-matsumoto-75bee6`, cut from `v2` at `6dcd82b4` and brought to `92045991` (A11 merged, #1737) before anything changed. Where it lands in build 51's queue is the owner's to place (below).

**The defect.** `BrowserViewModel.indexVolume(_:)` read `IndexingPipeline.progressStream` in a task of its own, beside the loop `AppState.connectIndexingProgress(pipeline:)` runs from boot. The stream is a plain `AsyncStream`, which hands each element to one of the readers waiting on it, so during Index Now the two readers split the volume's updates. The view model cancelled its task when the pass returned, and when that task had not had the volume's last update (`.complete`, or since A11 `.failed`) it was still waiting in the stream's `next()`: cancelling a task that waits there ends the stream for every reader. `AppState` then heard nothing until a relaunch: no banner, no Live Activity, no queue, no `.complete` to record a volume as indexed. iPhone and iPad (Browse ▸ a compilation ▸ **Index Now**); the Mac's Corpus Browser has always read `AppState.currentIndexingProgress` and had no reader of its own. A11's session showed the stream's behaviour with a standalone script (each of two readers got every other element; after one waiting reader was cancelled every later `yield` returned `.terminated`); this session showed it in the app.

**What changed.** App code only: not kit code, no index version, no CloudKit change.
- **`BrowserViewModel.indexVolume(_:)` reads no stream.** It names the volume it is indexing (`indexingVolumeId`), and `indexingProgress` (now `private(set)`) is kept from `AppState.currentIndexingProgress` by `updateIndexingProgress(from:)`. An update for that volume replaces it; one for another volume (a downloaded volume can be indexing beside Index Now's) and `nil` (which `AppState` sets as a volume ends) leave it, so the progress section holds the pass's last report until the pass returns and clears it. With one reader the section follows `AppState`'s 10-a-second forwarding, where it had shown whichever half of the updates its own reader won.
- **`CompilationView`** hands `AppState.currentIndexingProgress` to the view model as it changes: one `.onChange`, placed ahead of the three indexing kicks.
- **`AppState.connectIndexingProgress(pipeline:)`'s doc** had said it was safe to call more than once and that the earlier subscription was abandoned. Neither was so: an abandoned loop goes on reading. It now says the method is the app's one reader of both streams and is called once for a pipeline (boot calls it once). `currentIndexingProgress`'s doc names its readers. Comment only.
- **Every other reader of `progressStream`**: none in the app. The kit's tests read it in `IndexingStageTests` and `IndexingPipelineTests`, each on a pipeline of its own with one reader. `metadataStream` has one reader, `AppState`.
- **EditableContent:** six ranges re-pointed for the moved lines (two on `CompilationView.swift`, one on `BrowserViewModel.swift`, three on `AppState.swift`), each to start on its key and keep its length; the Amendment Log has the bullet. No text changed.

**Tests.** `IndexNowProgressReaderTests`, a new suite in `FRUSExplorerTests/IndexingBatchLifecycleTests.swift` (an existing file, so the project is not regenerated), serialized, four tests.
- **After Index Now, `AppState` hears its volume end and hears the volume indexed next**, for a pass that completes and one that throws after its second batch (`.failed`). A real pipeline, `AppState`'s own subscription and `BrowserViewModel.indexVolume(_:)`; then a second volume through the pipeline, held after its store until `AppState`'s progress names it (its progress, its queue's latest update), then the indexed set. **The fixture gives `AppState` the pass's last update**: a volume indexed first leaves `AppState` the reader that has waited longest; Index Now's volume is four documents stored two at a time; and the pipeline is held after each batch until the main actor has run, so both readers wait again before the next update. The turns then alternate, and the fifth update, the last, is `AppState`'s. If they slip in the three updates that go out unheld, the view model's task takes the last update instead, and the test fails at the first volume, since `AppState` never hears it end.
  - **On the code before** (this branch's tests with the app at `92045991`), three iterations of each case: **6 runs of 6 failed**, every one in the forced case: `AppState` heard the pass end, then saw nothing of the next volume (no progress, no queue, not recorded as indexed). **After**: passed, three iterations.
- **Index Now shows `AppState`'s progress for its own volume, and keeps the last of it until its pass returns**: before a pass the view model keeps nothing; in a held pass it keeps `AppState`'s progress, keeps it when handed another volume's update and then `nil`, and the pass's return clears it.
- **Two source scans.** Each of the pipeline's two streams is read in one place in `FRUSExplorer/` and `FRUSCoreKit/`, `AppState.swift`; and `CompilationView` passes `AppState`'s progress on, read as the `.onChange` and its call together.
- **Mutation**, after a commit, the tree restored after each run. The scans read the source as the test runs, so their three mutations ran together on mutated files with no rebuild, each failing its own expectation: the code before's reader put back and a second `metadataStream` reader, each named by its line, and the forward removed. The view model's, each rebuilt: the filter dropped and the clearing at the pass's end removed, run together, where the filter failed three ways (kept before a pass, replaced by another volume's update, cleared by `nil`) and the clearing was masked, since the dropped filter let `nil` clear it first; alone, the clearing failed the last expectation. The volume id never set, alone: failed twice (no volume named, nothing kept).

**Checked.** Each heavy job through `Scripts/heavy.sh`, Xcode 27.1, on the shared iPhone 17 under iOS 27.0 (`80CF0F18`), at the final code unless said.
- **The suite**: 15 runs of 15 passed (four tests, one with two cases, three iterations).
- **The unit target**, with `TEST_RUNNER_FRUS_TEI_MIRROR` set: "Test run with 7475 tests in 881 suites passed after 397.578 seconds with 6 known issues" (A11's 7,471 in 880, and this suite's 4 tests in one more; the six are #1606's). The result bundle: 8,234 passed, none failed, 17 skipped, one expected failure.
- **The Browse UI tests on the Index Now path**, `BrowseNestedSectionTests`' two cold-fixture tests: `testIndexingFromTheCompilationFillsItsDocumentList` taps Index Now and waits for the rows (kick 1); `testAnIndexStartedElsewhereFillsTheOpenCompilation` leaves the volume to the post-download index and waits for the rows from `.onChange(of: appState.currentIndexingProgress)` (kick 2), the value the new forward reads too. The other suites tap Index Now only if a compilation offers it, which boot's indexing prevents. *iPhone 17, iOS 27.0*: the first passed (21 s); the second failed once, at the Browse root, where the Subseries tile's tap had not opened the subseries list 15 seconds later (the first launch after the app was installed; the UI tree at the failure is the root, and nothing past it ran), and passed alone on the rerun (21 s). *iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 27.0*, booted for the run and shut down after it: both passed (20.6 s and 19.1 s).
- **The Mac** (`FRUSExplorerMac`, Debug, this worktree's build folder): `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **` in 43 seconds, warning only of the `GeneratedSummary` residue. The Mac compiles the two Browse files and does not use them (`BrowserView` is iOS-only); its Corpus Browser was already `AppState`'s reader.
- **Warnings**: the incremental builds that compiled the changed files printed only the `GeneratedSummary` residue. A clean `build-for-testing` was not run.

**Placed by the owner.** Next, as A11b, ahead of A12: "Place it next as A11b, ahead of A12, and open its PR." (2026-10-20; plan of record decision 75, with A11b's row and bullet in §1). It touches `AppState.swift`, `BrowserViewModel.swift` and `CompilationView.swift`, so a later lane in those files merges after it.

**Not done.**
- **Opened as #1738** on the owner's word (above), against `v2` at `92045991`; not merged.
- **Not seen on a screen**: the progress section's look during Index Now (it reads the same `IndexingProgressUpdate` as before, now `AppState`'s), and a second volume's banner after an Index Now on a device.

## Session 2026-10-20 — A13: on the Mac a facet's volumes outlast a change of project, the dimmed Add to Collection and Add Tags say why beside them, and Collocates' Within picker shows its label (#1686, #1683)

**What was asked.** Plan of record lane A13 for build 51 (decisions 59 and 69, and §0's defaults for #1686 and for the Within picker), started by the session running the build-51 queue once A12 had merged as #1739. Three fixes in one pull request, each its own commit. **#1686**, on the Mac: a change of project put back the volumes chosen in Filters before a Volumes facet's choice, or every volume. §0's default is the issue's first way out, a change of project deriving only what a project changes; the session was to work out what a facet's volumes do when the new project's Focus scope also sets volumes, and say why. **#1683, Select over 1,000** (decision 69): All N Shown stays, and the dimmed Add to Collection and Add Tags say why beside them on every platform. **#1683, the Mac's Within picker**: look for it in the check copy, fix it if it reproduces. Based on `v2` at `2d674c9f`, brought there with the app's sync tool (the worktree's local `v2` lagged by A12's merge).

**#1686.**
- **Seen first, in the Mac check copy at `v2`**: a search for *Khrushchev* (1,610 results in 36 indexed volumes), Filters opened once, Facets ▸ Volumes with `frus1961-63v05` and `v11` included and applied (418 results, a *Volume: 2 volumes* token); Research ▸ Switch Project ▸ Global Context ran the search again over every volume: 1,610, no token, the facet's rows unchecked.
- **The fix** (`MacSearchViewModel`): the facet panel's two routes are the view model's, `applyFacetNarrowing(_:)` and `applyFacetSelection(_:keys:)`, where `SearchSheet` wrote the window's parameters itself; each remembers what a Volumes facet wrote (`FacetVolumeChoice`). `applyProjectScope()` derives the project's History and Focus gates as before and keeps the facet's volumes while the gate still holds them (`FacetVolumeChoice.volumeGate(_:choice:derived:)`); any other writer of the gate (an edit in Filters, a hand-off, a recalled search) replaces the choice, and the volume filter's ✕ forgets it before it derives the scope.
- **Where the new project's Focus scope also sets volumes, the facet's volumes stand over them**, as a volume selection made in Filters does (#377 Phase 2b's rule). A change of project sets the scope back to Entire corpus, so Focus applies only once the reader chooses it in Filters, which by then shows the facet's volumes as its volume selection, its footer counting "your N selected volumes". The facet's choice is the reader's own, made from the counts of the search on screen, where Focus is derived from the project's subjects; and iPhone and iPad behaved so already, since there a facet's volumes are the filter fields' own selection (`SearchViewModel.applyFacetSelection(_:keys:)`).
- **Seen after, in the check copy at the lane's tree**: the same steps kept 418 and the token through Switch Project ▸ A3c walk and back to Global Context; Advanced… then read *Volumes 2 selected*; and the token's ✕ cleared the volumes, both after Filters had opened and, with the facet applied again, before it had (1,610, *no filters*). Focus itself was not walked: the copy's one project has no focus subjects, so its footer is read from the code.

On iPhone and iPad the Actions menu's items carry it under their names: a second text in a menu item's label is its subtitle (`ResultSelectionBar.addRefusal`), and the line above the results is gone (`ResultSelectionStatus` holds the outcome alone). On the Mac a checked row's two items carry it the same way, and the strip says it under its two buttons (`addCommands`), the row kept on its text's baselines so the count, the menu and the other buttons stay on one line. The sentence loses the words the commands' names now say: *Select 1,000 documents or fewer*, re-keyed `search.selection.overLimit.v3 %@`.

Each takes its own size now (`.fixedSize()`), so Within shows its label and both caps, and the two labels start at one edge (Rank by, centred in its frame, had begun about ten points in). The Mac pane's popover shows its Smart Collection section for every collection: a linked one keeps A1's `SmartCollectionLinkRows`, and one not linked gets the button, which sets `opensLinkPickerOnClose` and closes the popover; the popover's `onDisappear` then presents the picker as a sheet on the pane, so it opens on the window, as the pane's other sheets do, not on the popover. A pick commits through `CollectionEditorCommit.savedSearch(_:to:)` and saves, as the popover's Unlink does; the Mac pane records no active project, as none of its commits do. **#1689.**
- **The fix**: `IndexRemainingSelection.volumeIds(among:pipeline:)` (`StorageHubModel.swift`), which both hubs' `indexRemaining()` call: each volume the index holds no document of, or one `volumesWithUnfinishedStore()` names, in the hub's order. That takes a volume the interrupted-indexing sentinel names (the launch's reconcile leaves it to Needs Attention) and one cut short after the launch read the sentinel; a volume the sentinel names whose last store pass finished (stopped before it began writing) keeps its rows and record and is not taken. Among the volumes passed over until now was one Index Remaining had itself just failed on after its first batch, though the failure row on iPhone and iPad says to try Index Remaining again. Both hubs disable the button while any pass runs (`actionsBusy` takes `AppState.indexingBatch` on both), so a volume being stored is not read as cut short.
- **The words**: on iPhone and iPad the line under the button reads *Only volumes not yet fully indexed.* (`settings.hub.indexRemaining.detail.v2`, was "Only volumes not yet indexed."); the Mac button's VoiceOver name *Index volumes not yet fully indexed* (`.a11y.v2`, was "…that have not been indexed yet"). The Mac's tooltip, the owner's "Indexes only the volumes that still need it, and leaves the rest untouched", was already true and stays.

The walk's made-up entries for sections the index leaves out (Persons, Sources, the table of contents, the index, and in `SectionOwnTextTests`' fixture an editorial note printed as a section) are no documents to add or graph; with no outline the stored order stands. The kit is unchanged. Add Documents' Select All adds in the new order. (The brief named `BrowserViewModel` as the merge's caller; it is the reader's `readingSequence(forVolume:)`, through `DocumentViewModel` and `MacDocumentView`. Browse lists a section's own text first through `VolumeSection.ownTextEntry(among:)`, the same order.)
- **Seen after**, at `5d86d6c6`: *Meeting of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, 10 a.m.* above its minutes in both lists, *Truman – Stalin meeting, noon* above the Bohlen notes and Bohlen's memorandum it holds, and every other meeting before its documents.

## Session 2026-10-20 — A15: an Archives Visit plan prints a divided lot's claimant line for a lot cited through the National Archives, and keys the 688 Department-worded notes by their stored class, with a join (#1692, #1691)

**What was asked.** Plan of record lane A15 for build 51 (decisions 59 and 62, and §0's default for #1692), started by the session running the build-51 queue once A14 had merged as #1741. Two fixes in one pull request, each its own commit. **#1692**: a `coll|` target whose record carries a lot passes the lot as printed, so a divided lot cited through the National Archives gets its claimant line; and the 21 series keys that carry more than one lot (323 documents) checked for a label or series taken from another lot. **#1691's second line** (decision 62): the 688 Department-worded notes keyed by their stored class, with a join that carries a tier, note or exclusion set under the old text key to the class target, general enough for A18's index bump, a rule for which row a target shows where several meet, and no CloudKit change. Based on `v2` at `154d4e9f`; the app's sync tool found the branch already there.

**Measured first, at `v2`.** A throwaway app-target test (never committed; kept in the session group's notes folder, `A15-measurement/`) read every `document_sources` row of a full v69 index, an APFS clone of the "iPhone 17e A8 timing" simulator's library (`89404205`, 553 volumes, 318,104 documents, 264,590 source notes; the device was not booted), and drove the real `TripPacketBuilder` and `TripPacketExporter`: each note's key, and the target rows of every National Archives note carrying a lot, alone and with every other note of its series key.
- **#1691**: exactly 688 Department-worded central-file notes keyed `r|` and their text though the index stores a class for them (39 volumes, 200 classes, 670 distinct texts); every one of the 186,382 class keys equalled the stored class.
- **#1692**: 807 notes are a National Archives collection carrying a lot. Each alone, 630 printed a records line and an access line and 177 neither, the 99 citing 17 divided lots (#1589's count) among them. 21 series keys carry more than one lot (323 documents), and built over all their documents they took the first document's lot: `ARA Files` read "ARA Files, Lot 70 D 150, RG 59, National Archives" with 70 D 150's series over documents citing four other lots, `Bureau of Intelligence and Research` printed one lot's *Restricted - Fully* over six, and the key with no series, 609 documents of seventeen record groups, read "RG 111, National Archives". 9 notes printed an RG 59 lot's series for a note led by another record group (RG 306, 330, 218, 84, 383), the cards #1589 had Source Explorer refuse.

**#1692** (`d00c0988`).
- **The key does not move.** The builder keeps every record of a group (`TripPacketBuilder.sharedRecord(of:)`, `citedLots(in:)`). A collection target's label names what every one of its documents shares: the repository and series its key names, and the lot and record group only where every document names the same one, lots compared as the bundled lookups fold them (`LotResolutionAcceptance.foldControlNumber`, so `83D066` and `83D66` are one).
- **A National Archives target's lots.** Where every document cites one lot, it is the target's own: passed as printed, its series resolved, and its claimant line read. `TripPacketModel.restriction` now reads the line for any target or lot that carries a lot as printed, where it read a lot file's target alone. Where the documents do not all cite one lot, the target has no series or access line of its own, and `Target.lots` states each lot with its document count, its records line and its access line, in the target row (`TripPacketExporter.lotLines(_:)`), the editor (`archiveVisit.target.lot %@ %@`, its header), the inquiry's records of interest, its divided-lot questions ("claiming Lot 80D212 (Executive Secretariat, …)"), the coverage report's counts, the plan-level triage and the citation crib's example.
- **The record-group rule is Source Explorer's** (#1589): a lot cited through the National Archives is answered only under the record group its notes name (`TripPacketModel.lotFact(heldUnder:answers:)`), both for its one series and for its claimants; a lot file's notes name none and are answered as before.

**#1691's second line** (`eba82221`).
- **The key**: where the citation scan reads no class, `TripPacketBuilder.targetKey` takes `CollectionKeying.centralFilesClass(parsed:note:)`, the one definition `document_sources.decimal_class` is stored from (`IndexingPipeline.decimalClassColumn` returns it); the scan is that definition's own first step for these notes, so no key the scan gave moves. App code only; the kit is unchanged.
- **The join is general** (`ArchiveVisitTargetKeys`). A stored `r|` key names one source note or footnote citation by its text, and `textKeys(of:)` maps each such text to the targets holding it now, so a row on a note's old key answers for wherever the note sits: read exactly first, then with spaces removed (for a row minted before v59). It covers the 688, the 410 rows index v69 orphaned and the 7 of v59, whose notes gained a class the same way, and the notes A18 will store a class for. What it cannot follow is a class whose own spelling changes; the dash rule is still the only class-to-class join. The 108 v59 rows whose bucket key named another bucket, and `frus1964-68v02` d268's, stay orphans.
- **Several rows for one target**, the rule proposed and chosen here: a target that had a row of its own and a note whose row now follows it there, two notes of one file each with a row, or a re-spelled row beside one minted on the new spelling. The target shows the row minted under its own key, when there is one, so a target the reader had set keeps what it showed; otherwise the earliest created, by the order `DuplicateRecordCleanup` keeps one of two copies by (`isKept(_:over:)`, now shared), so every device shows the same row and an edit never moves the choice. The other rows keep their tier, note and exclusion, unapplied (`ArchiveVisitOverlay.superseded`); the editor lists them under Stored targets with a caption naming the target they are now part of (`archiveVisit.superseded.caption %@`), and a line where the row had excluded its own target (`archiveVisit.superseded.excluded`); each is written there by its own key; and the coverage report counts them as kept and labeled. Until A15 such rows were orphans, or, for two re-spelled keys, both were.
- **No CloudKit change**: no stored property, no key rewritten. The derivation's input signature carries each row's `createdAt` and id, which the choice reads.

**Measured after.** The same harness over the same index:

**What was asked.** Plan of record lane A17 for build 51 (decision 59, and §0's default for #1693), started by the session running the build-51 queue once A16 had merged as #1743. #1693's three lines in one pull request, each part its own commit: `CrossRefKit`'s mirror gains the whole-volume and footnote cases, branch for branch with the app, its doc comments and table corrected; `resolved-edge-index.json` regenerated with the footnote references and sections' own references, the render path for a citer that is a section traced first, and any other artifact the grammar moves regenerated, each from a control that reproduces the shipped file first; and the volume graph's volumes outside the catalogue looked at in the app before anything there changes. Based on `v2` at `b8be1631`, brought there with the app's sync tool.

**Controls first.** At the base, the three consumers of the twin built in release and run with each shipped file's own stamp (`GENERATED_DATE` 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11), corpus `6170e4b32` (its `volumes/` unchanged since `99d851c79`, `git log 99d851c79..HEAD -- volumes` empty): `resolved-edge-index.json`, `provenance-flow-index.json`, `broken-refs-index.json` and the report's JSON and CSV all reproduced byte for byte. `RefClassification` is CrossRefKit's own and reads no navigation; the validator calls only it.

## Session 2026-10-20 — cross-volume page references assessed as citations, amended for build 51's index bump, and decided: A18b (plan of record decision 80)

**What was asked.** Started by the top session after A17 (#1693), and based on `v2` at `b8be1631`. It was a read-only assessment for the owner, with no pull request: should a printed-page reference into another volume count as a citation of the document on that page? The places it would count are the reader's citing lists, the cross-reference graph, Cross-Reference Analytics and the bundled `resolved-edge-index.json`. The brief asked for:
- the population, by citing volume, target volume and citer;
- how many resolve to one document, several or none under `PageSpanResolver`'s own rule;
- the options with their costs, the surfaces each changes and what an index version costs;
- a recommendation for a build after 51.

In this session the owner then asked for two more things: to amend the memo for build 51's index bump (A18) and weigh pairing it with a generated bundled resource, and to record the result.

**What was found.** `Planning/Cross-Volume-Page-Citations-Assessment-2026-10-20.md` has the figures. The headlines:
- **The population.** 44,022 live cross-volume `pg_N` rows: 43,040 from documents, 380 from a division's own text and 602 from prose sections. 96.6% come from volumes covering 1960 and earlier, where 79.6% of the 8,700 cross-volume document citations come from 1961 on.
- **The resolver.** One document for 77.0% of the rows, several for 21.7% and none for 1.3%.
- **What a page reference cites.** A single page cites a document: 27,294 rows. "ff." mostly cites a compilation: 8,704 rows. A printed range is two rows, one per end, and only 971 of the 4,012 ranges lie within one document.
- **Rule C** counts single pages, and ranges whose two end pages name the same one document. It resolves 29,023 rows and adds 26,395 citing pairs; documents cited from another volume go from 5,803 to 20,032. The Atlantic Charter goes from 0 citers in other volumes to 156.
- **Build 51.** The change can ride A18's re-index as A18b (v70 → v71), with readers re-indexing once.
  - A bundled page map, prototyped at 16,153 pages and 519,368 bytes, resolves every row with no new column and no second pass.
  - Resolving only against volumes on the device would reach a median 3.5% of a 25-volume library's rows.
  - The map can go stale: 2 of 553 volumes changed their page layout in 18 days.
- **Five side findings.** A18b takes two of them (the 43 self-prefixed same-volume references, and the Agentic Analysis Guide's §6.6 query); the plan's §6g holds the other three.

**How it was measured.** The "iPhone 17e A8 timing" library (`89404205`, index v69) was read through an APFS clone. The kit's `PageSpanResolver.swift` was compiled into a throwaway harness and fed by its own two SQL strings. The device's own 553 volume files were scanned for each reference's printed form, and 44,022 of 44,022 rows were matched. The scripts and their outputs are in the session group's notes folder (`page-citations/`) and are not committed.

**What changed.**
- `Planning/Cross-Volume-Page-Citations-Assessment-2026-10-20.md`: new, amended the same day, its §12 holding the owner's choice.
- `Planning/Plan-Of-Record-2026-10-14.md`:
  - §0: decision 80, A18b's defaults, and the one-bump rule with A18b's v71;
  - §1: A18b's row and entry, A18's and A19's entries, and the order;
  - §2: A19's census and run, after A18b;
  - §4: the answer;
  - §6d: A18b's line;
  - §6g: the three findings A18b does not take.
- This entry.

**Not done.**

Before the record was written, the branch `claude/eager-khorana-ae6598` merged that commit (A17, merged as #1744) through the app's sync tool.
- **No code.** The lane is A18b's.
- **The device.** The "iPhone 17e A8 timing" device was neither booted nor changed; its library was read through an APFS clone in the session's scratchpad.

## Session 2026-10-20 — A18: index version 70 — a heading's footnote and the prose the index left out have rows, a section's row is dated by its documents, a volume's list of sources keys its files, and the class grammar reads names, slips and nine countries (#1640, #1645, #1690, #1638)

**What was asked.** Plan of record lane A18 for build 51 (decisions 59, 60 and 77): `currentDateIndexVersion` 69 → 70 with §6d's items, each measured before and after on a full index, as one pull request, the owner's answers gathered first and the pull request opened only on the owner's word. Started by the session running the build-51 queue once the page-citation assessment had merged as #1745, from `v2` at `b4190f1f`. **Built here, not through `lane-dev.js`**, on the owner's word ("Here, on Fable max"), with one review pass on the diff in its place.

**Asked first**, nine questions over three rounds on 2026-10-20, each answered as recommended: the prose kinds the index leaves out are all promoted and none of the corpus's lists ("All prose, no lists"); a promoted section is a front-matter row where its kind is front matter, as a preface is ("As a preface does"); a section whose only own text is a footnote on its heading has a row of the heading and the note ("A row, as own text"); a section's row with no date of its own takes the span of its documents ("Span of its documents"); the Search row draws that span where it has no dateline ("Draw it"); a volume's list of sources reads both a file with no subject number and one continued after a slash ("Read both"); the 62 Subject-Numeric citations with no class are read through their slips of punctuation and nine country names join the area words ("Slips and countries"); and of decision 77's forms, a person's name after the country is dropped and the short form `POL 2 DOM` completes ("People's names", "The short form"), the capitals names of a case or a meeting staying files of their own.

**Measured before changing anything**, on the XML of the 553 catalogue volumes at corpus `6170e4b32` and on a full v69 index built from them (the scripts are in the session group's notes folder, `A18-measurement/`): 3,516 chapters, subchapters and compilations whose only own text is a heading's footnote (471,486 characters, 5,173 references); the prose kinds reaching no row (the 45 Notes on U.S. Covert Actions, 866,558 characters; `message` 644,638 in 9 volumes; Intel's eight introductions 170,416; eight smaller kinds), against the lists that must stay out (`additional-volumes`, with 838 whole-volume references in 39 volumes, among them); 1,227 of the 1,337 own-text section rows undated, and the span rule dating every one (484 to a day, 78 within a month, 385 within a year, 280 longer), where the corpus's own `frus:doc-dateTime` on the section agrees for 962 and differs for 265 by #1326's shift; 14 content containers whose first subsection opens before their first document; about 670 Sources rows naming a file with no subject number and 259 continued after a slash; the 62 citations, note by note; and decision 77's six keys over 18 documents.

**What changed** (kit, generator and app; one code commit with the bump, then the artifacts, then the docs).
- **`FRUSDocumentParser`** (FRUSCoreKit): `TEIParserDelegate.headingHoldsNote` makes a heading's footnote the division's own text, so such a division has a row whether it holds documents or sections, and a container #1510 left out is left out only when its heading carries no note; `promotableQuasiDocumentKinds` takes `note-on-covert-actions`, `message`, `message1`, `editorial-note`, `editorial-policies`, `acknowledgments`, `report`, `recommendations`, `abstract`, `united-states` and `translation-of-the-memorandum`, each kind's measured count in its comment, and the lists stay out; an `editorial-note` section is stored under the `.editorialNote` wrapper and is front matter where it is printed in `<front>` or `<back>`, not by kind; `VolumeStructureParserDelegate` records `VolumeSection.leadsWithSubsections` (a transparent wrapper keeps its order where it can); `SourcesParserDelegate.classLeafKey` keys through `SourceNoteParser.frontMatterClassKey` and, for the row's leading designation alone, `frontMatterPrimarySubjectKey(leading:)`.
- **`VolumeStructure`**: `leadsWithSubsections`, decoded as `false` from an outline stored before 70 (`init(from:)` in an extension, so the memberwise initialiser stays); `frontMatterKinds` and `proseReadableKinds` take the new kinds, so Browse opens them.
- **`IndexingPipeline`**: version 70 with its history entry; `datingSectionRows` dates an undated section row by the span of the dated documents under it at any depth (`date_iso`, `date_iso_max`, the coarser precision, `range`, or `exact` for one day), after the document loop; `mergeReadingSequence` walks a section's subsections before its documents where the flag says so; `IndexedSearchRow` carries `dateISOMax` and `datePrecision` from the four SELECTs.
- **`SearchParameters` / `SearchService`**: `SearchResult.dateISOMax`, `datePrecision` and `drawnDate`, and `SearchResultDate.text(dateISO:dateISOMax:precision:locale:)`, Foundation only, for the words of a day or span at its precision ("August 21, 1945 – January 22, 1946", "1870 – 1871", "1862").
- **`SourceNoteParser`** (SourceNoteKit): `subjectNumericAreaWords` 155 → 164 (`ARABIA`, `BANGLADESH`, `BURUNDI`, `ITALY`, `KUWAIT`, `NIGERIA`, `SAUDI`, `SWITZ`, `UGANDA`); `SubjectNumericDesignation` drops a title-case name after a capitals country and a subject number (`POL 7 US Connally`, `PS 7-1 US- USSR Barghoorn`), reads a country in parentheses as the element (`DEF 12-5 (GER W)`) and drops a name there (`POL 7 US (LODGE)`), refuses a parenthesis right after the number (`DEF 18-3 (ENDC)`), refuses a digit token in a no-number designation (`POL Nigeria 03`, `POL US – USSR 5/1/69`) except a space-joined commodity (`INCO FIBERS 17 US-JAPAN`), and reads through an unbalanced closing parenthesis; `completingShortForm` makes `DOM` `DOM REP`; `joiningLeadSlash` reads `POL /27 ARAB–ISR`; `droppingClosingSlips` reads `.]`, a stray comma and the `)` of a parenthetical copy citation (`(Ibid., RG 59, Central Files 1970–73, POL 38–6)`), on the strict path without the parenthesis, so that `p. D15)` is no class; `frontMatterClassKey` and `frontMatterPrimarySubjectKey(leading:)` for the list of sources. `CollectionAuthorityGeneratorCore.FrontMatterSourcesExtractor.classLeafKey`, the twin, makes the same two calls.
- **The app**: `SearchView`, `SearchSheet` (the Mac) and `SearchResultAccessibility` draw `result.dateline ?? result.drawnDate`; `SemanticSearchBackend` passes the two columns.

**Measured after**, two full indexes of the 553 volumes (the base at `b4190f1f` and the branch, 318,151 → 321,749 rows), compared table by table without autoincrement ids (`diff-before-after-3.txt`, `moves-3.txt`, `visit-keys-3.txt` in the notes folder):

## Session 2026-10-21 — A18b: index version 71 — a printed page of another volume counts as a citation of the document on it, through a bundled page map and the regenerated resolved-edge index (plan of record decision 80)

**What was asked.** Plan of record lane A18b for build 51 (decision 80; `Planning/Cross-Volume-Page-Citations-Assessment-2026-10-20.md` §7, with §0's defaults): `currentDateIndexVersion` 70 → 71, rule C — a single page of another volume, and a range whose two end pages name the same one document, cite the document on the page; "ff." and a range across documents stay references to the volume — resolved when a volume is stored through a bundled page map, with the 43 self-prefixed same-volume references resolved as same-volume references, and the same generator run writing the map and adding rule C's pairs to `resolved-edge-index.json`; each measurement before and after on a full index; one pull request, opened only on the owner's word. Started by the session running the build-51 queue once A18 had merged as #1746, from `v2` at `75bf6eb5` (the app's sync tool found the branch already there). **Built here, not through `lane-dev.js`**, on the owner's word ("Here, on Fable max"), given what the workflow would run and cost (about 12–20 agents, roughly 100–250 million tokens and 6–10 hours, at the workflow's default model), with one review pass on the diff in its place.

**Measured before changing anything**, on a full v70 index of the 553 catalogue volumes at corpus `6170e4b32` (371 s through the kit's pipeline) and on their TEI, by replaying the assessment's scripts (the session group's notes folder, `A18b-measurement/before/`): 48,577 live references to a page of another volume (43,040 from documents, 4,931 from a division's own text — A18's heading rows among them — and 606 from prose sections; 27 more that the index marks broken or that point outside the catalogue), every one matched to its printed form in the TEI: 27,663 single pages, 10,634 "ff.", and 5,140 ranges as two rows each; the resolver answers one document for 37,022, several for 10,947 and none for 608; rule C resolves 29,390 and adds 26,747 citing pairs to a document and 126 to a section, taking the documents cited from another volume from 5,818 to 20,245 (the assessment's v69 figures were 29,023 and 26,395 to 20,032); 981 of the 5,140 ranges lie within one document and the two-end test decides 977 of them; 46 self-prefixed same-volume rows (43 at v69), all resolving; the map's prototype 16,363 pages in 380 volumes, 528,580 bytes. And where a form's deciding text sits in the TEI, over all 173,933 cross-volume page `<ref>`s: every range's dash and second page (36,044) and "ff." (10,641, 23 inside the reference) are siblings of the reference but one — `frus1955-57v14`'s "ff." printed after the note that holds it closes — so a sibling walk classifies the form.

**What changed** (kit, generator and app; the bump in the code commit).
- **`PageSpanResolver`** (FRUSCoreKit): `PageReferenceForm` — single, "ff." (`andFollowing`), a range's start with its end, a range's end with its start — and `form(ofPageReferenceAt:in:)`, which reads a reference's siblings: the next or previous `<ref>` a page of the same volume with one dash between (en, em, minus or hyphen), "ff" in the reference's own text or beginning the text after it; `citedDocument(inVolume:page:form:citing:map:)`, rule C over the map, the one function the device's store pass and the generator call; `citedDocument(among:facts:citing:)` over ids, which the claimants overload forwards to.
- **`CitedPageMap`** (new, FRUSCoreKit): the bundled map's type — `volumes`, a per-volume `documents` vocabulary, `pages` rows of `[page, claim, index…]` and `facts` rows of `[index, printedNumber, day]` — decoded into lookups (`entry(volumeId:page:)`, `facts(volumeId:documentIds:)`), refusing a malformed row (`CitedPageMapError`); `Codable`, so the generator writes it through the same type.
- **`IndexingPipeline`**: version 71 with its history entry; `collectDocumentRefs` classifies a page of another volume (`CrossReferenceRow.pageForm`), carried by `auxInsertCrossReferences` to `resolveCrossVolumePageReferences`, which runs in the store pass's transaction after the same-volume pass and before the settled targets, skips rows the broken-reference pass marked, and leaves everything on the volume when the host passes no map; the same-volume pass takes `target_volume_id = source_volume_id` beside `NULL`. `IndexingResources.citedPages`, `cited-page-map` among `indexResourceNames`, loaded by `loading(fromDirectory:)`; `PageRangeStore.citedDocumentFacts(inVolume:)` public.
- **`ResolvedEdgeIndexGenerator`**: `build(files:generated:index:)` returns the edge index and the map. Pass 3's parse keeps every row with each reference's form and hint (`parsedRows(in:)`, `references(in:volumeId:noteChildren:)`, the index walk's shape, an editorial note's text given no hint as the index gives none); pass 4 builds a full index of the run's volumes through the kit's pipeline (`buildIndex(of:in:)`, `resources: .none`, 194 s in release, the files cloned into the index folder), reads each cited page's documents and facts through `PageRangeStore`, writes the map (`pageMap(for:in:files:generated:)`: single pages that name anything, both ends of a range whose ends name the same one document, facts for the documents on a page naming several) and resolves every page reference over it. `INDEX_DIR` keeps the index, `INDEX_DB` reads one already built; the funnel gains `crossVolumePageReferences` and `pageEdges`, which `storedEdges` adds; the package target links FTS5Store.
- **The app**: `CitedPageMapStore` beside `BrokenRefsIndexStore`, `IndexingResources.bundled`'s provider, the `BundledArtifactProvenance` row (Tier 1, the edge index's inputs), the app's `ResolvedEdgeIndex.Coverage` reading the two fields, `xcodegen generate` and the scheme restore for the two new source files and the new resource.

**The bundled files**, from one run at corpus `6170e4b32` (`Planning/Generators-Runbook.md` has the entry), after a control run of the unchanged generator at the shipped stamp reproduced the shipped `resolved-edge-index.json` byte for byte: `cited-page-map.json` (new): 16,364 pages in 380 volumes naming 18,832 documents (13,124 pages where a document begins, 3,240 printed inside one, none in a volume numbering its pages per document), 3,938 naming several, 8,543 documents' facts, 536,162 bytes, `indexVersion` 71; `resolved-edge-index.json`: 48,604 references to a page of another volume in the rows the parser emits, 29,391 resolving; 9,209 → 38,600 stored edges into 5,818 → 20,273 documents (33 of them sections printed on a cited page, by §0's default) from 186 → 513 citing volumes, 9,027 → 35,901 citing pairs (129 to a section, 33,235 through a note), 295,999 → 1,112,590 bytes; the document and section funnels unchanged. A second run after the last code change, over the kept index, reproduced both files byte for byte.

**Measured after**, on a full v71 index built with the map (346 s), aligned with the v70 index row for row (`A18b-measurement/after/`): 29,391 of the 48,577 rows resolve — 21,076 single pages naming one document, 6,361 naming several (2,142 by the note's day, 3 by a number, 4,216 the first) and both ends of 977 ranges within one document — and 19,186 stay (10,633 "ff.", 8,326 ends of ranges across documents, 227 single pages naming nothing); the 27 broken rows keep their page; the 46 self-prefixed rows all resolve. The kit's forms agree with the assessment's raw-XML classification on every reference but the one expected (`frus1955-57v14`'s); the replay's 29,390 and 2,135 by the day differ by that one and by seven hints it built from a `context` cut at 500 characters where the index reads the whole note. **The bundled file equals the index**: every one of its 35,901 pairs is a cross-volume row the index stores against a document or section; the index holds 6 pairs more, all references by id to a section's row (`frus1948v02`'s `ch1` from five documents of `frus1949v03`, an appendix of `frus1917-72PubDipv06`), which the edge index's document pass has never kept (plan §6g). Analytics' documents with any in-degree 68,080 → 77,701 (the Potsdam protocol 103 → 219, the communiqué 46 → 206, the Moscow protocol 33 → 171, the Atlantic Charter 6 → 162); the Agentic Analysis Guide's §6.6 query holds 3 page anchors in its top 25 where it held 20; the Atlantic Charter has 156 citers in the bundled file where it had none, the Potsdam communiqué 122 where it had 29.

**Found, for the owner** (not fixed and not filed).
- A number typed with a mark, such as `1945.`, still searches nothing, and nothing says so. The parser decides which words run on the word as typed, and a digits-only word with a mark is dropped. Parser 6.8 keeps that, so results do not move.
- An `=` word never anchors a snippet. Its match is the literal word, which a stem cannot say, so its row opens where its other words do, or on its prose unmarked.
- The scan reads a hyphenated word whole. *long-range* does not anchor *long*, though the index reads it as *long* and *range*, so such a row anchors on its next tier. This predates the lane: A10b's scan was the same.
- A phrase can match across a document's heading and its form marker, since `body_text` begins with both. *"long telegram"* lists 136 documents on S1's index, and 13 of them match only because a heading ending *…to Minister Long* is followed by *[Telegram]* (`frus1916` d1256 is the first row). None of those 13 has *long telegram* in its text as written. Neither do three more of the 136. Their snippets open on the prose unmarked, or mark the other word.

## Session 2026-10-22 — The keyword scan reads ASCII from a table: 90% of what #1760 added to a question's snippet pass won back, the 33 searches' pass below A10b's in all, and not one snippet moved (plan of record §5, found in L2)

**What was asked.** Started by the coordinating session once L2 had merged (#1770, `38dc3d7c`). Make the keyword snippet scan faster without changing a single snippet. Try an ASCII fast path in `Gates.admit` and the word loop first, and a scan over `body.utf8` only if that was not enough.
- **Proof.** Every snippet byte-identical over the 33 searches L2 measured. `SearchSnippetCostTests` and `KeywordSnippetTests` unchanged and green.
- **Cost.** The release cost re-timed before and after, as L2's entry timed it.
- **Kit code.** `swift build --target FRUSCoreKit`, `swift test` and the unit target scoped to the snippet suites, and a *For the web edition* line.
- **Records.** The branch committed; the pull request only on the owner's word.

**Done.** On `claude/reverent-wiles-972304`, cut from `v2` at `38dc3d7c`. Kit code in FRUSCoreKit, and a new kit suite. No index version, no CloudKit change, no copy, and no snippet moved.
- **Where the time went.** `sample` over a release build looping *What was the Long Telegram?* at the Mac's 7,500 rows, 2.86 s a pass:
  - the word scan was 67% of the snippet pass;
  - `Character.isLetter` was 85% of the scan. It reads its first scalar's Unicode property through `_swift_stdlib_getBinaryProperties`, a search of the runtime's tables that no build inlines, and the scan asked it of every character, twice of most;
  - the rest: the window's string 12.5%, `Array(body)` 11% (it walks the graphemes twice, once to count them), `ProseSnippet.proseStart` 5%.
- **The word loop** (`WordCharacter`). One ASCII character, as nearly every character of a FRUS body is, is read from a 128-entry table. Any other character is read as `Character` read it (`init(asking:)`).
  - The table is built by asking `Character` the scan's own question of each ASCII character, so the two cannot disagree.
  - A character counts as ASCII only when its UTF-8 is one byte. An *e* with a combining accent, an apostrophe with a mark, the Kelvin sign and CR LF go the old way.
- **The first gate** reads a word that opens with one ASCII character from a table of the stems' first letters, by that character lowercased as `lowercased()` would. A stem's first letter of several bytes is compared with every ASCII character, since one can equal it (the Kelvin sign is K).
- **The second gate** compares bytes. The stems' openings are kept as each character's `asciiValue`, as the gate compared them.
- **The UTF-8 scan was not built.** Profiled on the branch, the slowest question left, *How did the Vietnam war end?* at 1,000 rows (0.37 s a pass), spends 37.5% of its pass in the scan.
  - 86% of that scan is the Porter stemmer: the stems *war* and *end* leave the second gate a one-letter opening, so every word that opens with *w* or *e* is stemmed until a rarer tier is found.
  - The scan's own reading of characters, all a UTF-8 scan could save, is about 3% of the pass. The window and the strip would still need `[Character]`.
- **What is left, for every keyword search.** `Array(body)` is 31% of that pass, the window's string 16%, `proseStart` 9% and deallocation 7%. On *What was the Long Telegram?* at 7,500 rows they are 28%, 33%, 13% and 6%. None of them is the scan, and none was touched.
- **Tests.** `KeywordScanCharacterTests` is new: three tests, run by Xcode and by `swift test`. Each pins what v2's scan made of a character the table could misread:
  - an apostrophe or a hyphen with a combining mark ends a word, where a bare one goes on with it;
  - an ASCII letter with a combining mark is one letter of its word;
  - a word that opens with a letter outside ASCII is gated on that letter lowercased (the Kelvin sign is k).
  - No test that reaches the scan held a combining mark before it: `SearchSnippetCostTests`' and `KeywordSnippetTests`' bodies are one scalar a character.
  - `xcodegen generate`, then the schemes restored. The project diff is the new file's four lines.

**Measured.** Over L2's index clone (S1's iPad, index version 71), APFS-cloned into this session's scratchpad. Release builds through throwaway executable targets in scratch copies, never in the worktree: A10b at `b385340c` with L2's own harness, `v2` at `38dc3d7c`, and the branch. Each was timed alone under the lock, as the median of five passes after a warm-up, on the M5 MacBook Air. The same-session A10b reproduced L2's within 2%.

**Done.** On `claude/l3-analytics-counts-3b801c`, cut from `v2` at `3aa63d6a` (L1, L2 and the snippet speed-up merged; the fast-forward the brief asked for first was a no-op). Not kit code: nothing under `FRUSCoreKit/` or a package target changed, so `swift test` was not owed and nothing the web edition compiles moved. No index version, no CloudKit change.
- **#1756, 1: the link counts the search it opens** (`b1ed286a`).
  - **The two rules.** The link printed the chart's own sum, `matchedDocumentCount`: each document at the year its `date_iso` begins, and an undated one at its volume's first year (`CorpusAnalyticsService.termFrequencyByYear`). The search it opened read the years as Search reads a `DateRange`: a document whose `[date_iso, date_iso_max]` overlaps them, and nothing undated. Over S1's full index, *Berlin* over 1953–1961: 2,775 documents begin in those years and 28 undated ones sit in volumes beginning then, 2,803 on the link; Search took the 2,775 and the 58 that begin before 1953 and run into it (5 in 1945, 1 in 1948, 7 in 1951, 45 in 1952), 2,833. S1's "no rule tried gives 2,803" was the volume-start fallback.
  - **The fix.** `AnalyticsSearchHandoff` builds the one search the link opens and counts it through `SearchService.matchKeys(parameters:)`, the whole match Search's count counts. The view takes the count in a `task(id:)` keyed on the search and the chart's run, prints it through `currentHandoffMatch`, which never shows a count taken for other parameters, and reads *View documents* until it is taken. The years go to Search only when the reader narrowed them: at the default range the old hand-off dropped every undated match, so *Berlin* across the corpus opened on 16,126 documents of its 16,273. No count is taken for a term the chart refuses, an `=` word, whose link stays hidden over the empty state as before: Search's exact-word filter re-reads every matched document's text, about a minute for `=government`.
  - **The spread line** decomposes the link's count, from the same keys. It had read the volume breakdown, which ignores the years, so it said "502 of 553" for every range; for *Berlin* over 1953–1961 it reads 99 of 553, top 3 hold 34%. It is one text now: at a phone's width its three texts side by side had wrapped the volume count into a narrow column beside the concentration, which a narrowed range shows far more often than the whole corpus did.
  - The link's tooltip says how Search's count can part from the chart's (`analytics.handoff.help.v3`).
- **#1756, 2: the Administrations drill** (`651ae34e`). `AdministrationAxis.drillOrder(_:)` orders a drill by `documents(of:)`, the figure each row prints, point and range together, most first, ties by the artifact's own rule (point documents, then the volume id); the artifact and its generator are unchanged, and the R-1 list never re-sorts. The caption says *most documents first* (`browser.administrations.drill.caption.v2 %@ %@ %@`), its volume count through `CountCopy` (George H. W. Bush's drill read *1 volumes*); the count scan's baseline drops the old key, 273 → 272.
- **#1756, 3: Chart Colors** (`67849d9e`). The fold stays as it is in both charts (`ChartSeriesPalette`: with more volumes than the count, one fewer volume and a gray *Other volumes*), so the words now count colors: Settings ▸ Display reads *Colors per chart: 8* with a footer naming the gray *Other volumes*, and Chronology's and Corpus Analytics' own Chart colors menus, which said *Colored volumes*, say *Colors per chart* with help to match. No case for changing the fold came up.

Make the flag record a Guide that was shown, or present the Guide once the screen in front is gone; check it with a first queue started from Volumes & Storage.

- **#1757, 1: the total counts the whole queue** (`c0854850`).
  - **What it did.** The total was `downloadQueue.count + 1` when the first volume began indexing, raised afterwards only from the backlog (`unindexedDownloadedVolumeIds()`), which lists a volume only once it has landed and has no index rows. A subseries still being queued read short, and the volume that opened the queue, still listed as downloading when its first update arrived, was counted twice.
  - **What it does.** The queue counts every volume it holds by id, once each (`IndexingBatch.count`): what waits to download or is under way (`AppState.downloadQueue`'s `didSet`), what has landed and waits for its pass (`landedVolumeIdsAwaitingIndex`, from the download manager's `onTransferFinished`, through `indexingQueueTransferDidFinish`: four transfers run at once, and six volumes of a 27-volume download were indexing before the first finished), what waits on disk (the backlog, now counted by id too), and the volume whose progress opened it. A download cancelled or failed for good leaves the count (`IndexingBatch.uncount`), unless its volume already finished in the queue. The Live Activity takes a new count at once (`refreshIndexingLiveActivityQueue`, from the last update it showed), where it had waited for the next volume's first update. The Mac's status bar reads the same total.
- **#1757, 2: the Guide hangs on the tab shell** (`517c1cef`).
  - **What it did.** Each banner hung the Guide's sheet on itself, and each of the five tabs drew its own banner. Measured with build 1861's code (below), the launch's first 27-volume queue opened the Guide 1.3 s after its banner first showed, and the Guide closed by itself as the queue ended (2.3 to 2.8 s after its last volume finished), with nothing touched: the queue's end gives the banner's place to the summary card, and the sheet went with the banner. The flag was spent as the banner asked, so no later queue in that launch could open it.
  - **What it does.** `IndexingGuideSheetModifier`, applied once by `MainTabView`, presents the Guide, so it stays until the reader closes it. It counts down 0.6 s once a queue of two or more volumes is in flight, the Guide unseen and the keyboard down, then asks `AppState.claimIndexingGuide(for:keyboardIsVisible:)`, which gives the request to one window of several on iPad; the flag is set in the sheet's `onAppear` (`indexingGuideDidAppear`), whichever way it was opened; a queue that ends before the Guide could appear withdraws the request and releases the claim (`releaseIndexingGuideClaim`), so the next queue asks again. Both banners' **Learn about FRUS while you wait →** set the shell's binding.
  - **What S3 saw.** S3's run 1 frame showed *Volume 4 of 6* with no Guide. Both first queues measured here showed the Guide and then lost it at the queue's end; a launch whose Search tab had been visited first (a hidden tab's banner could have claimed the flag) showed it too. What removed it in S3's run is not established; the teardown and the flag spent at the request are both gone.

## Session 2026-10-22 — L5: first launch — the splash from the first frame, a hand-off with no empty backdrop, and a word field in which no two words meet — #1759's three items, and the tags corrected (decision 99), in one branch (plan of record from 2026-10-21, §1)

**What was asked.** Lane L5 of the plan of record from 2026-10-21, started by the coordinating session on the owner's "start l5". Fix #1759 in one pull request, with a commit for each item, one for a plan-of-record correction, then a docs commit, and one review pass over the whole diff.
- **Item 1.** On the first launch after install the Welcome dock showed before the splash: under the fading launch screen on an iPad (5.44 to 5.69 s into S2's first launch), and in the Mac window's first two frames (S4). Make sure a new reader never sees the dock before the splash.
- **Item 2.** The splash emptied before onboarding's cloud arrived (0.46 and 0.79 s on S2's iPad, 0.18 s on S4's Mac), and the cloud then appeared in one frame. Make the splash flow into onboarding's cloud, as `LaunchSplashView`'s doc says it does: no empty backdrop, and the cloud fading in.
- **Item 3.** Two pairs of words overlapped in the Concepts layout `onboarding-volumes` shows: *objective* under *power*, and two vertical words at the left edge. Fix that seeded layout, and check that other seeded layouts do not regress.
- **The correction.** The owner's words of 2026-10-22: "include a plan of record correction: we will tag the 1.0/1776 test flight release as "build 51" in github, not 1.0/1861. 1.0/1861 will be tagged as "version 1.0"".
- **Limits.** No index version, no CloudKit change, neither TestFlight note, no screenshots (the captures each fix changes listed for R1), the pull request only on the owner's word.

**Done.** On `claude/l5-first-launch-6d9a69`, cut from `v2` at `311e94c8` (L1 to L4 merged; the fast-forward the brief asked for first was a no-op). Not kit code: the word-cloud packer and drift field are app code (`FRUSExplorer/Analytics/WordCloud/`), nothing under `FRUSCoreKit/`, `WordCloudKit/` or a package target changed, so `swift test` was not owed and nothing the web edition compiles moved. No index version, no CloudKit change, no string key.
- **#1759, 1: the splash from the first frame** (`6248de04`).
  - **What it did.** `ContentViewWithSplash` drew the splash only once `resolveSplash()` had run, from a `.task` after the first frame, so the onboarding dock beneath it was the first thing drawn, then covered.
  - **What it does.** `CloudSurfaceArbiter.firstFrameSplash` answers for the frames before the resolve: a fresh install's splash, and no other. A fresh install is final at frame zero, since `AppState` reads `hasCompletedOnboarding` from `UserDefaults` as it is created and the queue and the batch that would give the screen to the indexing backdrop are empty at launch; a CloudKit import's splash still waits for the resolve, the sync state arriving later. `ContentViewWithSplash.shownReason` draws it until the resolve latches the same answer, in the same pass.
- **#1759, 2: the splash flows into onboarding's cloud** (`252ff378`).
  - **What it did.** Onboarding's `WordCloudBackdropView` was mounted in a fresh install's first frame, before the vectors, and nothing told it they had landed: `BundledCloudVectors` is static state Observation cannot see, and only the splash read `AppState.areCloudVectorsReady`. Its body ran again only at its own next lens change, on the 4.2 s wall-clock grid, so its cloud popped in at a lens boundary, mid-crossfade, and the empty backdrop lasted from the splash's exit to that boundary — or did not show at all, when the boundary fell before the exit (the first launch measured below).
  - **What it does.** The backdrop reads the mirror itself (`vectorsArrived`, through an optional `@Environment(AppState.self)`, so a host without one still renders) and fades its cloud in when it turns: the fade `LaunchSplashView` used to give its own backdrop alone. Onboarding's cloud therefore arrives under the splash, and onboarding takes the splash's lens seed (`lensSeed: 0`), so the two name one lens when the splash fades out.
- **#1759, 3: no two words meet** (`96cd7175`).
  - **What it did.** The drift field's per-axis expansion, which spreads the packer's clump across a full-bleed canvas, knew nothing of the exclusion zones or the edge, and the packer's flattened field (`yCompression` 0.62) is spread furthest vertically: ×2.05 and ×3.33 on the 13-inch iPad's Add Volumes step. It carried *objective* into the dock's zone and *hostility* 67 pt off the left edge; each frame, `push` lifted *objective* back over the zone's top and `clamp` pulled *hostility* back to the edge, and neither looked at the other words. A scratch harness, compiling the app's own `WordCloudLayout.swift` and `WordCloudDriftField.swift` against the bundled vectors, reproduced S2's frame at its instant (16:38:34.363 EDT on 2026-10-21): *objective*'s box 1,040 square points into *power*'s and *conflict*'s 587 into *hostility*'s, the only two pairs that met.
  - **What it does.** `WordCloudDriftField.settle`: in rank order each word takes a home whose `Sweep` — every box it can be drawn in, from the drift's exact sine ranges at the largest breath — fits the canvas (the clamp's own test, bleed included), misses every zone, and clears every sweep settled before it. It tries its own ray first (the expanded home, then sixteen steps back to the packed centre), giving up drift a step at a time (`Particle.excursion`: 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0); then the nearest grid point of the canvas where it can stand still, and six 8 pt rings beyond that for more drift; a word with no room anywhere is left out, as the packer leaves one. A band (fill ≤ 1, no bleed: the indexing strip) is left exactly as it was. `push` and `clamp` stay as nets and never move a settled word. `WordCloudBackdropView` caches the settled field beside its layout (`fields`), and `packedWords` and `settledField` spell every argument the view passes, so a test packs a surface as the surface does.
  - **Measured** by the harness over every bundled scope's Concepts and Topics lists (216 layouts a surface) on the splash and onboarding canvases of an iPhone 17, an iPhone SE, an iPhone 17 Pro Max, the 13-inch and 11-inch iPad Pros in both orientations, an iPad mini, and the Mac's 560 × 540 window, each sampled every 2.5 s for five minutes. Before: drawn boxes met in most sampled frames of nearly every layout (on the phones and the Mac in 92–100% of frames; on the iPads in 35–100%), and words were drawn over the dock (up to 62,275 sampled word-frames on one surface). After: no two boxes meet in any frame and none reaches a zone; the iPads keep every word and 89–100% of the drift, weighted by amplitude; the iPhones 99.7–100% of their words and 72–85% of the drift; the Mac's window, the densest, 98–100% of its words and 76–84% of the drift. A field builds in at most about a millisecond on this M5 Mac (a median of 0.02 to 0.32 ms by surface), against 0.06–0.14 ms for the packer.
  - **Two policies were measured and set aside.** Holding drift as a hard rule (every word swept whole, or moved, or dropped) kept 10 of 38 words on the iPhone indexing strip and 32 of 45 on the SE's welcome step, which is why bands are left alone and drift is given up first. Taking simply the nearest standing room kept about half the drift on a phone and on the Mac; an unbounded search for full drift kept 76–90% but took up to 4 ms a field and carried words up to 640 pt. The bounded search sits between: 72–85% kept, words moved a mean of 33–65 pt on the dense surfaces (8–40 pt on the iPads), 1 ms at worst.
- **The correction** (`278d19cd`): decision 99, under a lead-in of its own after the fifteen answers of 2026-10-21; R2 (the owner tags the 1776 commit `build-51` after the upload), R3 (`version-1.0` on the 1861 commit, where it read `build-51`) and §2 (the tags, both named). **Measured, the iPad.** A new iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator under iOS 27.0, "iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) L5" (`AE46CA3C`), made for the lane; turned to landscape on its home screen by S2's rotator (cloned); erased before each build's first launch. ## Session 2026-10-22 — The Mac Corpus Browser opens a handed-off volume's page whatever it shows: the push waits until AppKit shows the new subseries' list (plan of record §5, found in L6)

**What was asked.** Started by the coordinating session while L6 (#1766) waited on the owner. Walking L6 on the Mac found an older fault, recorded unfiled in the plan of record's §5 on L6's branch. A volume hand-off (`AppState.openBrowseVolume`, consumed by `consumePendingVolume()` in `MacCorpusBrowserWindow.swift`) that reached an open Corpus Browser with a volume's page pushed, and had to change the sidebar's subseries, showed the new subseries' list and no page. Every producer goes through it: a link to a whole volume (#1603), the page-link fallback L6 adds, Cross-Volume Provenance rows and subject pivots.
- Find why the path is dropped when the stack's root and its path change together, and fix it so the hand-off opens the volume's page whatever the browser shows.
- Walk it in the check copy for a whole-volume link and a page link across subseries, with a page pushed and with only a list.
- Build `FRUSExplorerMac`, record the cause and the walk here, commit, and ask the owner before a pull request.

**Done.** On `claude/relaxed-hypatia-b0a197`, cut from `v2` at `88b3b7d1`: `8442597f`, Mac code in `MacCorpusBrowserWindow.swift` (a `#if os(macOS)` file) and two EditableContent ranges re-pointed, then this entry, which also corrects one figure in a doc comment (72 hand-offs to 74). No kit code, no index version, no CloudKit change, no copy. The manuals are unchanged: both already say a hand-off opens the volume's page.
- **The cause.** Changing the selection of the sidebar's `List(selection:)` makes SwiftUI's split view pop the detail column's `NavigationStack` to its root itself (`NavigationColumnState.popAllForSelectionChange`). It does so in an update action dispatched after the one in which the browser's own `.onChange(of: selection)` ran. The stack then reads no change of its path until AppKit has put the new selection's root in the window. The browser pushed the volume from that observer, in the same pass as the selection change, so:
  - with a page pushed, SwiftUI read the new path (`NavigationColumnState.setPath`), popped it, and wrote `[]` back through the binding: the new subseries' list, no page, no Back;
  - where the push slipped past the pop, the binding kept the volume while the stack showed the list, and nothing read the binding again.
  - Seen in a copy of the split view (below), from the call stacks of the path binding's reads and writes. On the Mac a `NavigationStack` keeps only its top view in the window: with a page pushed, AppKit puts the root's view back only after the pop, about 400 ms after the selection change in two runs with heavy lists, and a push made before then was never read.
- **The fix: the push waits for AppKit.**
  - `DetailStackRootReporter`, an empty `NSViewRepresentable`, sits in the stack's root with the selection as its identity, so each selection's root has one of its own. It reports each move into or out of the window to `DetailStackRootPresence`, which knows which selection's root is on screen.
  - `consumePendingVolume` keeps the volume in `pendingVolumePush` and changes the selection. The selection observer resets the path as before and asks the presence to push the volume once the new selection's root is in the window: on the next turn of the main queue after it arrives, or on the next turn if it is there already.
  - Within the selected subseries the hand-off still replaces the path at once, unless an earlier hand-off's push is still waiting, in which case that push opens the newer volume. A sidebar row chosen before the push lands cancels it.
  - The observer keeps its `{ _, _ in` signature and reads the selection from the state: `ProjectAdminServiceTests`' #1701 placement test finds the split view's modifiers by that line.
- **The harness** (`corpus-browser-handoff/` in the session notes, not in the repository) is a SwiftUI app compiled with `swiftc`: the browser's split view in miniature, with a `.sidebar` `List(selection:)` of 107 rows, a detail `NavigationStack(path:)` whose root switches on the selection, a `.searchable` volume list, a bar above each view and `navigationDestination` inside the root.
  - A second window hands a volume over through an `@Observable` property and `.onChange`, as a reader and `consumePendingVolume` do.
  - Each run was a new process launched in the background, logging the path binding's writes, the views' appearances and, at the end, the browser window's title. "Heavy" added 400 rows to each list and 300 to a page.
  - Starting states: a page pushed in another subseries, a page and a section, a page pushed from All Volumes, a list only, no selection, and a window the hand-off opens. Controls: a hand-off within the subseries, and a sidebar click.

**Measured** in the harness, on macOS 27.0.1 (the M5 MacBook Air):

| The push | Runs | Page lost |
|---|---:|---:|
| `v2`: from the selection observer, in the same pass | 14 | **14** |
| on the next turn of the main queue | 63 | 5 |
| on the second turn | 17 | 0 |
| 100 ms after the selection change, heavy lists | 21 | 5 |
| from the selection change's transaction completion | 9 | 2 |
| when SwiftUI writes `[]` back (a page pushed) | 3 | 3 |
| when the root's view is back in the window, else on the next turn | 86 | 3 (all from a list) |
| **when the new selection's reporter is in the window (the fix)** | **74** | **0** |

- **Also lost the page every time:** giving the stack a new identity with `.id` (3 runs), putting the sidebar's list in a stack of its own (3), wrapping the detail stack in a `VStack` or `ZStack` (6), setting the path in the same transaction as the selection (1), and setting it from the root's `.task(id:)` (1).
- **Two turns** passed every run, but nothing ties a count of turns to AppKit's swap. A push 100 ms after the selection change still came before it when the new list took 350 ms to draw.
- **With only a list showing**, the root's view never leaves the window, so a push on the next turn has nothing to wait on. It lost the page in 3 of 40 runs, where the new list took longer than the push to arrive (45 ms against 32 ms in two runs). A reporter re-created for each selection arrives with the new list, which is why the fix keys it to the selection.
- **The controls**: a hand-off within the subseries opened the page in every run, before and after, and a sidebar click returned to the list.
